title: Tony Pollard has decent outing
description: Titans RB Tony Pollard receives most of carries again in Week 5 and leads team in rushing
fullText:
Tennessee Titans RB Tony Pollard rushed for 52 yards on 14 carries against the Houston Texans in Week 5.

Why It Matters: Pollard continues to receive most of the work in the running game but has been held to 55 yards or less in three of his five games. He should still see a similar workload next week and can be a No. 3 running back or flex option in fantasy leagues.

title: Ben Johnson discusses Bears QB Caleb Williams' potential Week 6 return
description: Bears head coach Ben Johnson sounded off on quarterback Caleb Williams' potential return against the Falcons in Week 6.
fullText:
The Chicago Bears suffered a demoralizing 31-7 loss to the Green Bay Packers, where the team was out-coached and outplayed in the team's worst showing all season. It was their first loss without starting quarterback Caleb Williams, who's missed the last three games with a hamstring injury.

Williams was spotted going through a workout before Sunday's game, and head coach Ben Johnson said earlier in the week that Williams was throwing, running and making progress without any setbacks. On Sunday, NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported that Williams is making a push for a return in Week 6 against the Atlanta Falcons.

Following Sunday's game -- where Chicago started Tyson Bagent, benched him and then turned to Case Keenum -- Johnson was asked about Williams' status for next week's game against the Falcons. Johnson didn't give too much away but said that Williams is nearing a return, perhaps next Sunday.

"He's on track," Johnson said. "We'll see where he's at, it may be Atlanta or later….he's close."

The Bears have gone 2-1 since Williams went down with a hamstring injury in a Week 2 loss against the Minnesota Vikings and currently sit at 3-2. If Williams is able to return next week, it would be a huge boost for a Chicago offense that has plenty to clean up after a poor showing against the Packers.

title: Seahawks convert 49ers' turnover into game-tying TD
description: The 49ers scored a touchdown after a gift from Sam Darnold.
fullText:
The 49ers scored a touchdown after a gift from Sam Darnold. The Seahawks scored a touchdown after a gift from Jacob Cowing.

The 49ers' punt returner muffed Michael Dickson's punt and Eric Saubert recovered at the San Francisco 24. Six plays later, the Seahawks tied it up 7-7.

Emanuel Wilson ran it in from the 2.

Darnold is now 4-of-6 for 21 yards and a pick. Renardo Green had the interception on a third-down pass intended for Jaxon Smith-Njigba, giving the 49ers the ball at the Seattle 18. Mike Evans scored on a 2-yard reception from Brock Purdy.

Purdy is 2-of-7 for 15 yards and a touchdown.

title: Sirianni takes blame for late-game decisions in Philly's 19-17 loss to Jaguars in London
description: — The Philadelphia Eagles kicked a go-ahead field goal with 8 seconds left in London.That's how it's going for the Eagles these days.
fullText:
LONDON (AP) — The Philadelphia Eagles kicked a go-ahead field goal with 8 seconds left in London.

That's how it's going for the Eagles these days.

The Jaguars pulled off an improbable 19-17 victory on Cam Little's 57-yard field goal as time expired at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium on Sunday.

The Eagles have lost three in a row and are 2-3 for the first time since 2021.

Jalen Hurts had led a late-game drive to set up Jake Elliott's 48-yard field goal, giving the Eagles a 17-16 lead.

All they had to do was finish off the final 8 seconds. But the ensuing kickoff was kept inbounds and Ameer Abdullah returned it 53 yards, leaving 1 second on the clock.

Enough time for Little to send it through the uprights.

Eagles coach Nick Sirianni didn't sugarcoat it.

"I didn't make the right decision, and it cost us the game," he said. "There's no other way around it. There's nothing really else to say about that. It's just I didn't do my job good enough in that situation."

Sirianni fielded several questions about the fateful kickoff.

"There's really nothing else to say. I didn't make the decision — the right decision in that situation," he said. "They returned it to where they returned it, and then they made a kick. You know, credit to them on that. Again, bad job by me."

In some ways, Sunday's game had seemed a tough task for the Eagles. They only arrived in London on Saturday and were undermanned.

They played without injured leading rusher Saquon Barkley and his backup, Tank Bigsby, who was placed on injured reserve this past week. They were also missing wide receiver DeVonta Smith and had a patchwork offensive line after the retirement of Lane Johnson and the trade of Cam Jurgens.

The Eagles rushed for only 22 yards but Hurts kept them in contention by spreading the ball around to multiple receivers and converting on 6 of 15 third down attempts — a week after going 0 for 12 on third down.

Hurts completed 21 of 40 passes for 220 yards and one touchdown. His 62-yard touchdown pass to Darius Cooper gave Philly a 14-7 lead in the second quarter.

But he also missed open receivers.

"We didn't perform well enough. I didn't perform well enough, and that obviously starts with me," Hurts said. "I'll be thinking about all the different things that ultimately I could have done. I always use them as learning lessons, so I think that's what's great. We've got to learn from it."

Before Elliott's go-ahead field goal, Hurts threw incomplete on first down from the Jacksonville 34, which stopped the clock.

Hurts was asked about the play and said " it's not my place."

"I'm prepared as a quarterback to not worry about those things. I'm honoring the play call, honoring the things that are coming in the game," he said.

"When I'm up at night, yeah, I think ... should have I said something or should I have took a step back and said, wait," he continued. "But ultimately, there's a commitment to that and going out there and executing. So this was one where it did not work in our favor."

title: NFL Week 5 Winners and Losers: Commanders have game-management gaffe for the ages in tie to Giants
description: The Giants were quite pleased at the end to get the tie.
fullText:
The worst division in the NFL got a perfectly fitting end to Sunday's game.

The New York Giants celebrated a tie and they should have, because the Washington Commanders had a game-management fiasco that will be remembered for a long time.

The Commanders were in field goal range near the end of an ugly overtime. They didn't have any timeouts though. Washington took its time to run a final play in the last minute with the clock running. By the time they snapped it and Jayden Daniels was tackled after running around for a while, there were fewer than 10 seconds left and it wasn't enough time to get lined up and even try a field goal before the overtime was over.

The Giants and Commanders tied 27-27. It's the kind of mistake that will not get Washington coach Dan Quinn off the hot seat. It was inexcusable for an NFL team to not get a field-goal attempt off at the end. What happened will be remembered for perhaps the worst clock management errors in recent NFL history.

But it summed up the NFC East this season.

A wild finish to Giants-Commanders game pic.twitter.com/0QvJGVIPbG

The Dallas Cowboys looked horrendous on Thursday night in losing to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and their undrafted rookie quarterback. The Philadelphia Eagles took a brutal walk-off loss in London on Sunday that they might not rebound from, on top of all their injury issues. The Giants are 3-1-1 and they didn't cover themselves in glory on Sunday either.

But it was better than the Commanders.

The unbelievable clock management at the end was the finish of a bad collapse by the Commanders. The Giants came back after the Commanders took a 27-13 lead in the fourth quarter. New York took the game to overtime on a Malik Nabers touchdown catch with 1:43 left in regulation. New York got the ball first in overtime but Dominic Zvada pushed a field-goal wide left. The Commanders punted after their drive stalled and they took a delay of game penalty on fourth-and-5. The Giants drove into field-goal range but Cam Skattebo lost a fumble. It was ugly, even before the final minute.

The Commanders strung together some plays and looked to be in position to kick a field goal but managed to run a play with 55 seconds left, stand around waiting for the next play, snap it again with 12 seconds left and then run out of time before they could spike the ball to get the field-goal team on.

The Giants aren't pretty but everyone else in the NFC East is uglier. New York needed last-second interceptions in or near their own end zone to win home games over the Titans and Commanders the last two weeks. Sunday's comeback to tie was impressive in some ways but they also fumbled away a shot at the win in overtime, as well as missing a field goal in the extra period. But a half-win seemed like a win, after the Commanders were in position for a field-goal try. But thanks to Quinn and a horrible mishap, we'll never find out if that field goal would have been good.

Here are the rest of the winners and losers from Week 5 of the NFL season:

Kyler Murray: When the Minnesota Vikings finally got Murray and Justin Jefferson healthy for a full game, their offense didn't look quite as bad.

Minnesota had its best offensive game of the season in a 23-13 win over the New Orleans Saints, which pushes their record to 5-0. Murray was efficient with 229 passing yards and another 51 rushing. Jefferson, coming off an ankle injury, had a great touchdown catch with three Saints defenders around him in the end zone.

3 on 1? No problem for Justin Jefferson 😌@MINvsNO on FOX/FOX One
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QQsYW9NIhO

Murray was knocked out in the first game of the season due to a concussion. In the first half of his first game back, Jefferson suffered an ankle injury. Sunday was the first time they played a full game together. The offense looked much better. The defense continued its run as perhaps the best in the NFL this season. And the Vikings' lead in the NFC North continues to grow.

Houston Texans defense: It's not hard to shut down the Tennessee Titans offense this season. But the Texans still needed a game like Sunday.

The winless Texans, coming off a defensive let down that led to a Cowboys victory, weren't going to let it be a close game against the Titans. They looked like the defense everyone expected to see before the season started, as they clamped down on the Titans offense for a 26-3 win. Tennessee finished with 187 yards and scored only a field goal.

The Texans are 1-4 and while that isn't a good place to be my any means, it's better than 0-5. Houston needed a win and the defense showed up for it.

Drake Maye: Maybe all the talk of Maye being a below average quarterback was an overreaction.

Maye was never as bad as he looked in some tough games last postseason and to start this season, and now it looks like he's back. Maye carved up the Las Vegas Raiders and the New England Patriots had an easy 45-17 win. Maye had 374 yards and four touchdowns passing with another 25 yards and a touchdown on the ground. The blowout Sunday was the Patriots' second straight win. Last week the Patriots beat the Buffalo Bills with Maye playing well.

Drake Maye is dealing today 🎯@LVvsNE on CBS/Paramount+
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/WE4M8J3E3j

Maye came within one vote of winning NFL MVP last season. Patriots haters were quick to pile on when he started slowly this season. It appears the slump is over.

David Bailey: The New York Jets had a difficult decision with the No. 2 overall pick of the NFL Draft. Many thought they'd take Ohio State linebacker Arvell Reese due to his upside. Instead they took Bailey out of Texas Tech. It's working out pretty well.

Bailey had a massive game as the New York Jets got an ugly 17-12 win over the Cleveland Browns on Sunday. New York won after Cleveland flubbed a punt snap and the Jets recovered in Browns territory, then Braelon Allen scored on a 22-yard touchdown to give the Jets the lead. The defense held on after that.

Bailey had three sacks. The Browns were 3-1 coming in but their offense got shut down by the Jets, who were led by their rookie pass rusher.

THIRD sack of the day for David Bailey@CLEvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+
Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QTqQqo79NN

Bailey was a fantastic pass rusher in college and that has translated to the NFL. He had two sacks in his first four games and then had a true breakout in his fifth game. The Jets have a foundational piece for their defense.

Ben Johnson: Matt LaFleur got a little revenge on Sunday.

The Green Bay Packers coach has been criticized and Johnson is a big reason for it. Johnson came into the head coaching job of the Chicago Bears with bravado, saying he was going to like beating LaFleur twice a year, then had two massive wins over the Packers last season including in a playoff game. When Johnson won games with Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent replacing Caleb Williams the past couple weeks, the hype around Johnson got even stronger.

Johnson was humbled a little bit on Sunday. Jordan Love had a huge game with 367 yards and two touchdowns, a Packers defense that hadn't been playing well shut down Bagent and the Bears offense and Green Bay got its best win of the season as it blew out Chicago 31-7.

Johnson started Bagent over Keenum, even though Keenum was very good in his one start against the Eagles, and maybe there is some second-guessing that can be done there. Or, the lesson is, it's just hard to win on the road with a backup quarterback in the NFL no matter who it is. But Packers fans will be happy to take a victory lap regardless of the circumstances.

Malik Willis: Willis has almost nothing to work with on the Miami Dolphins offense, especially since De'Von Achane is done for the season with a torn ACL. But he also hasn't done anything to let the Dolphins know they can bypass a quarterback in the 2027 NFL Draft.

Willis is probably going to be graded by the Dolphins on a curve due to the situation he's in, but he still needs to play better than he has. With a minute to go in the first half against the Cincinnati Bengals, Willis was 1 of 7 for 22 yards. No matter who you're throwing to, that's not good enough. Willis rallied a bit after that, finishing with 137 passing yards, but he had two interceptions and the Bengals won 31-24.

Willis signed a three-year, $67.5 million contract in the offseason and it was a fine gamble from a Miami team that had no hope coming into the season. The Dolphins can easily get out of the deal after two years. They took a shot, after Willis played well as teh Packers' backup in limited starts, that they could find their franchise quarterback in free agency. It's not working out that way yet.

Chris Ballard: The Indianapolis Colts' roster is flawed on both sides of the ball. A quarterback they drafted fourth overall three years ago, Anthony Richardson Sr., looks like a bust as he backs up Daniel Jones. When the Colts signed receiver Alec Pierce to a four-year, $114 million deal it was shocking, and Pierce has 72 yards this season and is on injured reserve.

Colts coach Shane Steichen gets a lot of attention for his time on the hot seat, but Ballard is there too. The general manager of the Colts has overseen a roster that isn't good enough on offense or defense. The Colts lost 34-22 to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday to fall to 2-3. The defense allowed Jaylen Warren to score on an 80-yard touchdown pass and a 50-yard touchdown run. The offense was OK but Jonathan Taylor and Daniel Jones combined for zero touchdowns. Colts owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon let it be known after last season that everyone was on notice coming into this season. It's not starting well for Steichen or Ballard.

Nick Sirianni: It'll be tough for the Philadelphia Eagles coach to bounce back from this one.

The Philadelphia Eagles seemingly had a massive 17-16 win against the Jacksonville Jaguars on a Jake Elliott field goal with eight seconds left. But, there were eight seconds left. The Eagles kicked off and allowed Ameer Abdullah to return it 53 yards, giving Cam Little a chance for a 57-yard field goal. It was astounding that the Eagles allowed the Jaguars that chance to return the kick, especially considering they allowed a kickoff return for a touchdown on the opening play, though it was negated due to a penalty. The Jaguars lost their long snapper to an injury early in the game and the snap was high, but Little still hit the game-winning field goal. The Jaguars won 19-17.

The final sequence for the @Jaguars to get the win in London was truly WILD. pic.twitter.com/5viJ5yIdIX

For a moment it looked like a great win for the Eagles, who were heavily shorthanded due to injuries and right tackle Lane Johnson's retirement. Jalen Hurts came through with a drive in the final two minutes without much help around him. Elliott's field goal was clutch. But it ended in a massive disappointment, a long flight home and more questions about Sirianni after Philadelphia's 2-3 start.

title: Packers lose DL Javon Hargrave to Achilles injury late in win over Bears
description: Packers DL Javon Hargrave was carted off late in Sunday's win, and early indications are he tore his Achilles tendon.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers suffered another major injury blow to end Sunday's 31-7 win over the Chicago Bears. Veteran defensive lineman Javon Hargrave was carted off the field late in the fourth quarter, and coach Matt LaFleur said the injury "doesn't look good" and the team believes Hargrave suffered a season-ending Achilles tendon injury.

"Early indications look like Achilles," LaFleur said after the game Sunday.

Hargrave went down without contact while pressuring quarterback Case Keenum in the fourth quarter.

LaFleur said the end of the game was "bittersweet" given Hargrave's injury in a game that the Packers led by 24 points.

Hargrave was signed to a two-year deal in free agency. The Packers have Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks, rookie Chris McClellan, Jonathan Ford and Anthony Campbell on the roster at defensive tackle, but Campbell is battling an ankle injury and now Hargrave will likely miss the rest of the season. Warren Brinson is currently on injured reserve with a groin injury.

This would mark the second season-ending Achilles tendon injury in as many weeks for the Packers. Linebacker Edgerrin Cooper tore his Achilles tendon last week in Tampa Bay and will miss the rest of the season.

If Hargrave does have season-ending injury, he will join Cooper, receiver Jayden Reed and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele on season-ending injured reserve.

title: Bailey Stockton earns offensive player of the game in home loss
description: Florida Gators wide receiver Bailey Stockton's solid effort in the program's second straight loss earns him Gators Wire offensive player of the game.
fullText:
The Florida Gators returned home looking to bounce back from their first loss of the season, but instead suffered another setback in a 39-19 loss to the South Carolina Gamecocks.

Florida's offense struggled to consistently find its footing for the second consecutive week. Opposing teams seem to have figured out the Gators' rushing attack, forcing them to lean heavily on the passing game as they tried to keep pace with South Carolina.

There were few positives to take from the loss, but wide receiver Bailey Stockton delivered his best performance of the season. For his efforts, Stockton earns Gators Wire offensive player of the game honors for Week 6.

With Vernell Brown III out for the second straight week, Stockton emerged as Florida's most productive offensive weapon Saturday, hauling in eight receptions for 127 yards and a touchdown. His 127 receiving yards led the Gators and provided much of the explosiveness the offense struggled to generate elsewhere.

The performance also showed Stockton's ability to handle an increased role in Florida's passing attack. He consistently gave quarterback Aaron Philo an option on the perimeter and made the most of his opportunities, averaging nearly 16 yards per reception.

Among Florida offensive players who logged at least 40 snaps against South Carolina, Stockton finished as the third-highest-graded player.

The route runner's emergence becomes more important as opposing defenses continue to focus on slowing Jadan Baugh and Florida's rushing attack. If teams want to challenge the Gators to beat them through the air, players like Stockton will have opportunities to exploit favorable matchups.

Florida has plenty to correct following another disappointing performance, but Stockton's 127-yard outing gives the Gators something positive to build around as they attempt to get their season back on track.

title: Fantasy Football impact for Texans following Marvin Harrison Jr. trade
description: The Houston Texans have made a major move to upgrade their offense, acquiring wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Arizona Cardinals along with a 2027 seventh-round pick in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick.…
fullText:
The Houston Texans have made a major move to upgrade their offense, acquiring wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. from the Arizona Cardinals along with a 2027 seventh-round pick in exchange for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-round pick. The trade reunites Harrison with C.J. Stroud, his former Ohio State quarterback, while giving Houston another major weapon alongside Nico Collins.

From a fantasy football perspective, this is a major change for Harrison and a potentially significant development for several Texans pass catchers.

MORE: Fantasy Football studs & duds for Week 5 of 2026 NFL season

Nov 3, 2025; Arlington, Texas, USA; Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. (18) walks off the field after the game between the Dallas Cowboys and the Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Harrison is arguably the biggest fantasy winner from this trade. His time in Arizona had become increasingly disappointing, with just five receptions for 85 yards and one touchdown through four games this season.

A move to Houston gives Harrison a much-needed change of scenery and puts him in an offense that should have a legitimate role for him. Even more importantly, he is reunited with Stroud, who played with Harrison at Ohio State.

Harrison also no longer has to carry the expectations of being the unquestioned No. 1 receiver. With Collins already established as Houston's top target, Harrison can potentially settle into a complementary role while still receiving enough opportunities to become a strong fantasy option.

Oct 4, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Houston Texans wide receiver Nico Collins (12) warms up prior to a game against the Dallas Cowboys at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images

Nico Collins' fantasy value should not change drastically. He remains the Texans' clear No. 1 target and should continue to command a significant share of the passing game.

However, Stroud's fantasy value is now on the rise. Adding another legitimate big-play receiver gives Houston's quarterback another weapon on the outside and should create more opportunities for explosive plays through the air.

The downside comes for Houston's other pass catchers. Jaylin Noel, Kayshon Boutee, and Dalton Schultz are likely to see their target shares decrease with Harrison now entering the offense. Harrison's arrival gives Stroud another player capable of commanding targets, which could make those players more difficult to trust consistently in fantasy lineups.

Overall, the trade significantly raises Harrison's fantasy ceiling while giving Stroud another weapon and leaving Collins in a strong position as Houston's primary receiving option.

title: Studs and duds from Dolphins 31-24 loss to Bengals in Week 5
description: The Miami Dolphins lost to the Cincinnati Bengals on Sunday at Hard Rock Stadium. Here are some players who deserve some love and some who don't.
fullText:
The Miami Dolphins fell to the Cincinnati Bengals 31-24 on Sunday at Hard Rock Stadium, dropping them to 0-5 to start their season and Jeff Hafley's tenure as head coach.

Miami struggled in all three phases of this game, which has been a consistent problem for them throughout the year. They probably won't win any games if they play that way.

Before we move on to Week 6, let's give out some credit and criticism to those who deserve it.

Gordon has been impressive while filling in for De'Von Achane, who tore his ACL early in the year. On Sunday, he rushed for 88 yards and a touchdown on 4.9 yards per attempt. That's an impressive showing, considering Miami couldn't do much through the air.

Speaking of the problems in the air, Willis completed just 55.6% of his passes for 137 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions. While he ran for 74 yards, he also fumbled the ball away on Miami's final possession.

In an ugly game, it's hard to find much to be happy with, but Washington led the team in receiving, as he caught six of his eight targets for 43 yards. He also had a pretty strong punt return from the team's 2-yard line.

The Dolphins surrendered an 81-yard return on the opening kickoff, had a few penalties in the third phase and missed an extra point on their final touchdown in the fourth quarter. These problems have persisted all year. They need to fix these dumb mistakes.

title: How Bernhard Langer unintentionally taught future pro important lesson
description: Alistair Docherty joined GOLF's Subpar podcast to discuss finally earning his PGA Tour card, his first golf memory and more.
fullText:
Alistair Docherty's first golf memory provided a couple of valuable lessons. The 32-year-old pro, who will be a PGA Tour card-holder for the first time come 2027, joined this week's GOLF Subpar podcast and explained how a trip to Sahalee Country Club played a key role in his life.

Sahalee is a private country club in Sammamish, Wash., just outside of Seattle, and in 2010 it hosted the U.S. Senior Open. (It was also home to the 1998 PGA Championship, won by Vijay Singh.) But in 2010, Docherty attended the U.S. Senior Open with his father, and they found a spot to sit by the 10th tee.

That's when Bernhard Langer came through — and promptly fired his tee shot into one of the many evergreens on the famously tree-lined golf course.

"I looked at my dad and I'm like, 'Wow, pros hit bad shots too,'" Docherty said. But the best players in the world hitting bad shots wasn't the main takeaway, it was what happened next. "I'm like, 'What's going to happen now?' Well, he won that week. So a bad shot doesn't really determine the outcome. … And to be fair, if anyone's been up to Sahalee, it's called Sah-hallway for a reason."

title: WWE’s WrestleMania 43 main event plans are now obvious after Money In The Bank
description: WWE’s Money In The Bank PLE is in the bag and in the main, it was a night that very much delivered and set the wheels in motion to build towards WrestleMania. The 43rd edition of WWE’s flagship show will take place in Saudi Arabia next year as the company goes outside North America for the first time.
fullText:
WWE's Money In The Bank PLE is in the bag and in the main, it was a night that very much delivered and set the wheels in motion to build towards WrestleMania.

The 43rd edition of WWE's flagship show will take place in Saudi Arabia next year as the company goes outside North America for the first time.

Key to the show being a success over in Saudi will be how the main events of both night one and two go.

At the moment, WWE has a host of top stars jostling for position, while Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn currently hold the biggest prizes on offer across both brands.

However, while Zayn's trajectory looks unclear for now, it looks like WWE might be about to pull the trigger on a potentially massive main event involving Reigns.

For months now, fans have been clamouring for Reigns and Oba Femi to come across each other.

As it stands, WWE have held firm on putting anything in place, with Femi completing his current storyline with the Vision last night and Reigns' focus elsewhere too.

However, after MITB last night, Oba Femi commented on Reigns and effectively called out the World Heavyweight Champion, claiming it's time.

With that match seemingly the box office attraction in WWE right now, it looks pretty obvious from the outside looking in that the company will go with Reigns v Femi.

The big question will be whether or not WWE sees enough in Oba Femi right now to pull the trigger and allow him to be the main guy in the company. As we've seen with Cody Rhodes before, WWE have held on for longer, before getting an even bigger payoff.

Clearly though, Femi is set for superstardom and a programme with Reigns will instantly sell tickets.

title: Vikings are 5-0 again, but their own history and the NFL's recent past offer a warning
description: The Vikings have started 5-0 ten times in franchise history, while 15 NFL teams have done it in the past decade.
fullText:
The 2026 Minnesota Vikings are the 16th team in the last decade to start a season 5-0.

Fourteen of the last 15 made the playoffs. The lone team that didn't was the 2016 Vikings, who started 5-0 entering a Week 6 bye, only to finish 8-8.

Those other 14? Five reached the Super Bowl and lost; one lost in the conference championship; and eight lost in the Wild Card round.

2016 Vikings: Finished 8-8, missed the playoffs

2017 Chiefs: Finished 10-6, lost in the Wild Card round

2018 Chiefs: Finished 12-4, lost in the AFC championship game

2018 Rams: Finished 13-3, lost in the Super Bowl

2019 49ers: Finished 13-3, lost in the Super Bowl

2019 Patriots: Finished 12-4, lost in the Wild Card round

2020 Titans: Finished 11-5, lost in the Wild Card round

2020 Seahawks: Finished 12-4, lost in the Wild Card round

2020 Steelers: Finished 12-4, lost in the Wild Card round

2021 Cardinals: Finished 11-6, lost in the Wild Card round

2022 Eagles: Finished 14-3, lost in the Super Bowl

2023 49ers: Finished 12-5, lost in the Super Bowl

2023 Eagles: Finished 11-6, lost in the Wild Card round

2024 Vikings: Finished 14-3, lost in the Wild Card round

2024 Chiefs: Finished 15-2, lost in the Super Bowl

Of those 15 teams, eight of them saw their perfect records fall in their sixth game of the season. The 2018 Rams, 2019 49ers, 2019 Patriots, and 2022 Eagles all started 8-0 before suffering a loss; the 2021 Kyler Murray-led Cardinals started 7-0; the 2024 Chiefs started 9-0 before suffering a loss; and the 2020 Steelers started 11-0 before their first loss.

The last team to start 5-0 and actually win the Super Bowl was the 2015 Denver Broncos, who started 7-0, finished 12-4, and rode an elite defense and the arm of Peyton Manning to beat the Carolina Panthers in the Super Bowl.

This marks the 10th time in franchise history that the Vikings have started 5-0. The 2024 and 2016 teams both floundered, but what about the others?

2009 Vikings: Started 6-0, finished 12-4, and lost in the NFC title game

2003 Vikings: Started 6-0, finished 9-7, and missed the playoffs

2000 Vikings: Started 7-0, finished 11-5, and lost in the NFC title game

1998 Vikings: Started 7-0, finished 15-1, and lost in the NFC title game

1975 Vikings: Started 10-0, finished 12-2, and lost in the Divisional round

1974 Vikings: Started 5-0, finished 10-4, and lost in the Super Bowl

1973 Vikings: Started 9-0, finished 12-2, and lost in the Super Bowl

The Vikings are far from a perfect team, but they do have a defense that looks like it could be historically good, along with a kicker (Will Reichard) who never misses and a returner (Myles Price) who keeps flipping the field. If the offense can stop shooting itself in the foot, perhaps these Vikings can buck the trend, not only of the past decade, but of the franchise's painful history.

title: Daniel Suarez Gives Major Update on NASCAR Future Amid 2027 Spire Motorsports Reports
description: Daniel Suarez has addressed his NASCAR future amid reports he's expected to return to Spire Motorsports in 2027. After a career-best season highlighted by a Coca-Cola 600 victory, the driver says contract talks are getting close.
fullText:
Daniel Suarez has spent much of 2026 proving that his move to Spire Motorsports was the right one. Now, with the NASCAR Cup Series season winding down, it looks increasingly likely he'll get another year to build on that progress.

Suarez's future has been one of the remaining questions surrounding the 2027 driver lineup. But following a report Friday from The Athletic that he is expected to return to Spire, the 34-year-old offered an encouraging update on where things stand.

Speaking with reporters Saturday at Charlotte Motor Speedway, Suarez stopped short of confirming a new deal but made it clear the two sides are making progress.

"We're still working on it. We're pretty close, but we're still working on that," Suarez said.

It's not an official announcement, and Suarez was careful not to present it as one. Still, his comments suggest there may not be much longer to wait before his plans become clear.

For Spire, keeping Suarez would mean retaining a driver who has already delivered one of the biggest victories in the organization's history.

When Suarez joined Spire ahead of the 2026 season, there were legitimate questions about how quickly he could settle into a new team.

He had spent five seasons at Trackhouse Racing, collecting two Cup Series victories before moving to the No. 7 Chevrolet. Spire offered a fresh opportunity, but the organization was still working to establish itself as a consistent contender.

In May, Suarez won the Coca-Cola 600, one of NASCAR's crown jewel events, delivering a victory that immediately gave his first season with Spire a defining moment.

But his performance hasn't been built around that one afternoon.

Through the first 31 races of 2026, Suarez had an average finish of 15.3, putting him on pace for the best season of his Cup Series career. His previous best was 16.2, recorded in 2017 while driving for Joe Gibbs Racing.

That improvement matters when evaluating what comes next. Suarez has shown he can win with Spire, and the team's No. 7 program has given him an opportunity to produce consistent results.

A second season would allow both sides to build on a partnership that has already produced tangible progress.

The contract discussions come as Suarez attempts to salvage something from a difficult stretch in NASCAR's championship Chase.

He entered Sunday's Bank of America 400 at Charlotte 14th in the standings, 195 points behind leader Kyle Larson. Three consecutive 14th-place finishes have left him well outside the immediate championship fight.

Yet Suarez isn't approaching the final five races with a particular finishing position in mind.

"We have goals, but it's not a number," Suarez explained. "Most people will think that a goal has to be a number. For us, the goal is to maximize our potential."

It's a revealing perspective from a driver who has experienced plenty of uncertainty throughout his Cup Series career.

Suarez has raced for Joe Gibbs Racing, Stewart-Haas Racing, Gaunt Brothers Racing and Trackhouse before arriving at Spire. He's familiar with the challenges of changing organizations, earning opportunities and trying to establish some long-term stability.

This time, he may have found a place where the results are giving both sides a reason to continue together.

For now, Suarez isn't putting a date on an announcement. The reported 2027 agreement remains unconfirmed, and negotiations are still ongoing.

But after a season that has included a Coca-Cola 600 victory and some of the most consistent driving of his career, there's a compelling case for keeping the partnership intact.

And judging by Suarez's latest comments, that's exactly what the two sides are working toward.

title: Patriots Coach Mike Vrabel Embraces ‘Next Man Up’ Mentality Amid Multiple Injuries to Team
description: It’s a who’s who of players who have gone down for the Patriots early in the season. Mike Vrabel is embracing the “next man up” mentality.
fullText:
Patriots Coach Mike Vrabel Embraces 'Next Man Up' Mentality Amid Multiple Injuries to Team originally appeared on NESN. 

The term "next man up" has become a literal reality for the Patriots. Despite a 45-17 win over the Raiders this week, New England's injury list has grown.

The Patriots were already without A.J. Brown. Christian Gonzalez, Carlton Davis III, and others were unavailable for the game. Those who did play stepped up, as the defense earned three sacks on 64 total tackles.

Throughout the game, the Patriots had multiple players go to the sidelines. Will Campbell (knee) and TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) didn't return. Corey Kiner ran the ball for 52 yards in Henderson's absence. Meanwhile, Cory Durden was another player forced to the sidelines.

It's a who's who of players that have gone down for the Patriots. It doesn't seem to affect coach Mike Vrabel, who used "next man up" as part of the reason for the Patriots' win.

"We try not to panic. We just try to get the next guy ready. We ask everybody to prepare as a starter. It's a credit to the football player, the guys on this team, the guys we try to bring in here," Vrabel said after the game.

Mike Vrabel on embracing the "next man up" mentality "Cause that's what it has to be... when you get an opportunity and you do something with it, then you get more opportunities." 💪 https://t.co/Ujmgy5Lbfl

"And they realize that, when you get an opportunity, you do something with it, and you get more opportunities."

It's unknown what the status of Campbell, Henderson, and the others who went down is. The hope is that the team can continue to produce while shorthanded next week against the Jets.

title: Antonio Conte reveals his La Masia wish: ‘Barcelona are doing something extraordinary’
description: Italian tactician Antonio Conte has this weekend opened up on his admiration for the current work being done behind the scenes at La Liga giants Barcelona.Barca, of course, have emerged as one of the ...
fullText:
Italian tactician Antonio Conte has this weekend opened up on his admiration for the current work being done behind the scenes at La Liga giants Barcelona.

Barca, of course, have emerged as one of the talking points of world football across the early months of the new season.

Under the watch of mastermind Hansi Flick, the Blaugrana have looked nothing short of unstoppable en route to nine wins from nine across all competitions.

La Masia products have proven central to this ongoing excellence, with the likes of Pau Cubarsí, Fermín López, Lamine Yamal and breakout sensation Xavi Espart shining bright.

Speaking during an extensive interview with The Athletic (as cited by Mundo Deportivo) this weekend, the aforementioned Antonio Conte was therefore asked for his view on the continued success of Barca's famed academy setup.

And the former Juventus and Chelsea headmaster was full of praise in his response:

"They are doing something extraordinary. Seeing these La Masia lads integrate so naturally at 18 into a team like Barcelona, ​​in front of 100,000 people, and play football with such ease makes you realise there is a lot of hard work behind the scenes at the academy, as they work in perfect harmony with the coach."

"I would love to visit their youth academy. They have a well-defined structure, perfectly aligned with the first-team. This year, I was watching a Barcelona match, and I heard a name – that of the left-back (Xavi Espart) – that I didn't recognise. The DAZN commentator said something like: 'This kid only played four 10-minute games last year. This year they wanted to loan him out.' And yet, there he was, starting with astonishing ease."

title: Cagliari 1-1 Juventus ends in headloss as Spalletti and Pisacane see red
description: Luciano Spalletti and Fabio Pisacane were both sent off at the end of the 1-1 Serie A draw between Cagliari and Juventus on Sunday evening in a moment of headloss on the touchline immediately after th...
fullText:
Luciano Spalletti and Fabio Pisacane were both sent off at the end of the 1-1 Serie A draw between Cagliari and Juventus on Sunday evening in a moment of headloss on the touchline immediately after the full-time whistle.

It was a frustrating evening for Juventus at the Unipol Domus: Daniel Maldini fired the hosts into a 20th-minute lead and it took the Bianconeri until the 81st minute to find the equaliser through Randal Kolo Muani. The Bianconeri finished the game with 70% possession and 21 shots on goal.

You can see how the action unfolded on the Football Italia Liveblog.

REGGIO NELL'EMILIA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 13: Luciano Spalletti Head Coach of Juventus reacts during the Serie A match between US Sassuolo and Juventus at Mapei Stadium – Citta' del Tricolore on September 13, 2026 in Reggio nell'Emilia, Italy. (Photo by Emmanuele Ciancaglini/Getty Images)

The frustrations boiled over at the full-time whistle. Pisacance booted the ball up in the air in his technical area before high-fiving a couple of members of his coaching staff before making his way over for the customary post-match handshake with his opposite number.

Spalletti approached Pisacane, visibly frustrated and clearly taking a stern tone towards the Cagliari boss. Spalletti also appeared angered when Pisacane gripped him by the elbow while this exchange was unfolding.

Spalletti then leant in towards Pisacane while still shouting just before the pair were separated by their colleagues.

Spalletti looked stunned when he was shown a red card by referee Matteo Marcenaro shortly afterwards, as did Pisacane when he received the same punishment a few moments later.

BERGAMO, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 12: Cagliari Calcio head coach Fabio Pisacane looks on during the Serie A match between Atalanta BC and Parma Calcio at Stadio Atleti Azzurri d'Italia on September 12, 2026 in Bergamo, Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images)

Both will have to serve one-match suspensions assuming that their red cards are upheld, which will mean Spalletti will have to miss Juve's match at home against Lazio next Sunday and Pisacane will have to do the same for Cagliari's trip to Monza.

title: What happened when Serena Williams made her only appearance at the Wuhan Open in 2014
description: Serena Williams only ever made one appearance at the Wuhan Open in her career, which came in 2014. The Wuhan Open has been a tournament...
fullText:
Serena Williams only ever made one appearance at the Wuhan Open in her career, which came in 2014.

The Wuhan Open has been a tournament on the WTA Tour since 2014, and this year will be holding its ninth edition, having been absent on the calendar for four years.

Despite Williams making a comeback to tennis this year, she will not be competing at the 2026 Wuhan Open.

As a result, this makes Williams' appearance at the WTA 1000 tournament in 2014, her only time ever competing in Wuhan.

Williams came into the inaugural Wuhan Open as the world number one, and was in good form as well after winning her 18th Grand Slam singles title at the US Open, which was her last tournament prior.

As the top seed, Williams received an automatic bye to the second round, where she would play against Frenchwoman Alize Cornet. Cornet was the world number 21 at the time, and while she may have not appeared to be a huge threat to Williams on paper, she had already beaten the American twice that year, including at Wimbledon.

Cornet once again came out on top against Williams, but this was a very different affair to her two previous victories. With Williams leading 6-5 against Cornet in the first set, she received medical attention and did not appear to be feeling well.

Williams subsequently handed Cornet the win after retiring due to a viral illness, and apologised to the fans in Wuhan after the match.

"I'm sorry to all the fans in Wuhan that I had to retire from my match against Alize today," Williams said at the time. "I felt dizzy and nauseous in the first set and unfortunately couldn't continue.

"The tournament organisers have done an amazing job preparing the facilities for this year's event and I really hope to come back to the Wuhan Open in 2015."

Despite Williams stating her intention to return to the Wuhan Open, she would never compete at the tournament ever again.

While Williams losing her only ever match at a tournament is a rare sight, the Wuhan Open is not the only WTA 1000 event where she did not capture a title.

Williams' decorated career spans over 30 years, during which the WTA 1000 and equivalent tournaments have changed. Williams has competed at 15 different tournaments when they were WTA 1000 level events, and she has got her hands on at least one title at eight of those.

WTA 1000 tournament that took place during Serena Williams' career

Appearances Serena Williams made at the tournament

Won the title (2002, 2003, 2004, 2007, 2008, 2013, 2014 & 2015)

Won the title (2002, 2013, 2014 & 2016)

Won the title (2001, 2011 & 2013)

The only tournaments Williams never won as WTA 1000 events were the Qatar Open, Dubai Tennis Championships, the Wuhan Open, the German Open, the San Diego Open, the Zurich Open and the Kremlin Open.

Williams got close to winning some of these titles, but never made more than three appearances at any of these events when they were held as WTA 1000 tournaments.

The only WTA 1000 tournament where Williams lost her only match other than the Wuhan Open is the Zurich Open in 2007, having retired against Patty Schnyder in the first round after losing the first nine games of the match.

title: Commanders let clock run out, tie Giants 27-27
description: The Commanders blew a chance to win the game after a late Cam Skattebo fumble.
fullText:
The Commanders were handed a gift by the Giants in overtime of Sunday's game in Washington and they handed it right back.

Rather than take a knee and work the clock to take a game-winning field goal try with the Commanders out of timeouts after the overtime two-minute warning, Giants head coach John Harbaugh opted to hand the ball to Cam Skattebo on a first down from the Washington 24-yard-line. Skattebo fumbled the ball and the Commanders recovered to give themselves a chance to win the game.

They took advantage of it with Jayden Daniels completing two passes for 29 yards and running for 16 yards on a drive that moved to the Giants' 24-yard line in the final minute. The Commanders only needed to spike the ball to stop the clock and try a field goal, but Daniels instead took a snap and danced around before being stopped for no gain and the clock ran out before the Commanders could take another snap.

The result was a 27-27 tie that should feel like a loss for both teams and both head coaches given how their decisions shaped the ending. Not only did Commanders head coach Dan Quinn bungle the final play, he also saw his team blow a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter after stifling the Giants offense for the entire afternoon. Jameis Winston threw three touchdown passes in the final 15:44 of regulation and the Commanders punted on their final two possessions.

The Commanders elected to kick off in overtime and forced a Dominic Zvada field goal try from 46 yards. Zvada missed for the third time on the afternoon, but the Commanders punted on their first possession of the extra session.

Daniels ended the game with a boneheaded play, but he looked good in his return from a dislocated left elbow for about 50 minutes of play. He had touchdown runs of 38 and 26 yards while picking up 103 yards on the ground for the day and he moved the Commanders pretty consistently until the wind came out of their sails in the final stretch.

Winston lost a fumble and struggled until catching fire late. He had two touchdowns to tight end Isaiah Likely and tied the game with a strike to Malik Nabers. He was 33-of-54 for 326 yards, but the Giants did experiment with using J.J. McCarthy at points in the early stages of the game. McCarthy ran twice for two yards, handed the ball off and threw a pop pass for a five-yard loss that was wiped out by a penalty.

The result leaves Washington with a 1-3-1 record and they'll be on the road against the 49ers on Monday night in Week 6. The tie ends a two-game Giants winning streak and the 3-1-1 team will host the Saints next weekend.

title: All-Pro WR has heaps of praise for former Washington CB Trent McDuffie
description: Former Washington CB Trent McDuffie has been one of the NFL's best cornerbacks in 2026, and he's earned praise from some of the league's best WRs.
fullText:
In his first season with the Los Angeles Rams, former Washington Huskies star Trent McDuffie has asserted himself as one of the best cornerbacks in the NFL.

Through the first four games of the year, McDuffie has posted 13 tackles, 1 for loss, and an interception, while his 7 pass breakups are the most in the league, and he's posted those numbers while having to cover some of the NFL's best wide receivers, including Philadelphia Eagles standout Devonta Smith, Malik Nabers of the New York Giants, and perennial All-Pro Mike Evans of the San Francisco 49ers.

McDuffie's strong start has also impressed his teammates, as star wide receiver Davante Adams had plenty of praise for the 26-year-old two-time All-Pro in an interview with Amon-Ra and Equanimeous St. Brown on the St. Brown Podcast.

"Trent McDuffie, I can honestly say to you I can't remember the last time I felt this way about a corner," the three-time All-Pro said.

"Trent is the real deal because he's always there. He's putting them by the pin every time. If I had to pick a DB to go and cover whoever your favorite receiver is, if it's Amon-Ra, if it's whoever, if my life is on the line, I'm gonna pick Trent to go and cover whoever that receiver is because what I've seen from him, I really respect his game a lot."

Next up for McDuffie and the Rams is a battle with superstar quarterback Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills on Monday Night Football, where the former UW standout will likely find himself matched up with former first-round pick D.J. Moore, if Allen's top receiver is able to suit up after a shoulder injury has sidelined him at practice.

title: Brewers vs Dodgers live updates, score, highlights from NLCS Game 1
description: We have live coverage as the Milwaukee Brewers host the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series.
fullText:
Here we are again, four wins away from the World Series.

The Milwaukee Brewers face the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game 1 of the National League Championship Series at American Family Field.

It's been 363 days since the same scenario in the 2025 NLCS – Brewers-Dodgers Game 1 in Milwaukee. We all know how that game and the whole series turned out; the Dodgers swept the Brewers.

But today brings new hope – maybe even new confidence – for the Brewers and their fans.

The series starts with past and future Cy Young winners on the mound. The likely National League winner, Jacob Misiorowski, will start for Milwaukee. Tarik Skubal, the trade-deadline acquisition who won the past two American League Cy Young awards and a player the Brewers sought at the trade deadline, too, will start for Los Angeles.

It sets up as an epic showdown between two of the game's best pitchers and the two teams with the best records in the majors.

I'll be providing live coverage before, during and after the game. You can follow along here for the latest updates:

Location: American Family Field, Milwaukee

03:53 PM ET, October 11 2026, JR Radcliffe

A look at the three previous times the Brewers have been in the National League Championship Series and how Game 1 went – all games were at American Family Field.

2011: Brewers 9, Cardinals 6. The Brewers took a 2-1 lead after the first and scored six runs in the fifth after the Cardinals had re-taken a 5-2 lead. That frame featured a two-run double by Ryan Braun, a two-run homer by Prince Fielder and another two-run bomb by Yuniesky Betancourt. Zack Greinke struggled but the Brewers bullpen worked three scoreless innings, anchored with John Axford for the save. The Brewers still lost the series, 4-2.

2018: Brewers 6, Dodgers 5. It's the game remembered for Brandon Woodruff's unforgettable home run against Clayton Kershaw in the third inning, though this one turned into a nail-biter even though the Brewers had a 6-1 lead heading into the eighth. The Dodgers scored three times in that inning, once 

2025: Dodgers 2, Brewers 1. This game will be remembered for a defensive play, Sal Frelick's home-run robbery but non-catch that turned into a wild double play. But the Brewers offense had just two hits, with dominant Blake Snell striking out 10 and allowing just one hit in eight innings. Freddie Freeman homered and Abner Uribe issued a bases-loaded walk in the ninth, and though Jackson Chourio hit a sacrifice fly against Roki Sasaki in the ninth, Brice Turang struck out with the bases loaded to end the game shortly after nearly getting hit with a pitch that would have tied the game. It was the most competitive game of the 4-0 series loss for Milwaukee.

Bonus 1982 ALCS: Angels 8, Brewers 3. Played on the road in a best-of-five format, Mike Caldwell lasted only three innings for the Brewers, and Tommy John threw a complete-game for the Angels despite giving up his share of damage. Don Baylor drove in five runs in the first four innings, including a two-run triple in a four-run third for California and another two-run single in the fourth. Gorman Thomas had a two-run homer for one of the rare Brewers highlights, and Fred Lynn added a solo homer for the Angels. The Brewers came back to win the series, 3-2.

title: Biggest winners, losers from Steelers' Week 5 win over Colts
description: Here's a look at the biggest winners and losers from the Pittsburgh Steelers' Week 5 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts.
fullText:
The Pittsburgh Steelers looked incredible in the Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts, advancing to 3-2 on the season following their 34-22 victory. There's plenty to discuss, particularly when it pertains to a few studs — and duds — in the Steelers' Week 5 win over the Colts.

From one of the best running back performances in franchise history to a lackluster outing for one veteran receiver, here's a look at the biggest winners and losers from the Steelers' Week 5 victory.

Warren has solidified himself as one of the league's top running backs over the past few weeks, solidifying the argument with an amazing win over the Colts on Sunday. Warren recorded an 80-yard receiving touchdown, a 50-yard rushing touchdown, and finished the contest with 171 scrimmage yards.

Like Cameron Heyward, Aaron Rodgers appears to be unfazed by Father Time. Rodgers finished the contest with 235 passing yards and three passing touchdowns while completing 71% of his passes. This is now Rodgers' third straight game with three passing touchdowns, and the veteran quarterback deserves his flowers.

Muuuuuuuuth! The sixth-year Steelers tight end was unguardable in the red zone during the Week 5 win over Indianapolis, with Freiermuth finishing the game with five catches for 44 yards and two touchdowns. He's been one of Rodgers' favorite targets through five games and should continue to be a huge contributor in Pittsburgh's offense moving forward.

Michael Pittman Jr. went down, Germie Bernard stepped up. The second-round rookie finished the contest with 73 receiving yards and is primed for a big role with Roman Wilson also dealing with a new injury.

No Joey Porter Jr.? No problem! Asante Samuel Jr. made a handful of key pass breakups, including one against Colts tight end Tyler Warren in which Indianapolis was forced to settle for a 28-yard field goal. If this version of Samuel shows up each week, opposing offenses could be in real trouble.

Metcalf talked a big game when he called out Colts cornerback Sauce Gardner, but he didn't back it up in the receiving game. Metcalf made two monster blocks on Warren's 80-yard touchdown, but the Steelers need more than 12 yards out of their $132 million receiver.

As a whole, the Steelers' defense, particularly against the run, was great in the win. But the pass rush completely fell flat. Heyward was the only defender credited with a sack. Daniel Jones wasn't pressured much throughout the contest, and if there was a weakest link in the win over Indianapolis, it would be the Steelers' pass rush.

title: 5 takeaways from Packers' 31-7 win over Bears: Love makes a statement
description: Green Bay played their cleanest game of the year and Jordan Love reminded the NFL how good he is as they vanquished the Bears at Lambeau Field.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers demolished the Chicago Bears 31-7 to earn their first division win of the season and get their overall record to 3-2. After an up-and-down start to the season, Sunday's win was a much-needed boost to the outlook of what Green Bay can be in 2026.

Here are five takeaways from a huge win in every sense of the word:

Last week's win in Tampa Bay was a step in the right direction on both sides of the ball, even if Green Bay took the shine off it with some late turnovers.

Sunday's win against the Bears was the cleanest, most complete game the Packers have played this season by far, and it could not have come at a more important time. They averaged 7.3 yards per play on offense, allowed 3.6 yards on defense, did not turn the ball over and only committed four penalties.

Matt LaFleur has been the victim of his players letting him down with a lack of execution in recent games. On Sunday, they had the head coach's back in a cathartic win against Ben Johnson and what has become an obnoxious Bears team.

Protect Jordan Love and good things happen. He diced up Dennis Allen's defense at Lambeau Field, finishing the day 25 of 31 passing for 367 yards and two touchdowns, with a passer rating of 137.5.

Chicago's defense has been built on a house of cards and their lack of ability to get home with four was their undoing, with Love killing the blitz as he made a habit of doing last year. He was eight of ten for 130 yards and a touchdown against the blitz with a passer rating of 152.1.

It was not a perfect day by Green Bay's pass protection by any means, but they are clearing the bar of allowing the offense to function, and Love has shown he can do the rest. A word for LaFleur too, who called a great game on offense.

Jonathan Gannon's defense played a fantastic game even without Edgerrin Cooper, shutting down both Tyson Bagent and Case Keenum and limiting them to only seven points while generating five turnovers.

There were strong performances from all three levels of the defense, with Devonte Wyatt playing easily his best game of the year, Ty'Ron Hopper grabbing his opportunity and Brandon Cisse making multiple big plays.

Bagent in particular had a poor game, but the Packers deserve credit for their part in that, and Gannon's unit continues to impress early in the season.

Christian Watson continues to be a Bear killer, racking up 143 yards and two touchdowns on six catches, including a stunning 53-yard reception for a vital score. He has justified his payday and then some, continuing to play like one of the best wide receivers in football.

Matthew Golden just keeps getting better and set a new career high for receiving yards at 123, just two weeks after the last time he did so when he put up 100 yards against the Falcons.

His two deep grabs were sensational, and he is a perfect pairing with Love due to his ability to adjust and reward his quarterback for giving him a chance.

Tucker Kraft had some important catches of his own including a 46-yard reception as he continues to look more like his old self. These three pass catchers give Love all the ammo he needs to light up the scoreboard as they did today.

The only phase that arguably did not hold up its end of the bargain on Sunday was special teams, as Trey Smack missed three kicks which cost the Packers an additional seven points and Cam Achord's unit also gave up a 60-yard kickoff return.

Daniel Whelan did his part, booming punts all day long and flipping the field regularly, but there is work to do on special teams. Those points could have come back to haunt the Packers in a closer game.

title: Cam Skattebo, Jayden Daniels commit OT flubs as Giants, Commanders tie
description: The Giants and Commanders ended in a 27-27 tie after a series of late game blunders by both teams in overtime.
fullText:
The New York Giants appeared to have the game won in overtime ... and Cam Skattebo fumbled.

The Washington Commanders were in position for a game-winning field goal attempt ... and Jayden Daniels apparently lost his mind.

The NFC East teams finished in a 27-27 tie on Sunday in a game neither team could figure out how to win. Fitting.

The Commanders saw the Giants come back from a 27-13 deficit to force overtime after Big Blue missed a long field goal that would have won it.

In overtime, the Giants were driving for what appeared to be a game-winning score via field goal or TD. Skattebo fumbled on his 15th touch of the game.

Washington recovered and used short passes to turn into moderate to long gains.

CHAOS IN OVERTIME 

Cam Skattebo fumbles, and Washington recovers!

📺: FOX/FOX One pic.twitter.com/LeMXcD6EOI

Both teams had used their timeouts in the extra session, something Daniels must have lost track of.

Instead of spiking the ball as the clock ticked under 10 seconds, he called a pass play, tried to scramble and time ran out.

The Commanders can't get the play off in time and this game ends in a tie pic.twitter.com/WmPp6q5hU0

The Giants, who thought they were on the verge of defeat, actually celebrated Daniels' gaffe.

title: A brutal clock error costs Commanders in chaotic OT tie vs. Giants
description: A shocking mistake by Jayden Daniels cost the Commanders a chance to win in Week 5 against the Giants in overtime.
fullText:
The Washington Commanders appeared to be setting themselves up for a chance to kick a game-winning field goal at the end of overtime in their Week 5 game against the New York Giants.

They never got the chance after an inexplicable mistake by quarterback Jayden Daniels.

With 12 seconds remaining in regulation, Daniels fielded a snap from Commanders center Nick Allegretti on a second-and-8. The third-year quarterback scrambled around the backfield for a few seconds before intentionally going to the ground with eight seconds left.

There was just one problem: Washington had no timeouts remaining and was not able to get aligned to spike the ball before time expired. The Commanders' receivers remained far down the field and never stood a chance to get in position to stop the clock.

When they were in position to kick a game-winning FG, the Commanders ran out the clock. https://t.co/qxh9ZMGQ3t

title: Ducks on the pond: Oregon QB situation in flux after unnerving defeat
description: If Dante Moore can't return for Nebraska, Oregon must find a solution between Dylan Raiola and Brock Thomas to drive the offense moving forward.
fullText:
As public address announcer Don Essig announced Dylan Raiola as the Oregon Ducks' starting quarterback before the first series of the day, the crowd at Autzen Stadium erupted with cheer. A few hours later, those same fans couldn't stand the sight of Raiola under center.

That was illustrative of the roller coaster day for the Ducks. The offense struggled to pick up a first down on any given drive, held under 100 yards entering the fourth quarter. Meanwhile, the defense raked in three takeaways and delivered multiple short fields that the offense couldn't take advantage of.

Blame could be spread in a variety of directions. Dan Lanning wasn't good enough. Drew Mehringer wasn't good enough. The running game still wasn't great. But above all, Oregon's quarterback play with Dante Moore watching from the sidelines was atrocious. The offense has never been as out of sync under Lanning as it was on Saturday, and now the Ducks need to find an answer as the schedule only gets tougher.

"Never been in a situation where we turn the ball over that much and still have an opportunity to have success there in the game," Lanning said. "But we weren't successful on offense in any phase tonight. Obviously didn't really get into a rhythm, weren't able to create success there."

Raiola owned his poor play, finishing just 6-of-19 passing with 43 yards and responsible for three of the seven turnovers for the Ducks. Lanning stuck with the Nebraska transfer after halftime, but after two turnovers in the third quarter, Raiola was sent to the bench.

"I thought we were prepared. I thought our coaches prepared us," Raiola said. "We lost, and they were the better team today. I've got to do a better job of rallying the guys, making a play, or getting us going to flip the switch, because we're really one play away from things going the other way. But I can't turn the ball over. I was reckless with the ball today, and you can't win football games like that."

Similar to when Raiola first took the field, the crowd roared in approval when Eugene local Brock Thomas was announced as the new quarterback. Thomas led Oregon in relief last season against Wisconsin when Moore went down with an injury, and he found success to give the Ducks a victory in less-than-ideal conditions.

The Ducks were still hesitant to throw the ball with Thomas on Saturday, as Mehringer reduced the offense to the most basic and fundamental form. But when push came to shove, Thomas delivered, completing 11-of-15 passes for 153 yards and a touchdown.

EVAN STEWART -- HOW?!?! pic.twitter.com/A6h0kCrey2

So, why didn't Lanning make the quarterback change sooner, especially given Raiola's struggles in the first half?

"Probably a fair question," Lanning admitted.

Lanning didn't want to make a rash decision based on the series of turnovers prior to halftime, but after Raiola made another fatal error at the end of the third quarter, he felt like he couldn't put the move off any longer.

"Brock went in and operated well," Lanning continued. "You can always go back and say, 'Hey, we should have done that earlier.' If you knew that turnover was coming, you would have done that earlier, right? We felt like that's a play that we've seen Dylan make a lot in practice, and he didn't make that play today."

Lanning didn't commit to Moore returning to play against Nebraska, and it's fair to wonder if the star quarterback who is a projected first-round pick in the NFL draft will throw another pass for the Ducks this season. In the immediate future, the Ducks have two options: roll with Raiola and see find out if he can be the future for next season, or turn to Thomas, the senior who hasn't always played well but has certain limitations.

Thomas had success in relief, nearly leading the Ducks to tie the game before a facemask penalty against the Bruins prevented him from crossing the goal line on the 2-point try. In his four seasons playing for his hometown team, Thomas has never started a game. He could be in line to do so for the first time next week against Nebraska.

"I think Brock showed up when his number was called, waited for his opportunity," Lanning said. "There's going to be some things that he did really well in this game, and I'm sure there's going to be some moments for growth for him. But he works extremely hard. There's a reason we put him in that situation. I thought he operated well when he had those moments. I'm not surprised about what Brock was able to do when he did go in."

The Ducks didn't give Thomas a chance to throw the ball until seven minutes remained, trailing by two scores. He connected with Dakorien Moore down the left sideline for a 36-yard gain while eating a massive hit from UCLA defensive lineman Aidan Gobaira. The big play and the penalty yardage instantly put the Ducks' offense in goal-to-go.

BROCK THOMAS TO DAKORIEN MOORE HUGE PLAY OMG pic.twitter.com/mkxjZ87IZf

Raiola's poise and calmness were praised in the lead-up to Saturday's ranked matchup, but it was Thomas who displayed those traits in his limited action, giving Lanning and the offensive staff something to consider this week, as well as potential changes to the play-caller.

"Going in there, if you're frantic, freaking out, thinking about a million different things at quarterback, you're not going to be successful," Thomas described his mindset when Lanning gave him the nod. "Going in there with a clean mind, just trying to calm myself down, get in there and trust the guys that I've got around me, and going in there with the most confidence I can."

Sitting on the bench was disappointing for Raiola, but he understood the reason why.

"Look, Brock's my boy. If we're trying to spark something to get us going, I just want to win," Raiola said. "Unfortunately, I wasn't in the plans to lead us down the stretch. But I can't speak on that right now. I'm not sure what that's going to look like. I want to think it was just that we were trying to spark something, but we'll see. The game of football is all about competition. That's what it is, and we've got to be ready to go next week."

"He knows he didn't have the best day," Thomas said of Raiola. "He's going to respond better than anyone, in my opinion. He's a great guy, fun to be around. I've loved him ever since he came here, and I think he's going to do great."

Oregon now has a competition on its hands. Moore's immediate future with Oregon is uncertain. If the Ducks were to lose again, Moore might not have much to gain by returning to the field, risking injury or lowering his draft stock.

That leaves Raiola and Thomas dueling for the starting role, and even Akili Smith Jr. could get an opportunity at some point. Never has Oregon's offense been more of an unmitigated disaster, and the Ducks have to make a change this week. The problems go beyond preparation or "evaluating the film" to fix things in practice, as Lanning often says.

Raiola was not in a position to succeed, and he also didn't do himself any favors when he did have open receivers. Unless the offense makes a sudden change in scheme and overall aggression, it could be difficult for Raiola or Thomas to have more success next week against a Nebraska defense that held Indiana to 20 points.

Difficult conversations need to be had, and Lanning should provide some clarity to Oregon's quarterback position on Monday. If Moore doesn't return this week, the Ducks could be in a heap of trouble, and it doesn't appear there is much they are willing to do about it, other than hoping for a flip of the switch in practice.

title: Leeds United Target 23-Year-Old Centre-Back With £43.5m Clause: Does Farke Need Him?
description: Leeds United have reportedly tried to sign Sevilla centre-back Andrés Castrín, but the 23-year-old looks set to stay in Spain after agreeing to a new deal, according to Ficherio, relayed by Sport Wi...
fullText:
Leeds United have reportedly tried to sign Sevilla centre-back Andrés Castrín, but the 23-year-old looks set to stay in Spain after agreeing to a new deal, according to Ficherio, relayed by Sport Witness.

The Spanish outlet reported on 9 October that Castrín will extend his contract with Sevilla until June 2030. The agreement includes a salary increase and a €50 million (£43.5m) release clause, changing the situation that had made him an option for Leeds.

Valencia and Real Sociedad were also said to have made approaches. Castrín's previous contract was due to expire in June 2027, giving interested clubs an opening to negotiate a transfer or wait until he became a free agent. Ficherio says sporting directors presented financial and sporting proposals, although the report has not confirmed a formal bid from Leeds.

The reported renewal would give Sevilla control over the defender's future. Ficherio adds that Castrín's new salary will reflect first-team status, while remaining below the wages of academy graduates Kike Salas and Isaac Romero.

Castrín's rise helps explain the attention. He played 31 matches for Sevilla Atlético in 2024/25, then made one senior appearance for Sevilla. His role grew in 2025/26, when he featured in 21 first-team matches and logged 1,393 minutes.

He has continued to feature this season, with six LaLiga appearances and 480 minutes listed for 2026/27. At 23, he is a young centre-back already gaining top-flight experience rather than a prospect still waiting for his senior chance.

For Leeds, the attraction may have been financial. A defender approaching the final year of his deal could have offered value if Sevilla struggled to agree an extension. The reported €50m clause would make a move more difficult, although a release clause does not automatically establish market value.

SEVILLE, SPAIN – MAY 04: Isaac Romero and Andres Castrin of Sevilla FC celebrate following victory in the LaLiga EA Sports match between Sevilla FC and Real Sociedad at Estadio Ramon Sanchez Pizjuan on May 04, 2026 in Seville, Spain. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images)

Castrín looks more like a long-term option than an urgent requirement for Daniel Farke. Leeds already have Joe Rodon, Jaka Bijol and Tarik Muharemović, with Nico Elvedi providing experience and familiarity with Farke from Borussia Mönchengladbach. Any move would need to match Leeds' squad needs and budget.

A shortlist place makes sense. Castrín's progress and previous contract position offered a reason to keep watching him, but there is no confirmed evidence that Leeds United made a formal offer. If the reported renewal goes through, Leeds may have to look elsewhere for a centre-back at a more manageable price.

title: Blades Brown becomes youngest to earn PGA Tour card via Korn Ferry Tour
description: Blades Brown finished second in the Korn Ferry Tour championship on Oct. 11 and became the youngest player on the tour to earn his PGA Tour card.
fullText:
Former Brentwood Academy golfer Blades Brown became the youngest player to earn a PGA Tour card as a Korn Ferry Tour graduate on Oct. 11.

Brown, who is 19 years, 4 months and 20 days old, clinched it in the final round of the Korn Ferry Tour Championship at The Federal Club in Glen Alley, Virginia.

He finished second in the KFT finals, which left him ninth in the points standings and one of 20 players to earn their PGA Tour card on Oct. 11. The others were Ross Steelman, Sandy Scott, Ian Holt, Alistair Docherty, Alvaro Ortiz, Austin Hitt, Cole Sherwood, Doc Redman, Tommy Morrison, Cooper Dossey, Hunter Eichhorn, Dylan Menante, Michael Johnson, Jeremy Gandon, Taylor Dickson, Ian Gilligan, Davis Shore, Carson Young and Davis Lamb.

Brown turned down several college scholarship offers to turn pro in 2024. He made 11 starts on the PGA Tour and 17 on the KFT in the 2026 season. He made 24 of 28 cuts on the two tours.

He was third at the Puerto Rico Open on the PGA Tour and had three top-five KFT finishes.

Brown became the youngest U.S. Amateur stroke-play medalist in 2023 when he was 16. He won three straight TSSAA Division II AA individual state championship (2021-23).

title: Marvin Harrison Jr. trade grades: Texans take a shot for C.J. Stroud, Cardinals get great value
description: Marvin Harrison Jr. gets second life in Houston with his former college QB while Arizona gets some good return.
fullText:
Marvin Harrison Jr. trade grades: Texans take a shot for C.J. Stroud, Cardinals get great value originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

The Cardinals no longer need to be disappointed in the production of wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., their No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. Arizona followed through on hot trade rumors and dealt Harrison to Houston on Sunday.

Moving Harrison well before the trade deadline in November ensured the Cardinals would get the best possible return because he can still have some real impact on another team for most of the season. The Texans, bit by the injury bug plenty outside of Nico Collins, were tied most to Harrison give they are quarterbacked by C.J. Stroud. Stroud and Harrison built a strong downfield connection and boosted each other's stock at Ohio State.

Stroud's strong arm gets another field-stretcher. The Cardinals streamline their offense further with Trey McBride and Michael Wilson still being the go-to receivers for Jacoby Brissett. Here's breaking down the swap for both sides:

MORE: Full details of Marvin Harrison Jr. trade to Texans

Knowing how little Harrison has produced for Arizona, getting a second-rounder is a pretty good coup for a rebuilding team. Houston, at 1-4, was desperate enough to get back in the playoff picture to bring in Harrison as a potential big playmaker.

The Texans' desperation cost them quite a bit as they wanted to add more playmakers beyond Collins and busy slot ace Jaylin Noel. They also are forced to be a high-volume passing team because of an anemic running game, now with top veteran back David Montgomery hurt.

Collins is a dominant No. 1 receiver and his presence often demands double coverage. Behind him, Xavier Hutchinson and former Patriot Kayshon Boutte have been only sporadic targets. The Texans were expecting big things from Jayden Higgins as the outside No. 2 before he went down with a knee injury before the season. Tank Dell has been on the mend for a long while attempting his comeback to play.

The Texans want to be a downfield passing team with Stroud, stretching the field better. Harrison was supposed to provide that element for the Cardinals and also be a consistent red zone threat with his big frame. Now the Texans are hoping Harrison's size and speed will manifest more as he works to improve his route-running in a more favorable scheme under Nick Caley. Stroud's passing presence should be a boost to Harrison accelerating some part of his development.

Houston feels like it can still make a playoff run playing in the AFC South. Arizona didn't need a wideout it wasn't throwing to at all.

The Cardinals should be thrilled they got a second-round pick, which for now would be almost a first-rounder at No. 36 overall given the Texans' shoddy record. They will keep rooting for the Texans to struggle against better teams even with Harrison.

Harrison was seeing a very limited role in Arizona. The team will be fine moving on with Michael Wilson, Kendrick Bourne, Simi Fehoko and others at wide receiver, given how much tight end Trey McBride means to Mike LaFleur's offense. Harrison didn't take advantage of the new coach, having the same trouble he had under the previous regime with now Lions offensive coordinator Drew Petzing. That sealed his fate with the Cardinals early in a make-or-break season.

Arizona admitted early it made a big mistake drafting Harrison so high. They can't be blamed too much, given Harrison was dubbed as a can't-miss generational talent, the son of his. namesake Hall of Fame receiver. They deserve credit for not waiting too long for Harrison to prove his worth, instead flipping him for maximum value.
