title: Forrest earns major invites with Spanish Open win
description: Scotland's Grant Forrest holds off a charge from home favourite Eugenio Chacarra to win the Spanish Open and book a spot at The Open and the Masters next year.
fullText:
-14 G Forrest (Sco); -13 E Chacarra (Spa), V Perez (Fra); -12 J Skov Olesen (Den); D Brown (Eng), J Dean (Eng)

Selected others: -10 L Aberg (Swe); -8 S Lowry (Ire); -7 M Penge (Eng), F Molinari (Ita)

Scotland's Grant Forrest held off a charge from home favourite Eugenio Chacarra to win the Spanish Open and book a spot at The Open and the Masters next year.

With Chacarra in the clubhouse at 13 under, Forrest and playing partner Victor Perez needed to make birdies at the 18th to go above the Spaniard.

Both players' drives nestled down in the greenside rough on the 322-yard par four, and after Perez's birdie putt drifted past the hole, Forrest sunk his to seal his third DP World Tour title and a first professional win outside Scotland.

"I'm in pure shock just now," Forrest said. "It's been such a tough year. I've got good memories of this course and this tournament. To do it is unbelievable.

"It was tough. I wasn't too sure what other groups were doing. It was a matter of staying in it. I dug in so well.

"That's fairytale stuff, I've played two Opens and to be going to Augusta, I just can't get my head round it. You can have a great career in this game and never get to go to Augusta, so I cannot believe it."

Going into the final round in a share of the lead with England's Joe Dean on 13 under, Forrest birdied the fourth, but made bogeys at three, six and eight as he dropped two shots off the top.

However, Forrest showed excellent resilience and moved back into a share of the lead as he started his back nine with three birdies and a bogey in five holes.

And he got the job done with a tidy up-and-down at the last to card a closing one-under 70 and take home the £480,000 first prize.

title: Puerto Rican boxing legend Gomez dies aged 69
description: Three-weight world champion Wilfredo 'Bazooka' Gomez dies aged 69.
fullText:
Three-weight world champion Wilfredo 'Bazooka' Gomez has died aged 69.

The Puerto Rican won the WBC super-bantamweight title, WBC featherweight belt and WBA super-featherweight crown during a career in which he was renowned as a heavy puncher.

Gomez fought in 48 fights and won 44, with 42 by virtue of knockout, and was inducted into the International Boxing Hall of Fame, external in 1995.

Former president of the sanctioning body the WBO Paco Valcarcel confirmed the passing of his compatriot.

"He passed away a few hours ago, the one to whom I owe having entered the great family of international boxing," wrote Valcacel on social media on Saturday.

"Rest in peace, my eternal champion Wilfredo 'Bazooka' Gomez."

Gomez's best wins came against fellow greats Mexico's Carlos Zarate, two-weight champion Lupe Pintor, domestic rival Juan Laporte and American Rocky Lockridge.

Zarate was his finest win, stopping the then 52-0 knockout specialist in five rounds in front of his home fans in San Juan to retain his WBC super-bantamweight title.

Boxing schedule and results 2026

Watch every Born to Brawl episode

Competing during a stacked era of talent at his weights, Gomez suffered heartbreak in two of his biggest fights when he was knocked out by Salvador Sanchez in 1981 and Azumah Nelson in 1984 - both at featherweight for the WBC world title.

The WBC and its president Mauricio Sulaiman called Gomez "one of the greatest icons in the history of the sport" and that he had passed away "after being hospitalised for the past two weeks due to respiratory complications".

"Universally recognized as one of the greatest ring legends of all time and a ruthless brawler who holds the historic record of 17 consecutive super bantamweight title defenses - all won by knockout - Wilfredo Gomez leaves behind an indelible legacy both inside and outside the ring," a statement said., external

As an amateur, Gomez competed at the 1972 Olympics aged just 15 and at 17 would win gold at the inaugural World Amateur Championships in Cuba.

title: Jaguars stun Eagles with last-second win in London
description: Cam Little kicks a 57-yard field goal in the final second to seal a 19-17 victory for the Jacksonville Jaguars against the Philadelphia Eagles in an exhilarating NFL London game at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.
fullText:
Cam Little kicked a 57-yard field goal in the final second to seal a 19-17 victory for the Jacksonville Jaguars against the Philadelphia Eagles in an exhilarating NFL London game at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

The Jaguars had conceded the lead with eight seconds remaining after the Eagles completed their own 48-yard field goal, but Ameer Abdullah made 53 yards on the return before being tackled with a second on the clock.

The 23-year-old Little completed the lengthy pressure kick and tore off his helmet, racing to the end of the pitch to celebrate in front of the fans, arms outstretched like England midfielder Jude Bellingham, before being mobbed by his team-mates.

The game featured drama in its opening moments as Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr and Jaguars defensive end Bryan Thomas Jr were ejected for fighting on the opening kick-off.

Josh Cameron had scored a 90-yard touchdown for the Jaguars from the kick-off, but the score was nullified for the penalties resulting from Trotter seemingly shoving his opponent to the ground before appearing to receive a kick in return.

The Eagles, who were missing their top two running backs in Saquon Barkley and Tank Bigsby, were the first to concede when Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington reached the endzone in the first quarter.

In perhaps a nod to Manchester United legend Wayne Rooney, Washington did a boxing knockout celebration.

However, the Eagles went into half-time with a 14-3 lead following touchdowns from third-choice running back Will Shipley and wide receiver Darius Cooper.

Little's 34-yard field goal cut the deficit in the third quarter, although he missed the extra-point kick when Parker Washington's 27-yard touchdown gave the Jaguars a 16-14 lead with three minutes and 20 seconds remaining.

This time, Washington copied Chelsea forward Cole Palmer's cold celebration.

Jake Elliott appeared to have completed a winning kick in the closing moments, before the Jaguars' special-teams line-up set up Little for a dramatic conclusion.

The Jaguars are now on a three-match winning streak, while the Eagles are on a losing run of the same length.

The Florida franchise sit top of AFC South early in round five with a 4-1 record, while the Eagles are second in NFC South with both their wins coming in their opening two fixtures.

title: Jota comeback helps Celtic lift gloom in strong response
description: Jota's comeback from long-term injury and Celtic's convincing victory over Motherwell provide positivity following the club's recent acrimony.
fullText:
After weeks of acrimony at Celtic, the full-time scenes at Fir Park on Sunday provided welcome cheer for a disgruntled fanbase.

Off the back of three straight defeats before the international break - two of them inflicted by rivals Rangers - Martin O'Neill's side returned to winning ways as they deservedly beat struggling Motherwell 2-0 and returned to the Scottish Premiership summit.

Camilo Duran fired the visitors in front early on and midfielder Benjamin Nygren made sure of victory in the second half.

On top of the performance and result, influential winger Jota made his long-awaited return from injury after almost 18 months on the sidelines and it was the Portuguese who led the post-match celebrations.

Jota had been introduced as a 74th-minute substitute and almost provided an assist with his first touches in a lively cameo.

"I was waiting on this for a long time," he told Sky Sports. "Just happy to be back. I've been working hard, the guys have been helping me as well. It was just the normal nerves, but after I stepped on the pitch everything goes well."

The 27-year-old was asked about the mental toll of his long spell out of action.

"Imagine if someone takes away your child and I've got my child back today - that's how I've been feeling the last year," he said.

"I found my child again today and I just want to keep it as long as I can.

"I'm feeling very good and I'm ready to play more and more and help the team. I know what I can do."

Celtic back on top as win at Motherwell halts losing run

Decision to stay at Celtic did not take long - O'Neill

The party atmosphere at full-time was in stark contrast to the general gloom that has surrounded the club lately.

On top of the disappointing run of results before the international break, Celtic's largest shareholder, Dermot Desmond, was the target of a protest during the Alfred Dunhill Links golf tournament in St Andrews.

O'Neill questioned whether he had the energy to continue as manager after Rangers won at Parkhead last month, before committing to stay on.

"I could only imagine the pressure on Martin O'Neill - I know what it's like in Glasgow if you are beaten by Rangers twice," former Scotland defender Willie Miller said.

"But it seems like he's got his mojo back and is back to his old form and that's what results do.

"All round, when you look at his team, it must give him a lot of satisfaction."

O'Neill himself added: "Of course, there was a lot of noise and a lot of it we brought on ourselves as well too. So, nice to win.

"We have to take the criticism at the time. We lost three matches in a week - two to our big rivals. But we fought back today and let's see what Thursday brings.

What Thursday brings is undoubtedly a sterner test for O'Neill and Celtic with Portuguese giants Benfica lying in wait in the Europa League.

Celtic then host Hearts - who Benfica beat 7-2 on aggregate in European qualifiers earlier this term - before facing Celta Vigo in another stiff Europa League test.

They missed a heap of chances against Motherwell, with opposition goalkeeper Alex Paulsen making 12 saves, but O'Neill was not concerned by his side's profligacy.

"We had a lot of chances and we could have [scored more]," he said.

"The first goal's really important, a great goal by Camilo and it settled us down which was good.

"A lot of things have flashed across the box, a number of chances in both halves, but delighted to win.

"Just really pleased. Pleased with the performance, pleased with the energy that we showed and delighted to win.

"It's psychologically a big boost to play as well as we did and go back to the top of the table."

title: Verstappen perfect and Antonelli hugely mature - driver ratings
description: BBC Radio 5 Live F1 commentator Harry Benjamin rates how the drivers performed during the Singapore Grand Prix.
fullText:
Max Verstappen took his second win in a row with victory from pole position at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The Dutchman also won the final sprint event of the campaign at Marina Bay and has moved up two places in the drivers' standings from sixth to fourth.

Championship leader Kimi Antonelli finished third and has extended his title advantage over Mercedes team-mate George Russell, who was ninth, to 102 points.

Here are my ratings for how the drivers performed across the whole weekend in Singapore.

Pretty much the definition of a perfect weekend. Pole and victory in both the sprint race and grand prix, and once George Russell crashed out of the sprint on Saturday there was barely a moment where Red Bull's Verstappen looked like losing control of either race.

Consistently Verstappen's closest challenger and took two podiums from the weekend. Third in the sprint followed by second in the grand prix was about as much as Ferrari could realistically have asked for.

Another hugely mature weekend from Mercedes' championship leader. Fourth in the sprint and fourth in qualifying before fighting his way on to the grand prix podium late on, despite dealing with brake concerns and flirting a little too often with track limits.

Sunday was solid enough, with fourth probably the maximum McLaren had on outright pace. But his collision with team-mate Oscar Piastri in the sprint cost both drivers heavily, and prevents this from being rated as a particularly strong weekend.

The victim rather than the instigator of McLaren's sprint collision and recovered with a decent Sunday performance. A slow puncture forced an extra stop but he still chased down and passed Lewis Hamilton for fifth, although seventh in qualifying left him with plenty of work to do.

His Saturday was excellent - a brilliant start helped turn sixth into second in the sprint before he qualified third for the main race. Ran in the podium places for much of Sunday too, but his decision to stay out on worn tyres backfired badly and eventually dropped him to sixth.

A really impressive weekend for Racing Bulls' Lawson. Fifth in the sprint, ninth on the grand prix grid and seventh on Sunday meant points in both races and another reminder of just how strong his recent form has become.

Another very useful weekend for Audi. Took points with seventh in the sprint, narrowly missed Q3 and then finished eighth in the grand prix, holding Russell behind late on in the process.

The pace deserved a much higher score. Fastest in practice, second in sprint qualifying and sensational off the line to take the sprint lead. However, throwing it into the wall at the end of lap one was a major mistake. Recovering from 19th on the grand prix grid to ninth was an excellent response from the Mercedes driver.

Almost everything that went wrong before Sunday was outside of his control. Mechanical trouble on his Red Bull ended his sprint and reliability problems meant he couldn't set a qualifying time, so recovering from the pit lane to score a point was an excellent drive.

Eighth in qualifying was one of the stronger midfield performances of Saturday. Just missed the points in both races and comfortably led Alpine's challenge across the weekend, even if there wasn't quite enough race pace to convert it.

A particularly good sprint where he produced a smart move on Gasly and came home sixth. He qualified P12 and the grand prix was less spectacular, but scoring three sprint points still made this a useful weekend for Haas' Bearman.

Finished 10th in the sprint and 13th in the grand prix without ever really looking like threatening Haas team-mate Bearman's points haul. A fairly anonymous weekend in which Briton Bearman had the upper hand.

Starting the sprint from the pit lane immediately made life difficult and there was little improvement afterwards. Qualified in 14th and finished there, making this another frustrating weekend for Williams.

There was obvious pace in qualifying, where he reached Q3, but the rest of the weekend was a lot messier for the Racing Bulls driver. Spinning to the back in the sprint and then slipping from 10th to 15th on Sunday meant the potential never really translated into a result.

Aston Martin had hoped Singapore would suit the car but it never materialised. Alonso was only 17th in qualifying and finished there on Sunday after an equally quiet sprint.

Verstappen dominates for first Singapore Grand Prix win

Hamilton apologises to Ferrari as Antonelli moves to brink of title

Another difficult weekend for Cadillac. His sprint ended almost immediately after contact with Lance Stroll, and 20th in qualifying left him with little chance of recovering on Sunday, eventually finishing 17th.

A messy sprint included the three-car incident with Gabriel Bortoleto and Valtteri Bottas before the Williams driver eventually retired. Qualifying 17th didn't offer much encouragement either, and another retirement late in the grand prix completed a poor weekend.

Caught up in the sprint collision involving Albon and Bortoleto, before qualifying 21st for the grand prix in his Cadillac. Reaching the finish on Sunday was about the only positive, three laps behind the winner.

His sprint was over on the opening lap after the collision with Perez, for which neither driver was penalised. Qualified 19th before a clutch problem ended his race midway through.

Not much chance to build any momentum across the weekend. Retired early from the sprint, hit the wall on his final qualifying lap and then suffered a suspected driveline or gearbox-related technical issue on his Alpine in the grand prix.

His sprint retirement came in the three-car accident with Albon and Bottas, so there wasn't much he could do about that. P15 in qualifying was less impressive, before another early retirement on Sunday brought a frustrating weekend to an end for the Audi man.

title: Winless and an 'easy touch' - what's happened to the Anfield fear factor?
description: Liverpool's struggles at Anfield continue as Iraola still awaits his first Premier League win at Anfield.
fullText:
It is early days but Andoni Iraola will know that if his time at Liverpool is going to be a success, then he must make Anfield a fortress again.

Right now, the struggle is real.

Liverpool were impressive for the most part against a Manchester City side that arrived on Merseyside with a 100 per cent record.

However, once Ryan Gravenberch was sent off in the 62nd minute, they capitulated to a 3-0 defeat.

As Iraola said post-match to Match of the Day: "We played two different games. One until the red card, and then after.

"For 60 minutes, the players were very good. The second game from the red card was where City were better than us."

His unbeaten start is now over. This was actually his first Premier League defeat in 24 games (W10, D13) since January, including his time at Bournemouth.

The Reds, though, are now winless in three Premier League home matches this season - although they have won at Anfield in the Champions League and Carabao Cup - for just the second time ever.

That winless run in the league at Anfield stretches back to last season with Liverpool now winless in five successive Premier League home games (D4 L1).

Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock told BBC Radio 5 Live: "The best teams in the world are also horrible to play against. Liverpool aren't horrible.

"They're an easy touch at the moment. They have too many players that are nice and they have to change that part of things.

"Liverpool have got a lot of work to do.

"They don't have enough leaders at the moment, apart from Virgil van Dijk barking orders."

'Man City's Anfield win has feeling of irrelevance with season in limbo'

Man City cruise to statement win over 10-man Liverpool

Going back to the start of the year, Liverpool have won just four games in 13 Anfield Premier League matches.

In fact, they have won more matches away from home than at home during this period.

A closer look at the stats clearly shows Liverpool's home form has dropped off season by season since 2023-2024, although it is important to note this season is still a very small sample size.

Away sides have a lower win percentage at Anfield (12.5 per cent) than at any other stadium in Premier League history.

However, is this reputation starting to dwindle?

Ex-Man Utd midfielder Paul Scholes told The Good, the Bad and the Football podcast in September: "When you go to Liverpool, especially when Jurgen Klopp was there, the crowd played such a major part. It feels like that's gone… I don't think the fans are quite on board at the minute with what's happening there.

"When we used to go there, I'd think, 'how are we going to get the ball?', because they were on top of you. Teams seem to have a lot more possession and look a bit more comfortable than they ever have."

And Scholes' former team-mate Nicky Butt added: "The likes of Fulham five years ago are going to Anfield and they're beaten before they even go up the steps."

While Liverpool have won twice on their travels this season, they now sit ninth in the league - and their main issue seems fairly clear.

They have scored just seven goals this season - just twice at Anfield - and only seven teams have managed fewer.

It was early on in the first half when the cameras panned to Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai in the Main Stand at Anfield - all three of them were out with injuries.

Among them, the trio have scored six of Liverpool's seven league goals this season and on a day when Man City's attack showed their class, Liverpool didn't show any quality in the final third.

City (16) have scored more than double the goals Liverpool (7) have scored this season in the top flight.

Across three league games at Anfield this season, Liverpool have failed to score in two of them. That must improve.

In Isak's absence, Lewis Koumas put in a great shift. However, the 21-year-old lacks that killer edge in front of goal at this level.

The focus must fall on Florian Wirtz and Bradley Barcola. It is this kind of game where you need a match-winning moment and neither showed anywhere near the quality that is expected when you have a price tag of over £100m.

There was one moment at 0-0 in the 55th minute when Wirtz had Milos Kerkez and Barcola in acres of space to his left, but chose to shoot and fired wide.

"You learn a lot in games like today," Iraola said. "I am very proud of my players. They put the work rate and everything in today. It's a loss and we didn't get anything from the performance but I liked it a lot."

But deep down, Iraola will know there is a lot of work to do and getting the big money signings to deliver will be high on his agenda.

title: Hamilton apologises to Ferrari as Antonelli moves to brink of title
description: Lewis Hamilton's incorrect strategy call during the Singapore Grand Prix means Kimi Antonelli can win the world title at the next race in Austin.
fullText:
Lewis Hamilton apologised to his Ferrari team after overriding the pit wall and choosing his own strategy during the Singapore Grand Prix.

Ferrari were on course to finish second and third with Charles Leclerc and Hamilton, but instead the seven-time champion fell back to sixth in the closing laps as he fought a losing battle to hold off three cars while on fading tyres.

Hamilton apologised to the team over the radio on the slowing-down lap after the race, saying: "Sorry, boys. I let you down today with that strategy. My call, and I lost us valuable points. I'll try and make up for it in the next one."

Team principal Frederic Vasseur said: "Clearly we asked them to pit. Charles pitted. Lewis didn't want to pit because he... I don't know why. And then he realised it was the wrong call. It's why he apologised to the team.

"Now it's not a drama for me that he made the wrong call. I'm making mistakes, he's making mistakes, we're all making mistakes sometimes. Now we have to look ahead and make mistakes positively."

Verstappen dominates for first Singapore Grand Prix win

Verstappen perfect and Antonelli hugely mature - driver ratings

Hamilton did not speak to the media after the race after saying he felt unwell and being given permission to miss the interview zone, known as the media pen.

In a statement released by Ferrari, he said: "Under the virtual safety car, the team called me in but I missed the entry. After that, I decided to stay out and try to hold track position to the end but in the closing laps, I was struggling massively with tyre degradation and lost three places, finishing P6, which doesn't reflect the pace we had in the car.

"A painful lesson, but I take full responsibility for the decisions I made. Not every call will work out, and I can accept getting it wrong but I'm sorry for the team for the points we lost today. They put so much into every weekend, and I wanted to deliver more for them. I'll continue to put the work in and come back fighting at the next race."

Ferrari called both cars in to the pits during a virtual safety car that was called mid-race. Stopping under the VSC saves about 10 seconds versus stopping under racing conditions.

Hamilton said in the statement that his decision was based on his improved pace on the soft-compound tyre after he had been forced to make an earlier pit stop than planned because the medium tyre on which he started the race was not performing.

"At a track (where it's) difficult to overtake, you need to try something different and I chose to start on a new medium tyre, to go long and try to make a one-stop work," he said.

"Unfortunately the medium didn't perform as well as the soft. I had a good second stint and the pace was back, but I couldn't make the progress I needed."

His first stop was six laps before Leclerc's and when the Monegasque emerged back on to the track, Hamilton was right behind him and was initially faster.

At one stage, he pointed out to the team that he had "lost two seconds on that lap", but the team decided not to invert the cars. Hamilton followed Leclerc within two seconds for a further 10 laps before slowly starting to lose ground a couple of laps before the VSC.

Vasseur said the team decided to leave Leclerc in front because he had pitted later than Hamilton.

"The tyre advantage was for Charles, that he pitted six laps later," Vasseur said. "I think it was the right call."

However, that argument appears to be somewhat undermined by the fact that the medium tyre emerged as the worst option for the race - as Hamilton had found out in the first stint and other drivers found later on.

Leclerc was put back on the soft when he stopped under the VSC.

Hamilton's error means Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli is in a position to clinch his first world title at the next race, the US Grand Prix in Austin, after finishing third behind race winner Max Verstappen and Leclerc.

Antonelli's lead over team-mate George Russell, who finished ninth after starting from the back of the grid, has extended to 102 points and 111 over Hamilton.

The Italian needs to leave Austin with an advantage of at least 125 points to clinch the title, with five races at most remaining after that.

He will do so if he wins the race with Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton fifth or lower at the Circuit of the Americas on 25 October.

If he becomes champion this year, the 20-year-old will be the youngest in Formula 1 history.

Asked if he would be daring to dream about the title on the flight home, he said: "For sure, but at the same time, I know it's very close, I know it's there, but I just need to make sure that I keep doing the best I can.

"The mindset is always the same, to go out there and win and perform the best way I can.

"This weekend I haven't particularly driven that well. I felt like I could have done a better job, but I feel confident that a week to reset and I'm really looking forward to being back in Austin.

"But at the end of the day, if I don't do my job well, then the result won't come. So in order to achieve what I want, I need to perform, as simple as that."

There is some doubt about the mathematics of the championship because it is not completely clear how many races are remaining.

F1 is pushing ahead with the original schedule, which ends with two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, despite the war in the Middle East, having been reassured the countries are safe.

But if the war intensifies before mid-November, those races will have to be cancelled. In that event, the season would end at Imola in Italy, on the same 6 December date as Abu Dhabi, after a two-week break following the Las Vegas race on 22 November.

Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff said: "I haven't looked at it from that perspective, because the moment I have the thought of 'how many points is it actually, and when could he win it,' I remind myself that this is motor racing and crazy things have happened.

"The aim must be to score points, not to lose too many on the others, like today, gaining on Lewis, which was unexpected, and then it's going to come towards him, whether that's in Mexico or Brazil (the races immediately after Austin) or further down the line."

Mercedes split their cars between two different specifications in Singapore in an attempt to understand why a major upgrade introduced at the previous race in Malaysia did not work.

Antonelli drove the new spec and Russell the old, and by the end of the weekend the team said they had made some progress in understanding the new aerodynamic package.

Antonelli said: "We're just trying to understand how to extract more potential out of it because we do see the gains, we do see what it could bring.

"It's just that the window is very small at the moment where the car operates and is very sensitive to the way you drive it, the way you take a corner, the way you brake. So it reacts very differently.

"So hopefully now in Austin, we have three free practices, so we can be very open-minded with set-up and hopefully we can find a way and we can use the full potential of the package and finally see the gains."

Russell was asked how he viewed the rest of the season now the championship was almost over. He replied: "The goal is to improve the car. We were dominant for so long and since the break we have seen Red Bull be exceptionally fast on many different types of circuits and we need to go back to winning ways."

Verstappen's victory was his first grand prix win in Singapore. It was also his second in succession, emphasising Red Bull's return to the front after a difficult start to the season.

Verstappen said: "Very different tracks that we have gone well at now. That's of course always nice to see.

"Our car has taken a really nice step forward. It's just been more driveable and more predictable. That's what I wanted and needed from the car to find that last step to fight up front. And I hope that we can carry that momentum forward.

"We don't really have anything to win in the championship, right? Kimi is miles ahead. I don't care if I'm second, third or fourth. It doesn't do anything. But I just want to have fun until the end, you know, try to go for a day's success."

But the four-time champion was cautious about the prospect of being competitive at every race before the end of the season.

"It's very difficult to say and I don't want to say now that I will be in the fight in Austin," he said.

"Yeah, the last few weekends have been great. But I just take it race by race and once we are in Austin, then we'll see how it will go there. But it's again a very different track.

"From what I saw in WEC (the World Endurance Championship), the track is incredibly bumpy. Oh my God, yeah, I'll probably need to order a new spine, I think, after the weekend. Yeah, I'll become like Robocop. Yeah, crazy. That's again a new challenge for everyone, to deal with those bumps.

"And then we just go from there. We have to go to Mexico, high altitude, everything will run super hot, and we need to see how the engine is going to perform in that altitude, how the car is behaving, because it's very different.

"So there are so many different things that you can get right or wrong in those races."

title: Burnham to release details of Man City meetings
description: Andy Burnham has faced criticism for comments he made in the wake of Manchester City being found guilty of all charges related to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.
fullText:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said he will release details of his meetings with senior figures at Manchester City following criticism of his comments in the wake of the club being found guilty of all charges related to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules.

An independent commission found City had broken rules over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018 by creating "sham" contracts with commercial partners to secretly funnel more than £830m into their football operations.

Burnham's previous role as mayor of Greater Manchester has led to questions about his relationship with City's Abu Dhabi ownership, with Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch demanding No 10 release all details of meetings between the prime minister and senior figures at the club.

"I've been asked by the leader of the opposition to publish details of my meetings, which I'm happy to do and I'm going to," Burnham told the Rest is Politics podcast.

"I will quite clearly put out there everything that I have done working with them in my previous role as Mayor of Greater Manchester.

"None of it is recent, actually, in terms of the meetings I had. I only had one significant meeting, actually, and that was in 2021."

The prime minister initially told the BBC he would be "really concerned" if Manchester City's owners decide to sell up following the guilty verdict before later denying his reaction had "downplayed the seriousness of the findings".

However, some Premier League clubs were so "astonished" by Burnham's stance that sources told BBC Sport they were "concerned" about political interference in the appeal process.

Sanctions are yet to be announced and City have lodged an appeal against the verdict.

City returned to action for the first time since the guilty verdict when they played at Liverpool on Sunday, winning 3-0.

Clubs fear political interference in Man City appeal

Premier League: Man City face Liverpool at raucous Anfield in first game since guilty verdict

Burnham was mayor of Manchester from 2017 until earlier this year and his tenure took place during a sustained period of success for City.

As mayor, he championed investment from the Gulf as a way of growing Manchester's economy, a strategy which was initially pursued by the city's leaders before Burnham became the inaugural elected mayor of the Greater Manchester Combined Authority.

"I don't think I misspoke," said Burnham of his past comments on Man City's owners.

"What I would say is my mind hadn't been on all of the issues. My mind had been on Labour Party conference and I was doing interviews in relation to it.

"And also, I didn't link those two things. You know, the questions linked those two things. What I would say is they're very separate.

"The football issues are different from the investment issues. People will try and conflate those two things, but they shouldn't, in my view.

"The football issues, the findings of the independent commission are serious, as I said in the interview."

The entire process involving the charges against Manchester City is independent of the Premier League.

An independent commission held a 42-day hearing in 2024 which led to the verdict announced last month, with City also guilty of all charges except one relating to non-cooperation with the Premier League investigation.

The commission's report said that "a number of important club witnesses gave false evidence in key respects and that some knowingly gave untrue and dishonest evidence".

A separate independent appeal board will hear City's appeal. The club continues to deny any wrongdoing.

title: Man City's statement win has feeling of irrelevance with season in limbo
description: Manchester City record what they will view as a statement win at Liverpool - but is it a statement that carries any weight during a Premier League season in limbo, asks Phil McNulty?
fullText:
Manchester City made what they will regard as a powerful statement in the most hostile territory against Liverpool at Anfield - but is it a statement that carries any weight during a Premier League season in limbo?

City's attention turned to on-field matters in their first game since being found guilty of 114 charges related to breaches of Premier League financial rules between 2009-10 and 2017-18.

The fates, and fixture list, decreed it would be at Liverpool, whose fans nurse the most burning sense of injustice after finishing second to City in 2013-14, 2018-19 and 2021-22.

Their argument centres on the belief those titles could have been theirs had City not possessed the high finance of their Abu Dhabi-based owners, using it in the manner that led to them being investigated.

With this as the backdrop, City strode into this fevered Anfield atmosphere, with Liverpool fans high on adrenaline and determined to make their contempt for their rivals obvious - then outclassed Andoni Iraola's side in a 3-0 win.

On another day, in other circumstances, the manner of City's victory would have fed the narrative that this was a performance of champions, a winning marker laid down to their rivals as they hold a three-point lead at the top of the table.

Not here. Not in the Premier League's dysfunctional state.

Instead, once the predictable sound and fury had been diluted by City's composure and the swift realisation they were not unnerved by Anfield or the storm raging around the club, this was a surreal experience.

After the feast of excitement delivered when Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp presided over the greatest domestic rivalry of recent years, this was an occasion - remarkable as it seems - that seemed robbed of a sense of jeopardy by the circumstances surrounding it.

Yes, it was a statement display and City celebrated wildly at the final whistle, but will it count for anything given they await potential sanctions suggested including Premier League relegation or a record points deduction?

As Erling Haaland looked close to tears in front of Manchester City's fans, including his father Alf-Inge, and head coach Enzo Maresca pumped his fists in jubilation, Anfield's DJ slipped Fleetwood Mac's 'Little Lies' on to the loudspeakers in a final message of defiance.

Maresca said: "We knew there was going to be noise but we need to make our own noise by winning games. We need to learn to deal with the noise but the message is to win games.

"For me it's quite easy. I try to focus on things I can control. There are things that are not in my hands so I don't stress about them.

"I cannot control things outside football, so why stress? I stress about gameplan, day-by-day training sessions, but the rest it's not in my hands."

Haaland added: "For every single person part of Manchester City, every fan, this is a lovely moment that will stay with us for a long time. It was tough. It was hard, but we showed amazing character from back to front. So proud of everyone.

"It's always tough to come here. If you look at the record it's tough. With the Pep Guardiola and Jurgen Klopp era it was tough for both teams, always has been. It was important to stay strong mentally, stick together and do what you can do something about. The thing we can do something about is to play good football and fight together. That's the only thing we can do."

City have appealed against the verdict, but until the dust settles and final decisions are made, this Premier League season is in a holding pattern.

When City come to Anfield and win, especially as convincingly as they did here, it should be a win without qualification or questions.

This does not apply amid the current uncertainty.

Every victory, every league table, will come with a metaphorical asterisk until clarity and finality comes. No-one knows when this will be.

City's players did their jobs to perfection, victory secured by second-half goals from Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki. It is all they can do.

There can be no escape, however, from the cloud hanging over Manchester City because every win will carry the same rider - producing a state of inertia that is not good for the Premier League.

In the end, a day that promised huge discomfort for City ended in a stroll.

City navigated the hostile reception awaiting them at Anfield by arriving through the staff and contractors' entrance - while an inevitable febrile environment awaited them.

Even the derided half-and-half scarves were doing a roaring trade, until it was noticed the sky blue half read: 'Shamchester City - The Cheats'.

The announcement of City's line-up was drowned out by deafening jeers, while banners around Anfield carried a variety of messages.

They including 'A Generation Of Supporters Cheated', 'And After All You Really Robbed Us All' and - in a nod to the Oasis song Stop Crying Your Heart Out, written by Noel Gallagher who was at Anfield, 'All Of Your Stars Are Fading Away'.

This was all watched by an impassive City chief executive Ferran Soriano, but any notion their fans would turn on the owners was dispelled by a flag reading: 'In Khaldoon We Trust. We've Won It All', a gesture of support for the embattled chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak.

City's fans also waved hundreds of inflatable bananas, an old habit when they spent time in the lower leagues in reduced circumstances. There remains the possibility they will get the chance to wave them down the tiers once 

The first half did much to pour cold water on what started as a red-hot atmosphere, further diluted by City's second-half domination, although Liverpool's fans rammed home their disgust until the final whistle, chanting "cheat" every time their opponents passed in a lengthy period of possession.

Former Liverpool and England defender Stephen Warnock told BBC Radio 5 Live: "This needs rectifying as quickly as possible, but this isn't an easy thing to come to a conclusion. It's never-ending. It's so difficult and it's going to take so long to sort out."

He added: "The hard part is that this is a brilliant Manchester City team, but you have to caveat it and say they have done it illegally and they bought their way. You're caught in what you're thinking about this City team.

"I admire them because they're so good individually and so great, but the way it has been done and put together has not been put together correctly."

While ex-Man Utd striker Wayne Rooney, added: "I know what it is like from managing Derby County when they had a points deduction. The mindset and message to the players was simple – just try to win the next game.

"All the noise around the club, from the media and other fans, will make them even hungrier to succeed."

As City walked off, they were accompanied by the taunt of "You're going down" from the Kop.

City's fans answered with the trademark: "We're not really here."

This, in essence, is what makes this Premier League campaign one that might yet be rendered void. City might win the title - but who knows if they will be here next season?

As Maresca's side move into top gear and threaten to accelerate away from the chasing pack with wins such as this, no-one has a clue what their final destination will be.

title: Lakers' Luka Doncic reveals how he let LeBron James and LA down last season following injury
description: The Los Angeles Lakers fell short of their goal last season. Luka Doncic just got honest about how he let LA down last season in the playoffs despite not playing.
fullText:
Lakers' Luka Doncic reveals how he let LeBron James and LA down last season following injury originally appeared on The Sporting News. Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here.

Luka Doncic is going to be on a mission this season, as he believes last year was difficult in several ways that were beyond his control. The superstar was one of the best offensive players in the game but also dealt with personal issues away from the court.

Doncic and his ex-fiancée separated, making it difficult for him to spend time with his two daughters.

"I didn't see them almost the whole season. Yea I can't go another season like that. You wanna spend time with your kids everyday. So last season was pretty hard. I saw them for 5 days in the whole season which is impossible to do. But you know I had to focus on basketball," Doncic said.

However, Doncic also believes he hurt the Lakers during the playoffs last season when he suffered an injury. The franchise star feels he could have prevented the injury from becoming as serious.

"When it comes to my spirit of trying to win, I am just stubborn. I felt a little bit in the first half that I should have just stopped. I should have come out. I think we had a team that could compete for the championship. I definitely regret it," Doncic said.

On Saturday, Doncic revisited those comments, explaining that he felt he had let the team down.

"I thought we had a team that could compete for a championship, so it was kind of disappointing, kind of let the team down, so it's definitely motivating for this season," Doncic told the media.

This season, the potential MVP will look to approach things differently and avoid pushing through an injury when doing so could make it worse. With LeBron James no longer on the roster, the Lakers will rely heavily on Doncic to lead the team.

Missing the playoffs always stings, especially when a team believes it has the pieces to make a deep run. Doncic will look to make the most of this season, as Los Angeles will need him available as often as possible.

title: Donations to major parties and an ex-premier as a lobbyist: how datacentres play the political game in Australia
description: As governments face community backlash for fast-tracking developments, big tech’s financial contributions face renewed...
fullText:
As governments face community backlash for fast-tracking developments, big tech’s financial contributions face renewed scrutiny

Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

On 14 June 2025, Anthony Albanese stood inside an enormous sphere of glass and steel, surrounded by 40,000 plants from around the world. His mind was firmly fixed on datacentres. The prime minister was in the Seattle headquarters of Amazon Web Services. He stood alongside the company’s chief executive, Matt Garman, who outlined a $20bn plan to build datacentres in Melbourne and Sydney.

Speaking to a travelling press pack, Garman was emphatic that Australia was “incredibly important and a great market” for the world’s biggest datacentre company.

Within days of Albanese returning home, Amazon reported its largest payment to an Australian political party on record. The company’s federal disclosures show a $46,500 payment to the Labor party’s federal branch on 28 June.

This was one of 34 payments – totalling $538,000 – that Amazon made to Labor and Liberal branches over a six-year period.

While the money did not influence the government’s decision making, it continued a trend of Amazon disclosing payments shortly before or after multibillion-dollar announcements.

Payments such as this are legal. But as governments face community backlash for fast-tracking datacentres, these financial contributions are facing renewed scrutiny.

So, too, are the well-connected political operatives, from former policy advisers to at least one former premier, who have been paid to lobby governments on behalf of datacentre companies.

Transparency International Australia’s chief executive, Clancy Moore, says a cutting-edge industry is relying on old methods.

“Datacentres are the new extractive industries but [are] using the old techniques of cash for access payments and full scale lobbying to influence our political system,” Moore says.

In 2024 the Albanese government announced a $2bn deal with Amazon Web Services to build three top-secret datacentres to store sensitive information gathered by intelligence agencies.

Eight days before that deal was announced, on 26 June, Amazon disclosed a $33,000 payment to Labor, according to Australian Electoral Commission filings. Less than six weeks later, another $33,000 payment was disclosed.

The payments were membership fees for the party’s fundraising vehicle, the Labor Business Forum, which facilitates access to ministers and MPs. Amazon has paid more than $200,000 in membership fees to the forum since mid-2021.

Under Australian electoral law, such membership or subscription fees to political fundraising vehicles are not technically classed as donations. Instead, they are listed as “other receipts”. But ultimately, the money goes to the same place: the party.

The proximity of these payments to major deals, while coincidental, highlights ongoing concerns about companies paying political parties for additional access to decision makers.

Amazon has also been busy attending state fundraising events.

Between mid-2021 and mid-2025, Amazon paid $38,100 to the New South Wales Labor party and $37,400 to the Liberals. During this period, the company was also pursuing several new datacentres on Sydney’s outskirts.

An Amazon spokesperson said its payments to fundraising forums were not related to public investments, including datacentre projects.

The federal government and the ALP national secretariat were contacted for comment.

In his final weeks as prime minister in 2022, Scott Morrison toured a new five-storey datacentre in Sydney’s north-west. After cutting a blue ribbon to declare the facility open, Morrison praised his hosts for keeping Australia at the “leading edge” of the digital economy.

Three days before Morrison’s 25 March speech, Macquarie Technology Group disclosed a $3,000 donation to the NSW Liberal party. This came shortly after two separate payments from the ASX-listed company to the same branch worth $15,000 in January 2022.

The company had been sending a steady stream of money to the NSW Liberal branch as the IC3 East datacentre was being built in the Macquarie Park innovation district. The money was also flowing as it plotted another larger adjacent datacentre, known as IC3 Super West.

Australian Electoral Commission disclosures show Macquarie made six payments to the state Liberals worth $10,700 between 12 November 2020, and 7 June 2021. NSW disclosures show the company also paid the branch $1,500 to attend a boardroom lunch with then Liberal treasurer, Dominic Perrotett, on 15 June 2021.

While there is no suggestion these payments sought to influence planning decisions or had any impact on applications, they overlap with milestones for the company.

On 15 July, Macquarie told investors about its plans for IC3 Super West, which could be fast-tracked by new rules deeming datacentre’s “state significant developments” that could be approved by a minister, rather than a local council.

Government documents show a planning application was under way by early August with a sustainability and emissions report completed on 26 October.

Three days earlier, on 23 October, the company paid $1,980 to secure a lunch meeting with Ryde’s Labor mayor, Jerome Laxale, and the then Labor leader, Chris Minns, at a Parramatta restaurant.

Laxale had no role in assessing the application, as it was before the state government. At the time, he was preparing for council elections on 4 December. In 2022, he stepped down after winning the federal seat of Bennelong.

A spokesperson for Laxale said “all donations were reported in accordance with requirements”.

The City of Ryde has now become a strident critic of datacentres, despite having 12 existing or proposed facilities within its boundaries. It told a parliamentary inquiry in March this year that it was “deeply concerned” about a “rapid concentration” placing “significant pressure” on electricity and water supplies.

According to the AEC, Macquarie has paid $2.2m to state and federal branches of the Liberal and Labor parties since 2000.

A company spokesperson said “any suggestion that these activities influence planning outcomes is incorrect”.

“Macquarie Technology Group engages with federal, state, and local representatives from across the political spectrum through business forums, industry events and stakeholder engagement activities.

“[The group] complies with all state and federal electoral disclosure requirements and does not provide political support in exchange for planning approvals, government decisions, or policy outcomes.”

A NSW Liberal spokesperson said the party disclosed all donations in line with its obligations.

Datacentre companies are increasingly turning to well-connected lobbyists to further their commercial interests.

Viridis Green datacentres, which is proposing a number of small datacentres in regional areas, is among them.

The company has paid former Queensland National premier Rob Borbidge to lobby Liberal National party ministers and senior public servants on its behalf.

Lobbying records show that, in late August, Borbidge gave two of the state’s most senior planning officials a tour of a Brisbane datacentre built by the company.

This followed four meetings with public servants since March, including one arranged after discussions with a minister’s office.

Borbidge’s engagement came after Viridis made a $20,000 donation to the Queensland LNP on 20 October 2025. Sources familiar with the payment say it funded an event at the LNP party conference on the Gold Coast in November.

Viridis was contacted for comment.

Abigail Boyd, the upper house Greens MP leading a NSW parliamentary inquiry into datacentres, questioned why companies would pay political parties if they didn’t expect a return.

“Multi-billion dollar companies don’t make donations to major political parties for fun; they do it to acquire access, influence and good favour,” Boyd says.

The independent Australian Capital Territory senator David Pocock, a member of a federal inquiry into datacentres, says he is concerned about technology companies bankrolling election campaigns.

“We’ve seen big tech pour huge money into political donations ahead of the US midterm elections,” he says. “While at a smaller scale and in different ways, I’m concerned the same pattern is playing out here.”

The Centre for Public Integrity’s executive director, Catherine Williams, says a lack of transparency about federal lobbying activity “heightens community concern” about payments to political parties.

“There is a legitimate question to be answered about the purpose of any entity paying for party forum membership, or to attend political party/candidate events, if it is not to obtain access and influence that is beyond the reach of ordinary Australians,” Williams said.

Hughes focused on Albania before World Cup dream
description: Wales forward Elise Hughes admits reaching the World Cup would fulfil a lifelong ambition.
fullText:
Wales forward Elise Hughes says the prospect of reaching the World Cup would fulfil a lifelong ambition but insists the focus remains on Tuesday's play-off second leg against Albania.

Rhian Wilkinson's side take a slender 1-0 advantage into the return fixture in Llanelli after edging the first leg of their play-off semi-final.

A draw would be enough to send Wales through to the next stage of qualifying for next summer's tournament in Brazil.

"When you're a kid, it doesn't get bigger than that," Hughes said of playing at a World Cup.

"You dream and you're in the garden thinking of the World Cup and you're at your grassroots team thinking of the World Cup.

"Now this group has a chance to do it and that is the most important thing for the group here and now.

"But to do that, we've got to win the game on Tuesday. This is the most important game to date because it's next."

Should Wales overcome Albania, they will face either Norway or Romania in a two-legged play-off final in December.

Even if Wales win that play-off final they could face a potential inter-confederation play-off in February.

Head coach Wilkinson acknowledged her side will need to improve in Llanelli after an unconvincing 1-0 first-leg victory in Shkoder.

"There's always room for improvement," Sunderland's Hughes told BBC Sport Wales.

"We've won games by many more goals and always had room for improvement.

"We knew they're a good side and what they're going to bring [but] we let them into the game. It's all about focus and getting the result."

title: Karaoke-singing Zheng makes history with China Open win
description: Zheng Qinwen becomes the first Chinese champion of the China Open after overcoming Mirra Andreeva in straight sets.
fullText:
Zheng Qinwen became the first Chinese woman to win the China Open by beating Mirra Andreeva in straight sets in Beijing.

Zheng, who entered the tournament as a wildcard ranked number 54 in the world, saved three set points in Sunday's opening set before overcoming fourth seed Andreeva 7-5, 6-4.

Th 24-year-old fell to the floor as she secured match point and treated the raucous home crowd to some karaoke following her victory speech.

"The feeling was incredible. To win here in Beijing in front of my home crowd is one of my dreams," she said.

"I've been through a very, very tough year."

For Zheng, who underwent elbow surgery last year, it was a first WTA 1000 title and her sixth title over all. The triumph brings an end to a two-year title drought for a player who has struggled with form and fitness in the past 12 months.

Andreeva, 19, was on top in the early stages of both sets, but was reeled back in both times.

The Russian led 2-0 in both sets and 5-4 in the first before Zheng defended three set points and won the remaining 11 points to win the opener 7-5.

Andreeva continued to make mistakes in a second set that was finely poised at 4-4 before Zheng took control.

The crowd was passionate ,although disruptive, at times between points and a late double fault from Zheng in the final exchanges briefly threatened to derail a special occasion for Chinese tennis.

But there was to be no late collapse and Zheng sealed the win with an ace.

The win is her 14th win over a top-10 opponent and her third this season.

Despite the loss, Andreeva is expected to rise to number three in the world when the rankings are updated on Monday.

Zheng is set to leap up 31 spots to number 23.

title: Wall Street banks had a blockbuster first half. Higher rates could change everything.
description:
Wall Street's biggest banks entered the second half of 2026 after one of their most profitable six-month runs in at least a decade. Then interest rates surged. 
When they kick off third quarter earnings on Tuesday, starting with JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Goldman Sachs (GS), and Citigroup (C), followed by Bank of America (BAC) and Morgan Stanley (MS) on Wednesday, investors will be hunting for clues around whether sharply rising interest rates are beginning to spoil the first-half boom.
Profits at these giants should fall from last quarter, as their revenues from trading, dealmaking, and financing are expected to retreat from the levels that powered standout second quarter results, according to analyst estimates compiled by Bloomberg. Still, most are expected to show profits rose from a year ago, with Bank of America and Morgan Stanley expected to prove the exceptions.
fullText:
Wall Street's biggest banks entered the second half of 2026 after one of their most profitable six-month runs in at least a decade. Then interest rates surged.

When they kick off third quarter earnings on Tuesday, starting with JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Goldman Sachs (GS), and Citigroup (C), followed by Bank of America (BAC) and Morgan Stanley (MS) on Wednesday, investors will be hunting for clues around whether sharply rising interest rates are beginning to spoil the first-half boom.

Profits at these giants should fall from last quarter, as their revenues from trading, dealmaking, and financing are expected to retreat from the levels that powered standout second quarter results, according to analyst estimates compiled by Bloomberg. Still, most are expected to show profits rose from a year ago, with Bank of America and Morgan Stanley expected to prove the exceptions.

"Right now, you look out the window, and it feels okay. I think this is more about the risks than what's happening out the window," said Brendan Coughlin, president of regional lender Citizens Financial Group (CFG), which reports later next week.

The mood among investors has already soured. Collectively, these five banks have shed about $270 billion in market value from their respective summer highs through Friday's close, even as the S&P 500 (^GSPC) remains up roughly 14% this year.

"A great deal of the recent underperformance for banks has been driven by the dramatic rise in long-term rates," UBS analyst Erika Najarian recently told clients. A Truist Securities survey earlier this month found just 35% of institutional investors expect bank stocks to outperform the broader market, down from 68% in July and 82% in December.

The key focus for investors next week is less on what higher borrowing costs mean for third quarter profits than on whether the rapid repricing of money will begin to undermine the unusually strong activity that defined 2026's first half.

Higher rates can initially lift banks' lending income, but they also raise deposit and wholesale funding costs, pressure bond portfolios, and complicate math for dealmakers.

The speed of the move in rates also adds unease. Macquarie strategists noted this week that many of the highest-profile financial blowups over the past 50 years happened shortly after abrupt moves in long-term bond yields.

Trading results are expected to bring the most immediate evidence for a Wall Street slowdown. In September, bank executives telegraphed softer activity, particularly in fixed income, compared to the frenzy that kicked up this spring.

title: Verstappen dominates for first Singapore Grand Prix win
description: Red Bull's Max Verstappen secures his first win in the Singapore Grand Prix, ahead of Charles Leclerc and Kimi Antonelli.
fullText:
Red Bull's Max Verstappen took his second dominant victory within a week as he secured his first win in the Singapore Grand Prix.

Verstappen fought off an attack from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc off the start line to control the race from start to finish.

The win followed his and Red Bull's maiden victory of the year in Malaysia last weekend and sprint race success in Singapore on Saturday, confirming the team's re-emergence as a major force.

Leclerc took second as team-mate Lewis Hamilton finished sixth after a baffling strategy that was a consequence of the Briton choosing not to pit when asked.

Hamilton, trying to last out on a set of soft tyres for a mammoth 44 laps, lost out in the closing laps to Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and the McLarens of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.

Antonelli's third place combined with team-mate George Russell finishing only ninth after starting from 19th extends the Italian's championship lead to 102 points.

That means it is possible for Antonelli to clinch his first world title at the next race, the United States Grand Prix on 25 October.

To become champion in Austin, he would need to win the race with Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton fifth or lower.

The key stories of the race were:

Verstappen's dominance reviving memories of his pomp during his title-winning era

A confusing day at Ferrari with regard to strategy

Antonelli closing on the world title

Verstappen knew he needed to get into the first corner first to try to win the race, given the difficulty of overtaking in Singapore, and he fought tooth and nail to make sure he did.

Leclerc got a better start than Verstappen off the line and challenged down the inside as they approached Turn One.

But Verstappen squeezed him tight towards the pit wall and with their entry to the first corner so compromised, Leclerc eventually backed off and the four-time champion could claim the corner.

Verstappen, Leclerc and Hamilton ran nose to tail for the first four laps before the seven-time champion began to drop back from about lap five.

Leclerc stuck within a second of Verstappen for a further five laps before the Red Bull began to edge away from him as well.

From then on, Verstappen continued to build his lead and never looked like being beaten as he motored away into the distance.

"I think the last few races have been really positive for us and it is just great to see and we have a lot of motivation in the team to try and deliver even more results," said Verstappen.

"It is a really good group of people - I really enjoy working with them and hopefully we can have a bit more fun until the end of the year."

In the interviews immediately after the race, Antonelli was told he can win the title in Austin and responded: "Can I? Really? Let's not worry about that, let's try to do the best weekend possible and finish the job."

Hamilton had started on the medium tyres while Verstappen and Leclerc chose the softs. Despite his theoretically more durable tyres, the Briton pitted on lap 18 to switch to the softs, while Leclerc waited until lap 24 to swap his softs for mediums.

Leclerc came out of the pits from his stop just ahead of Hamilton, who had stronger pace on his softer tyres.

Yet Ferrari chose not to order Leclerc to let Hamilton through to maximise his pace, a decision that was questioned by Hamilton from the car.

A virtual safety car was called on lap 39 and Leclerc and Antonelli, who had chased the Ferraris closely from the start from his fourth place on the grid, took the opportunity for a cheap pit stop - it takes 10 seconds less to stop under a safety car than under racing conditions.

Yet Hamilton, despite having older tyres, did not stop, a decision that promoted him to second behind Verstappen.

As Leclerc was catching Hamilton, the Briton was told he needed to stop again; he pushed back to suggest he try to go to the end, but was told they were six laps short to make it in terms of tyre life.

Leclerc soon caught Hamilton and passed him on lap 46 and set off after Verstappen, but could get no closer than 7.3 seconds to the Red Bull.

Hamilton never did stop, but as his tyres lost grip he fell back into the clutches of Norris and Antonelli.

A passing attempt by Norris on lap 54 with eight to go saw Hamilton run off track and take to the escape road at Turn One, but as he did, Antonelli grabbed the chance to pass the McLaren, and then Hamilton later on the same lap.

Norris followed him through, and now Hamilton fell back towards the second McLaren of Oscar Piastri, who passed him on the final lap after a resolute attempted defence from Hamilton.

It was Hamilton's call not to stop and he apologised for it on the slowing down lap - but there remain a number of questions as to the choices made.

Russell's fight back through the field took him up to seventh as he delayed his pit stop as long as possible.

But after dropping back to 10th behind Audi's Nico Hulkenberg and Alpine's Pierre Gasly, he passed Gasly after trailing him for 10 laps or so, but could not make it past Hulkenberg, who was himself chasing Racing Bulls' Liam Lawson.

Red Bull's Isack Hadjar took the final point in 10th after starting from the back.

Constructors' championship standings

It's off to the Circuit of the Americas in Austin for the United States Grand Prix, from 23-25 October, where 20-year-old Antonelli has his first opportunity to become the youngest Formula 1 world champion in history.

title: Late Sale penalty try continues Harlequins woes
description: Harlequins' poor start to the Prem season continues with a third successive loss of the campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium.
fullText:
Tries: Canakaivata, Warr, Bamber, penalty try Cons: Ford 3

Tries: Riley 2, Smith 2 Cons: Smith 2

Harlequins' poor start to the Prem season continued with a third successive loss of the campaign against Sale at CorpAcq Stadium.

The Sharks came from behind to win the game with a 73rd-minute penalty try after the returning Marcus Smith had touched down twice in the opening quarter to give Quins an early lead.

After their opening-day reverse to Bristol at home, Sale have bounced back strongly with back-to-back wins over Saracens and Quins.

Despite their first points of the season, the loss leaves Quins rooted to the foot of the table.

Harlequins, crushed 48-0 by Gloucester last weekend, were much more resilient and, with Smith involved for the first time this season after a finger injury, much more threatening.

But Sale, while nowhere near their best, fought their way out of a tight corner to record their fifth successive win against Quins in domestic and European competition.

Quins were good value for a 17-14 half time lead, scoring three tries and having two more disallowed by the television match official (TMO).

Hooker Sam Riley gave them a third-minute lead after Smith and George Furbank had combined in midfield. Then Smith finished off some fine approach play from Furbank.

Sale, without Tom Curry who dropped out through illness, struck back with a try of their own from Fijian Elia Canakaivata on his first Prem start before Smith sliced through some poor defence for his second try.

The hosts cut the deficit just before half-time through scrum-half Gus Warr but with the Sharks making too many errors, Riley was mauled over for Quins' bonus-point try in the 53rd minute.

Sale fought their way back through a try by lock Ben Bamber after a break by Nicky Smith and a big line-out steal from Courtney Lawes kept them within striking distance.

And they went ahead after a rumbling maul which took Quins back 30 metres before Riley pulled the ball down close to the try line.

Referee Christophe Ridley awarded a penalty try and sent the hooker to the sin-bin.

There was no way back for Quins who must hope a change of competition to the Challenge Cup next week, with a home fixture against Vannes, brings a change of fortune.

Sale: Carpenter; O'Flaherty, Marchant, Lozowski, Reed; Ford, Warr; N Smith, Jibulu, Opoku-Fordjour, van Rhyn (c), Bamber, Lawes, Tshiunza, Canakaivata.

Replacements: Cowan-Dickie, McIntyre, Francis, Dugdale, Hanson, Louw, Loganimasi.

Harlequins: Furbank; Green, Northmore, Bradley, Murley (c); M Smith, Porter; Hobson, Riley, Kerrod, Dun, Treadwell, Kenningham, Driscoll, Cunningham-South.
