title: Sensational Smith, relentless quicks - Australia veterans serve reminder
description: The fearsome pace quartet and Steve Smith's brilliance serves as a reminder of Australia's quality as the tourists take charge against South Africa.
fullText:
First Test, Durban (day three of five)

Australia 390 & 33-0: Maddinson 17*

South Africa 284: Bedingham 49; Cummins 3-54

Australia's modern Test side remain a fascinating one to unpick.

Viewed by many in England as there for the taking in last winter's Ashes despite a 4-1 win, they are also labelled too old by many observers at home.

The victims of recent shock defeats by West Indies and Bangladesh, they are still unbeaten in their past nine Test series.

But while their struggling batting line-up was bailed out by Matt Renshaw across the first two days of the first Test in Durban, they took control over South Africa on day three in an all-too familiar way.

Nine years after they first appeared together as Australia's bowling quartet, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood, Pat Cummins and Nathan Lyon produced their latest relentless performance to dismiss South Africa for 284. There was even some magic from Steve Smith thrown in too.

Cummins took three wickets, Starc, Hazlewood and Lyon two apiece, in doing so brushing off any doubts about their effectiveness at the start of a run of Tests against the world Test champions, in-form New Zealand, India and England.

At 82-1 in response to Australia's 390, South Africa appeared well in the Test.

Australia's bowlers searched for early swing and Aiden Markram and David Bedingham countered with a second-wicket partnership which progressed at almost 4.5 runs per over.

It was then, at the 20-over mark, captain Cummins reverted to Australia's tried and tested - Lyon one end, the quicks rotating at the other.

Having bowled 34% of their deliveries full in the first 20 overs, Starc, Hazlewood and Cummins dragged back their lengths. There were only 19 deliveries pitched fuller than six metres between the 20th and 60th overs.

With deliveries easy to hit scarce, Markram and Bedingham attempted forced back-foot drives and edged to slip for 37 and 49 respectively.

Wiaan Mulder was caught in two minds and bounced out by Cummins. Tristan Stubbs top-edged the Australia captain to fine leg.

In Australia's first innings, Renshaw, who ground out a superb 190, faced 52 deliveries pitched as short and played a pull or hook shot to four of them. He scored runs with only one of those shots - when he had 176 runs to his name and had faced 368 balls.

The contrast to Renshaw's application could not have been greater.

Six overs after Stubbs was caught, Marco Jansen, who had struck six fours in quickly reaching 26, also tried to pull Hazlewood off a fuller length and was tamely caught at mid-off.

The quality of the bowling and fact the Proteas are playing their first Test since November were other factors in South Africa's slide.

At the other end, off-spinner Lyon bowled 19 overs at less than three runs per over.

The 39-year-old had a more worn pitch to utilise than South Africa's spinners and found significantly more turn and threat.

He also had the sprawling Steve Smith to his advantage.

Both of Smith's catches off Lyon, first to dismiss Temba Bavuma and then Kyle Verreynne, were feats of anticipation. He saw both right-handers shape to reverse sweep, gambled and clung on at close range. The first was good. The one-handed second was spectacular.

In between, Smith's leaping catch at second slip after Cummins found Bedingham's edge took the 37-year-old back above Joe Root as the non-wicketkeeper with the most catches in Test history on 223.

While he ended the day with three more catches than Root, he still has a catch percentage about 77%, which sits below the format average.

He creates, and occasionally drops, chances such as these - chances others would not have created.

The result is Australia's fabled foursome now have 607 wickets in Tests in which they have played as a quartet.

The next most successful bowling four-pronged attack is James Anderson, Stuart Broad, Ben Stokes and Moeen Ali, who took 415 wickets in their 31 Tests together for England.

Much has been made of Australia's ageing side and a perceived lack of succession planning.

At 37, Starc is the oldest of the three quicks but his average pace of 141.21km/h in 2026 is higher than any of his past three years. He is also averaging his most swing in a calendar year since 2015.

The concern for Australia comes when they are not fit, with Hazlewood having missed all five of last winter's Ashes Tests and Cummins four.

Australia's issue right now is keeping each of their quartet on the field, because they appear as good as ever.

At 33-0, Australia lead South Africa by 139 runs.

Even with bad light halting play early again, they should have the time to press home an advantage across the Test's final two days.

Notifications, social media and more with BBC Sport

title: Next steps in the Cornell sexual assault case — and the challenges that lie ahead
description:
New York Gov. Kathy Hochul has tapped Attorney General Letitia James (right) to be the special prosecutor in the Cornell University sexual assault case. They attended a press conference on October 2 in New York. - NDZ/STAR MAX/IPx/AP
When New York Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed Attorney General Letitia James to take over the investigation into an alleged gang rape at a fraternity house at Cornell University, she asked for a “fresh and thorough” review of all the evidence.
fullText:
When New York Gov. Kathy Hochul appointed Attorney General Letitia James to take over the investigation into an alleged gang rape at a fraternity house at Cornell University, she asked for a “fresh and thorough” review of all the evidence.

And there is a lot of evidence.

Far from the two-party “he said-she said” structure of many sexual assault allegations, the Cornell case features seven men accused of wrongdoing in a civil suit filed by the woman known as Jane Doe. There are interviews with Doe, the accused men and other witnesses; scores of texts and Snapchat posts; secretly recorded phone calls; and lengthy, conflicting reports from the police, district attorney and university investigators about who knew what when.

In all, it’s a far cry from the limited evidence the local prosecutor said he reviewed before deciding not to bring charges in 2024.

Putting the array of evidence together represents the primary task ahead for James, the special prosecutor tasked with leading the investigation and considering whether to bring charges. How the investigation proceeds will be closely watched by community members, university students and advocacy groups across the country.

“There is literally an avalanche of statements to collect in this case that apparently were not reviewed by the original prosecutor,” said Paul DerOhannesian, an Albany-based attorney and author of “Sexual Assault Trials.”

“Getting all those statements is a big task,” he said.

Mimi Rocah, former Westchester County district attorney and former federal prosecutor, likened the work ahead to “putting the pieces of the puzzle together.”

Hochul laid out the questions James will try to answer in a news conference on October 2.

“Attorney General James will be the one who puts a spotlight on this case and says, ‘Who knew what when?’ ‘What did they do wrong?’ ‘Why didn’t they come forward?’ and ‘How was this woman denied justice?’ and we anticipate that will come out over the right period of time,” Hochul said.

For James, the investigation faces several key challenges ahead, including the potential loss of evidence two years after the fact, questions about her potential bias, a supposed “loophole” in New York’s sexual assault law and intense pressure from the community.

The most important job of a special prosecutor, Rocah said, is “to try to conduct a fair process and really convey that to the public and be transparent at the end of the day about what you did and why you did it.”

At the news conference, James laid out her next steps as special prosecutor.

“Every New Yorker deserves to know that when they report a crime, it will be investigated fully and fairly. That they will be seen and heard,” she said. “We will review the facts, gather evidence, interview witnesses and, if warranted, pursue prosecutions.”

Much of the evidence may already exist. Notably, Cornell held its own formal Title IX investigation, the federal civil rights law banning discrimination based on gender – which includes sexual harassment and violence.

The investigation included more than 50 interviews, including with all of the men accused of wrongdoing, except one who declined to be interviewed, according to a heavily redacted 99-page document summarizing the panel’s findings. CNN has not seen the Title IX filings, which are generally confidential and restricted to the parties involved.

Separately, Cornell is reviewing its own response to the sexual assault allegations. This review, led by former US Deputy Attorney General Sally Q. Yates, will examine how Cornell “prevents and responds to sexual harassment, sexual assault and related misconduct on campus,” the university said.

Still, James will have the opportunity to reinterview certain witnesses rather than simply relying on previous evidence.

DerOhannesian said James will have a few extra tools at her disposal in this investigation. She could try to cut a deal with some of the accused, offering leniency or immunity in exchange for their testimony. Or she could try to look for evidence of process crimes, such as obstruction of justice or lying to investigators, if the evidence allows.

Her role here as special prosecutor is not so different from how prosecutors may reexamine cases started by their predecessors.

“That is not uncommon for people in decision-making positions to have to take a look at past investigations and past decisions,” Rocah said.

With so much ahead, the investigation is likely to take a while, DerOhannesian said.

“Because of the quantity of information that has to be processed, the multiple legal questions that have to be answered for multiple individuals, I think it’s gonna take a lot of time,” he said. “That may be frustrating to the community, that it will be taking time to get these answers.”

The office has reached out to several experienced attorneys to bolster its team, CNN reported Tuesday.

The attorney general’s office, known as OAG, “has spoken with the Tompkins County District Attorney, Jane Doe’s attorney, and several candidates for outside counsel to support the investigation. The DA has agreed to cooperate, and OAG remains committed to a thorough and independent investigation guided only by the facts and the law,” a spokesperson for James said in a statement.

Once the investigation is complete, James likely will either take her findings to a grand jury or issue a report explaining why she does not recommend charges.

One challenge for James is some evidence may have been lost in the two years since the October 2024 encounter. Memories may have faded, or digital evidence could have been lost or deleted.

“There are real challenges looking at something several years after it happened,” Rocah said.

Doe’s attorney, Thomas Giuffra, said her rape kit was conducted weeks after the incident rather than immediately afterward, potentially losing some DNA evidence. He also speculated that photos and videos of the incident may have been lost or deleted due to the failures of the original investigation.

“I mean, if this was a normal investigation that was done in New York City, for example, they would have gotten search warrants,” Giuffra told CNN’s Jake Tapper on Monday. They would have grabbed every single one of these phones of these guys. They would have downloaded all this material.

Another challenge for James is convincing the public to trust her independence and judgment. Late last month, she posted about Doe’s case, calling her a “survivor” and declaring, “We stand with you.” Days later, at the news conference announcing her appointment as special prosecutor, she declined to comment on the post.

Andrew Miltenberg, a lawyer for one of the seven former fraternity members, on Monday called for James to recuse herself from the case, saying her statements “could reasonably be understood as accepting that the alleged conduct occurred before she assumed responsibility for determining what the evidence establishes.”

Finally, any criminal charges would have to follow New York’s law defining sex crimes and lack of consent. In particular, lack of consent can result from being involuntarily “mentally incapacitated” by drugs or alcohol. But if someone voluntarily takes drugs or alcohol, they can’t be considered mentally incapacitated – an exclusion critics have called a “loophole.”

In Doe’s case, she has said she drank alcohol and took drugs that night. She also told police she was OK with an initial encounter but said she did not consent to sexual contact later in the night, according to a six-page statement obtained by CNN.

Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten cited this law and Doe’s alcohol and drug use in defending his decision not to charge the accused fraternity members. However, he acknowledged he did not see all the evidence in the case before coming to that conclusion.

Giuffra said Doe’s reactions to the incident were a “textbook reaction to trauma.”

“Ms. Doe’s internal processing went from denial to shame and ultimately acceptance that she had been raped by people that she thought were her friends,” Giuffra told CNN Thursday.

This aspect of New York law will make bringing charges a “tough climb” for prosecutors, said CNN senior legal analyst Elie Honig.

Still, investigators could bring charges here under different theories, legal experts said. Even when someone consumes drugs or alcohol, they still may not be able to consent, or they could offer consent at one time and revoke it later, DerOhannesian said.

It all depends on the specific facts of the case, Rocah said.

“It makes a case under facts like this more challenging, but not impossible,” she said.

CNN’s Kara Scannell contributed to this report.

title: Republicans want Abdul El-Sayed to be the main character of the midterms. He's on board.
description:
PORT HURON, Mich. (AP) — Abdul El-Sayed, holding a handheld mic and wearing his signature V-neck black shirt, slowly shook his head as a woman at his town hall described how she burned through her savings after undergoing emergency brain surgery.
“I’m really sorry for your experience, and I hope that you’re on the mend,” said El-Sayed, the Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate in Michigan, after outlining proposals for guaranteed health care and paid leave.
fullText:
PORT HURON, Mich. (AP) — Abdul El-Sayed, holding a handheld mic and wearing his signature V-neck black shirt, slowly shook his head as a woman at his town hall described how she burned through her savings after undergoing emergency brain surgery.

"I'm really sorry for your experience, and I hope that you're on the mend," said El-Sayed, the Democratic candidate for U.S. Senate in Michigan, after outlining proposals for guaranteed health care and paid leave.

Later that night, while talking to reporters in the basement below the theatre, his tone was far different. El-Sayed called his Republican opponent Mike Rogers a "coward," said President Donald Trump was "afraid" to visit the state and dismissed as "dumb" a question about whether Iran or Israel posed a greater threat to the United States.

The exchanges captured two sides of a candidate who is the central figure in one of the nation's most consequential Senate races. El-Sayed would be the country's first Muslim senator, and he's crisscrossing the state to counter a Republican effort, fueled by tens of millions of dollars, to portray him as a dangerous radical. But he has also embraced his confrontational side by mocking and taunting Trump and Rogers.

"If they want to make me the main character in the midterms, I'm not shying away from it," El-Sayed said in an interview. "Run against me. See how well that works out for you."

El-Sayed's brash, swaggering confidence rubbed some Democrats the wrong way during a divisive primary against Rep. Haley Stevens. The former public health official has shown little interest in toning it down, remaining unapologetic about his progressive agenda and adversarial approach, emboldening supporters who believe he's the right candidate for an angry electorate that has lost faith in the political establishment.

But his doubters fear he'll cost Democrats control of the Senate by failing to unite his party's disparate factions ahead of November.

"If you want their votes, you have to make nice with those people, and he's not really doing that," said Michigan political strategist Adrian Hemond, who supported Stevens. "Maybe he doesn't have to. The entire theory of this candidacy has been he can remake what the electorate looks like."

Even though Michigan backed Trump twice in his three presidential campaigns, no Republican has won a Senate race in the state since 1994.

The political landscape is no friendlier this year. Trump started an unpopular war with Iran, leading to higher gas prices. Rogers has opted for a low-key campaign with fewer public events than El-Sayed as he tries to make the race all about his Democratic opponent.

As of Oct. 10, Republicans had outspent Democrats by $78 million to $63 million in the Michigan Senate race, according to AdImpact, which tracks political advertising. Around $40 million in Republican spending has gone toward negative advertisements, compared to only around $20 million from Democrats.

The ads portray El-Sayed as "dangerously radical" and "too extreme," highlighting his past calls to defund the police and relax immigration enforcement. Others tie him to Hasan Piker, a popular online streamer with whom El-Sayed has appeared and who has drawn criticism for past comments, including saying that "America deserved 9/11."

On Friday, Rogers appeared alongside Louisiana Sen. John Kennedy, who told reporters that El-Sayed "sleeps in a Bin Laden jersey." Rogers laughed.

Vice President JD Vance has called him "evil." In one social media post, Trump shared a photo of himself with first lady Melania Trump alongside a photo of El-Sayed and his wife, who wears a hijab, with the caption: "Two VERY DIFFERENT America's."

Late Wednesday, Trump referred to El-Sayed as "Mohammed" and said he "goes back to the days of the Jihad."

El-Sayed has hardly backed down. At the campaign stop in Port Huron, he taunted Trump to visit Michigan, suggesting Rogers and other Republicans were afraid the president would hurt their chances.

"Donald, if you're watching, don't wuss out, man," El-Sayed said.

And he responded to Kennedy's attack by suggesting the Republican is in the KKK.

"That's rich coming from someone who wears his bed sheets out at night," El-Sayed posted on social media.

Before the Port Huron town hall, El-Sayed worked his way down a line of people who couldn't fit inside the theater, shaking hands, taking photos and stopping for conversations.

Jeff Petrucella and his wife Alice traveled from Macomb County to see El-Sayed. They described themselves as politically "middle of the road" and said they had voted Republican in the past.

"I'm pretty done with the Republicans right now," Jeff said.

Alice said she was "looking for a change that is better for my granddaughters," pointing to El-Sayed's support for Medicare for All. Nor was she put off by his more confrontational appearances on Fox News.

"I think he expresses himself well. You can tell he's a well-spoken, educated man," she said.

Pat Kreiner was among those who waited nearly an hour to see El-Sayed. Her children had persuaded her to support him in the Democratic primary.

"My son said to me, 'I have been living with this trickle-down economy since the day I was born,'" Kreiner said. "'It doesn't work for me.'"

Kreiner also expressed anger about Trump's trade war with Canada, just across the river from Port Huron.

"We are heartsick about our neighbors," she said. "They used to come over a lot. We don't see them now."

Visiting smaller towns such as Port Huron has become central to El-Sayed's campaign, with his team recently saying he's held more than 500 events in over 100 cities across the state.

"Go everywhere. Talk to everyone. That's what we do," El-Sayed said in an interview.

The personal approach has not erased all the skepticism surrounding El-Sayed, including within his own party.

His criticism of Israel and association with Piker have raised concerns among some Jewish Democrats. El-Sayed has held a series of private gatherings with undecided Jewish voters as he works to win their support.

He has also sought to strengthen his standing with Black voters. In the Democratic primary, Stevens drew more support in Wayne County, home to Detroit and its large Black population.

Ahead of Thursday's debate, El-Sayed attended two events with Black leaders before stopping at a Black barbershop, where he moved from chair to chair talking with customers. He stopped at one point to speak with a pregnant woman, congratulating her and asking when her baby was due.

"November 8th?" El-Sayed joked. "Make sure you vote early, huh?"

While El-Sayed has spent much of his campaign trying to win over Michigan voters, his candidacy has taken on significance far beyond the state. Republicans have made him a symbol of what they warn is an increasingly radical Democratic Party, while progressives see his campaign as a chance to prove their politics can win in a closely divided state.

At a New York City fundraiser on Oct. 5, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez cast his campaign as a test for progressives nationwide.

"If Abdul can win in Michigan, anybody can win anywhere," said the New York Democrat, a potential presidential candidate.

Ocasio-Cortez plans to campaign with El-Sayed in Michigan next week, followed by former President Barack Obama on Oct. 24.

The national stakes have also drawn renewed opposition. United Democracy Project, a super PAC affiliated with AIPAC, disclosed an initial $94,000 expenditure against El-Sayed on Friday, after spending nearly $30 million to oppose him in the Democratic primary.

And El-Sayed, despite insisting the election should focus on Michigan voters and their economic struggles, has embraced the larger implications of his candidacy.

"I am grateful for your support," he told the audience at the New York fundraiser, according to remarks obtained by The Associated Press. He said he had two goals — "pick up a U.S. Senate seat" and "change the nature of our politics for the better."

title: Ukraine pushes back on Trump's call for a new president as drones hit Russian data hub
description:
— U.S. President Donald Trump said Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an “energy ceasefire,” but offered no details on its terms.
Trump’s brief social media post said only that the ceasefire took effect immediately, adding: “Do not break it!”
Moscow did not immediately comment on the announcement, and the White House did not clarify the president’s post.
fullText:
WASHINGTON (AP) — U.S. President Donald Trump said Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an "energy ceasefire," but offered no details on its terms.

Trump's brief social media post said only that the ceasefire took effect immediately, adding: "Do not break it!"

Moscow did not immediately comment on the announcement, and the White House did not clarify the president's post.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on X: "We discussed the energy ceasefire announced by President Trump. Ukraine supports the ceasefire, and it is important that Russia support it as well. We are awaiting details from the American side."

Zelenskyy added that he had spoken with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Finnish President Alexander Stubb and NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte.

In an interview broadcast Sunday, Zelenskyy said Ukraine was ready to stop striking Russian refineries if Moscow halted attacks on Ukraine's energy system, and asked Trump to press the Kremlin to agree.

"We are asking President Trump, (to) give them (a) signal, not (to) attack energy infrastructure of Ukraine," he told ABC's "This Week."

Trump said Saturday it was time for Ukraine to get a new president, suggesting Zelenskyy has not done enough to end the war and blaming him for high diesel prices in the U.S.

Zelenskyy said in response to Trump's comments that Ukraine could hold elections if Russia agreed to a 60-day ceasefire.

"Give us two months, 60 days off. Total ceasefire, 60 days, and we will organize elections," he said, adding that Ukraine would be ready to accept whatever choice its people made.

"With all respect to President Trump, it's up to our society, up to our people to choose one or another leader," he said. Zelenskyy added that holding a vote during the war would be unlawful and that Ukraine would need security guarantees to allow people to vote safely.

Ukraine has been under martial law since Russian President Vladimir Putin launched the full-scale invasion in February 2022, and the Ukrainian Constitution bars elections while it remains in force. Beyond the legal barrier, a nationwide vote would be vulnerable to Russian attacks, and organizing one is widely seen as logistically impossible, with roughly a fifth of the country held by Russia, millions of Ukrainians displaced abroad and soldiers on the front line. Zelenskyy's term formally expired in May 2024, but the constitution allows him to remain in office until a new president is sworn in.

The exchange came as Kyiv pressed its campaign against infrastructure deep inside Russia, with a drone attack on Sunday shutting down a data center in the city of Vladimir, east of Moscow, run by technology giant Yandex. It was the third strike on the company's facilities in four days.

Russia and Ukraine have been locked in a long-range aerial war while their armies remain largely deadlocked on the front line.

Trump, who on Friday struck a deal with Putin to buy diesel from Moscow in an attempt to address high fuel prices ahead of U.S. midterm elections, has been urging Zelenskyy for weeks to stop strikes on Russian energy infrastructure.

He has sought to blame record U.S. diesel prices on Ukraine rather than the U.S.-led war in Iran, which has driven up world energy prices. Ukrainian and European officials reacted to the diesel deal with dismay, saying it will help pay for Russia's war effort.

The Ukrainian drone attack on the Yandex data center in Vladimir caused outages across the company's services, leaving users in dozens of Russian cities and in Kazakhstan, Belarus and Armenia unable to order taxis or access banking services, according to Russian independent news outlet Astra.

"Operations at the data center have been completely halted. There were no injuries," said the Yandex Cloud Telegram channel, which provides operational updates on service availability.

Moscow residents described disruption to everyday tasks. Pavel Belyavskiy, a driver for Yandex Taxi, said it was unclear whether orders were coming through at all, and that on several rides he had to cancel after waiting a long time because he could not reach the passenger.

"I'd press the 'call' button to contact them, but nothing happens," he said, "There's nothing I can do, so I'm just forced to cancel."

Igor Mann said he went to check on an order on the Yandex Market shopping platform but the page was unavailable, and connecting through a virtual private network did not help. "Nothing worked," he said.

Another Muscovite, Eduard Malyavko, said the outages had "direct impact" and weren't just about "convenience."

"It's also about work," he said, adding that the outages also affected "healthcare, and everything else."

On Thursday, a drone attack took a Yandex data center offline in the Ryazan region, southeast of Moscow. The next day, Ukrainian drones hit the company's major data center in the Kaluga region, southwest of Moscow, disabling part of the facilty, Yandex said.

Yandex, often described as Russia's Google, runs the country's most popular search engine and a wide range of digital services, and is heavily involved in Russia's artificial intelligence development.

Elsewhere, search and rescue operations ended in the southern city of Zaporizhzhia after a Russian bombing on Saturday, according to Ivan Fedorov, former regional head and co-chair of the regional defense council.

Zelenskyy said 23 people were killed in the attack, including four children. More than 30 people were wounded, Fedorov said, with eight still hospitalized.

A man was killed and two women wounded in a Ukrainian drone strike on Russia's Bryansk border region, local officials said Sunday.

Blann reported from Kyiv, Ukraine, and Morton reported from London.

Follow the AP's coverage of the war in Ukraine at https://apnews.com/hub/russia-ukraine

title: Trump weighs joining Saudi strikes as Riyadh airport is hit for a second straight day
description:
— A projectile struck a passenger terminal at the international airport in Riyadh on Sunday, a day after a missile hit the same terminal and killed 12 people, the Saudi-led coalition fighting Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen said. The Houthis claimed responsibility for those attacks and others.
Saudi authorities said there were injuries in the latest attack on the King Khalid International Airport complex for terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights. Saturday’s missile attack was the deadliest in a Gulf Arab nation since the Iran war began, with another 300 people wounded, some critically. The airport was still closed Sunday.
fullText:
CAIRO (AP) — A projectile struck a passenger terminal at the international airport in Riyadh on Sunday, a day after a missile hit the same terminal and killed 12 people, the Saudi-led coalition fighting Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen said. The Houthis claimed responsibility for those attacks and others.

Saudi authorities said there were injuries in the latest attack on the King Khalid International Airport complex for terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights. Saturday's missile attack was the deadliest in a Gulf Arab nation since the Iran war began, with another 300 people wounded, some critically. The airport was still closed Sunday.

The sharp escalation in the new front in the war threatens to draw in greater U.S. military involvement, as President Donald Trump has said he is weighing joining the fight against the Houthis. There was no immediate White House comment Sunday.

The latest strike in Riyadh came shortly after the Houthis said the airport in the rebel-held Yemeni capital of Sanaa had been struck again, and blamed the Saudis.

At stake, again, in this escalation are global supplies and prices of oil as well as commercial shipping through a crucial alternative waterway to the Iran-threatened Strait of Hormuz — along with civilians and aviation throughout the region.

Trump on Saturday also said he planned to speak with Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who has been seeking assistance.

A U.S. intervention could prompt the Houthis to halt shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the southern end of the Red Sea off Yemen and further restrict the flow of oil out of the Persian Gulf. The rebels seized key areas along the strait last month and the Saudi-led coalition has been trying to seize them back.

Saudi Arabia is running low on missile interceptors and has asked France, Britain, Pakistan and Egypt to deploy air defense support to the region, regional officials told The Associated Press last month, with one noting that the U.S. has seen its own stock dwindle during the war with Iran.

Sunday's attack occurred as the Saudis hosted a major international energy conference in Riyadh, with other high-profile events including an investment gathering on the horizon. Saudi Arabia under Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has sought to open more to the world as a business and tourism destination, but the Houthi attacks threaten those efforts.

"There is no way that somebody will break our back. We are like a phoenix, we come out of the ashes all the time," the Saudi energy minister, Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman Al Saud, told the conference.

He added that the kingdom is also working on pipelines in addition to the East-West one that was attacked and closed for days last month, with no details.

Earlier Sunday, the Houthi-run health ministry said a child was killed and six people wounded in a suspected Saudi airstrike on a house in Sanaa. The ministry also said 91 Yemenis have been killed by the Saudi-led coalition in five weeks, 60% of them women and children.

There was no immediate comment from Saudi authorities on the claims.

On Sunday, the Houthis also claimed attacks on King Fahd Airport in the city of Damma, as well as oil and gas facilities in the kingdom's east. They have targeted the Riyadh airport, which has no military facilities, every day since Wednesday.

The rebels again warned "all airlines, experts, employees, workers and ​travelers against using Saudi airports and airspace, as they are vulnerable to attack and have become a theater of operations for our ​forces." Several international airlines have suspended flights for varying periods.

Brig. Gen. Yahya Saree, the group's military spokesperson, wrote on X that airports in the holy cities of Mecca and Medina, however, were exempt. The kingdom earlier called Mecca a "red line."

A Saudi statement said the dead in Saturday's attack included four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a U.S. citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese.

The Egyptian woman was a flight attendant identified as Azza Ramzy, who worked for Saudi airline Flynas, according to Egyptian state-run TV.

The Syrian woman was a widowed mother of four who had been living in Saudi Arabia for five years, relative Nisreen Oweida told The Associated Press. The Syrian Embassy identified her as Buthaina Ahmad Oweida.

Until recently, the Houthis had been largely on the sidelines of the Iran war, but they have developed their military capabilities in recent years to become one of Tehran's most powerful allies. Now, the rebels are helping Iran to pressure a key U.S. ally.

The Saudis and the Houthis began fighting in 2015, when the kingdom entered Yemen's civil war on behalf of the internationally recognized government. Relative calm after a 2022 ceasefire ended in July when the Houthis resumed attacks, saying the Saudis fired on the Sanaa airport as a plane from Iran was trying to land.

That revived anger over the Saudi-led blockade that has largely isolated Houthi-run areas. The Houthis say they have now imposed a blockade on Saudi Arabia.

Fighting has escalated, with the Saudi-led coalition providing air support for Yemeni government forces attempting to reverse recent Houthi gains near the Bab el-Mandeb, a crucial alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has been attacking ships.

But Ahmed Nagi, the International Crisis Group's senior analyst for Yemen, said the Houthi pressure tactics could backfire. "Rather than pushing Riyadh to step back, attacks on critical Saudi infrastructure could make the Saudis more determined to continue the campaign," he said.

A previous version of this report has been corrected to show that the Egyptian killed in the strike was a woman, not a man.

Frankel and Anna reported from Jerusalem. Associated Press writers Victoria Eastwood in Cairo, Collin Binkley in Washington, Sally Abou AlJoud in Beirut and Omar Albam in Maarat al-Numan, Syria, contributed to this report.

title: Former NFL star drops bombshell on why Josh McDaniels was really fired by Las Vegas Raiders
description: Former Las Vegas Raiders guard Richie Incognito revealed the truth behind the firing of Josh McDaniels as their head coach. This comes after his initial statement on McDaniels’ tenure as the Raiders’ HC, where he won only 9 out of the 25 games in charge.
fullText:
Former Las Vegas Raiders guard Richie Incognito revealed the truth behind the firing of Josh McDaniels as their head coach.

This comes after his initial statement on McDaniels' tenure as the Raiders' HC, where he won only 9 out of the 25 games in charge. Incognito was not part of the team when McDaniels took over, but he believes the players could use the upcoming matchup as motivation to prove a point to their former HC.

"What Josh McDaniels did to this team for two years. He disrespected everybody on this team. He alienated everybody on this team. He lorded over them.

"Yeah, Josh you're a great offensive coordinator, but you will never work outside New England… Those boys have stories from McDaniels that would blow people's minds how bad he treated this team and the ultimate sign of disrespect is we don't even talk about it," said Incognito on the Initial Contact podcast.

However, his comments did not sit well with Jerry Thornton, who is a New England Patriots writer with Barstool Sports.

The Raiders job was McDaniels' second stint as HC and there were a lot of expectations on him due to all the success he had with the Patriots. In 2009, the Denver Broncos also gave him the HC job, but he only lasted 28 games with them before losing his job.

Incognito explained why the Patriots OC failed to keep his job in Las Vegas in response to Thornton's push back.

"No, they fired him because he was a d***** who alienated his entire locker room and ran the team into the ground. Did the same thing in Denver. Two failed head coaching stints, two fractured locker rooms, and every time he goes crawling back to Foxborough. Funny how the Patriot Way never seems to work outside New England," Incognito posted on X.

Incognito's co-host, Christian Fauria, engaged in a social media back-and-forth with him and pointed the blame at the Raiders' ownership. However, the former Pro Bowler was not going to agree with Fauria.

It is unclear if Incognito had a conversation with McDaniels before he announced his retirement in 2022.

His Raiders will play against McDaniels' Patriots on Sunday. Going into the game, Klint Kubiak's team has a 3-1 record and will be hoping to improve on that against a Patriots side that has looked lacklustre this season.

title: Scottish FA Make Official Motherwell vs Celtic Announcement
description: The Scottish FA have made an official announcement regarding the game between Motherwell and Celtic.
fullText:
Celtic will return to action following a three-week international break when they take on Motherwell away from home. With the Rangers already winning this weekend, the pressure is on Martin O'Neill's side to produce a positive result to remain atop the Premiership table at the end of this matchday.

That is easier said than done though, especially for a Celtic side that is completely out of form and clearly short of confidence.

They went into the international break on the back of a three-game losing streak. Even losing once is often considered a crisis at a club like Celtic.

So, I do not need to tell you what losing thrice on the treat means, even more so when two of them came against the Rangers.

So, a win against Motherwell will go a long way in restoring some confidence in this team. But if they fail to take home all three points again, that would only intensify the questions around the club as a whole.

The Scottish FA have announced the officials for the upcoming game between Motherwell and Celtic. Steven McLean has been named the referee. Jonathan Bell and Ross Wilson will be the two assistants.

Don Robertson is set to be the one on VAR duty and he will be assisted by Calum Scott. George Calder will be the fourth official.

Obviously, the officials often end up becoming a topic of discussion in Scottish football. One would hope that no bad decisions are made in this game which end up having an impact on the overall result.

Good News Confirmed for Celtic Before Facing MotherwellCeltic have been handed some good news ahead of their game against Motherwell.

Celtic will be looking to get a win against Motherwell this weekend. There is no doubt about that. That is very much the minimum expectation from O'Neill's side.

When you consider how poorly the Rangers had started off this campaign, it is remarkable that they could be top of the table by the end of this weekend.

But that just goes to show how bad Celtic have been as well. Unfortunately, this has been the running theme of things for the past few years now.

It is not just on the players or the coaching staff, but on how the club has been run, consistently weakening the squad every summer by allowing key players to leave, sometimes inexplicably, and then failing to replace them with those of similar or better quality.

title: Truro stay fourth after win over Braintree Town
description: Truro City deserved to score more goals in their 2-1 win at Braintree Town, says assistant manager Stewart Yetton.
fullText:
Truro City deserved to score more goals in their 2-1 win at Braintree Town, according to assistant manager Stewart Yetton.

The Tinners found themselves a goal down after eight minutes at National League South's fourth-bottom side after Courtney Senior turned in an eighth-minute cross.

Jack Stretton and Luke Jephcott had good chances to equalise before Max Kinsey drew the Cornish side level as he headed home a corner midway through the first half.

Stretton and Jephcott had more chances before Will Dean got his third goal of the season early in the second half as the visitors hung on to secure the win.

Truro's second win in three games keeps them fourth in the division, one point off league leaders Maidstone United.

"I think we were good value for the win," Yetton told BBC Radio Cornwall.

"It wasn't pretty in the last 20 minutes. They obviously were kind of spoiling a lot, a lot of fouls and we kind of got suckered in a little bit to that - a few of their boys and our boys are going at it off the ball and it gets a little bit scrappy.

"But I'm pleased to come away with the win. I think that's the most important thing. We had enough chances I think, first half, to probably be a couple more ahead."

title: Official Lazio Squad vs Monza: Three Midfielders Return, Four Players Out
description: Ahead of Sunday’s contest against Monza, Lazio have released their matchday squad, and it includes three returning players.Lazio to Host Monza on SundayThe Biancocelesti will be looking to extend th...
fullText:
Ahead of Sunday's contest against Monza, Lazio have released their matchday squad, and it includes three returning players.

The Biancocelesti will be looking to extend their purple patch and keep pace with Inter Milan and Roma when they host the newly-promoted side at a virtually empty Stadio Olimpico. The game kicks off at 15:00 local time.

Luckily for Gennaro Gattuso, the midfield emergency is seemingly over, with three players returning from injury to bolster the department. The first is Fisayo Dele-Bashiru, who has been out after picking up a muscle injury on the opening day of the season in Bologna. The Nigerian international already featured in last weekend's friendly test against Juve Stabia.

Danilo Catlaldi has also recovered from groin surgery and a few other setbacks to make himself available at the manager's disposal. The experienced Lazio stalwart will add depth to the midfield department, as will 19-year-old Adrian Przyborek, who also recovered from a slight knock.

Despite the triple boost, the midfield is still lacking Nicolo Rovella's influential presence. The 24-year-old is aiming to return next weekend against his former employers, Juventus. The same goes for Adam Marusic and Matteo Cancellieri, while Albert Gudmundsson could be facing a longer spell on the sidelines after dislocating his shoulder during Iceland's game against Estonia.

Albert Gudmundsson and Mario Gila (Photo by Marco Rosi – SS Lazio/Getty Images)

Lazio also remain without their third-choice goalkeeper Alessio Furlanetto, who tore his ACL at the end of last season, and could remain out until spring.

Goalkeepers: Mandas, Motta, Renzetti.

Defenders: Doekhi, Floriani M., Lazzari, Leite, Pedraza, Provstgaard, Šutalo, Tavares.

Midfielders: Belahyane, Cataldi, Dele-Bashiru, Farcomeni, Frattesi, Przyborek, Taylor.

Forwards: Isaksen, Noslin, Pinamonti, Serra, Zaccagni.

title: Colts vs. Steelers: 3 things to know, plus a prediction
description: Here are three things to know about the Colts vs. Steelers matchup, along with a game prediction.
fullText:
Next up for the Indianapolis Colts is a road matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Both teams will enter this game at 2-2, however, the Colts are coming off back-to-back wins, while the Steelers lost their last game.

As part of our matchup preview, here are three things to know, plus a prediction.

The Steelers had a few extra days of rest and time to prepare for this matchup. While the Colts played last Sunday, the Steelers' previous game came on Thursday of Week 4. In addition to that, the Colts also had to travel to London and are again on the road this week, playing in Pittsburgh.

Not only is Indianapolis lacking explosive passing plays, but without a deep threat on the field, opponents are able to defend the Colts more aggressively, shrinking the field by playing closer to the line of scrimmage, which makes moving the ball on short- to intermediate routes more difficult as well.

As good as the Colts run game can be, finding consistent success without a passing game that can consistently help shoulder the workload won't come easily. The Steelers are allowign 7.4 yards per pass attempt this season, which ranks 23rd in the NFL.

title: Sunderland 0-2 Brighton Player Ratings and Fan Reaction
description: Ferdi Kadioglu dominates and Yasin Ayari shines as the Seagulls return from the break in style. Discover who dazzled and who struggled in this comprehensive individual performance breakdown.
fullText:
Brighton and Hove Albion were immediately back to winning ways after the extended international break, with a stunning 2-0 victory against Sunderland.

It is now the morning (just about afternoon) after, which means it is time to take a look through the players individually and see who stood out the most...

The Dutchman had some important tests, including multiple long-range efforts from Sunderland forwards.

While he wasn't tested to the highest degree, once again, he delivered when called upon. Verbruggen is slowly becoming the goalkeeper that every Brighton fan has wished for over the years! Stable.

A monsterous performance from last season's best player. The Turkish full back was electric, up and down his flank and even inverting into midfield.

Kadioglu hasn't started the season the best, but he paid everyone's faith back with a fantastic defensive and offensive performance yesterday. Back to his best.

Despite a shaky first half, Vuskovic grew into the game. The teenage centre-back put his body on the line on many occasions and won his aerial duels remarkably well again.

The Croatian has stepped up his maturity and showed it well after Pascal Struijk's sending off.

Struijk wasn't actually bad until he was sent off, and particularly in the first half, he was the better of the two centre-backs.

However, the red does lower his rating somewhat, but he had a fairly steady game beyond that. Yes, I do think it was a red card.

A rating that could feel harsh, but from my view, it felt like a game that Boscagli struggled in. The game seemed to change after Hadjam and Yalcouyé were introduced.

While his passing is solid, the Monacan often struggles to keep up with the physical opponents, especially with away trips.

Calm, composed, and becoming stronger on and off the ball. Andrés may not have stood out as much as his full debut game against Arsenal last time out, but the Spaniard is everything that Albion have been looking for regarding a presence in midfield.

One of the best players on the pitch by some margin. The Swede seems to keep improving his overall game, and yesterday he simply didn't stop running and pressuring for duels.

While he was previously viewed as a more technical but lightweight midfielder, Ayari is becoming more and more complete as the season progresses.

Is he getting... better? Groß just seems to be the most timeless asset amongst the Albion squad. Since returning from Borussia Dortmund, there really hasn't been anyone close to the class and quality of the Seagulls legend.

Another excellently weighted assist, and overall fantastic performance. Even at 35, he created chances and covered a silly amount of ground.

Another excellent performance from Gomez. The Paraguayan is one of the club's hardest workers, and while he may not be the most technically gifted, he has everything Hürzeler needs in his squad.

Energy, work ethic, and tenacity. Gomez was key to Albion's win yesterday.

Not much to say for our Greek forward, who was unfortunately sacrificed after Struijk's red card.

A FORWARD, not a left-back. De Cuyper has shown how lethal he can be in front of goal this season. Energetic and a magnificent box crasher. It is no mistake that he keeps popping up with goals this season.

Georginio was on the pitch for a matter of minutes but influenced the game perfectly well. He threaded a great pass through to Hadjam and staked a claim to return to the Albion starting side.

Plus, some bonus points for his celebrations. Who couldn't love Georgi?

A very happy welcome to the club to our full-back. The Algerian finished off a swift counter-attacking move with thanks to Georginio and Groß.

Hadjam may have been on the pitch for a short period of time, but what a moment for him!

The Portuguese defender had little to do, but perhaps looked a little more unsure than some of the other substitutions. With that said, he contributed towards one of the all-time Brighton defensive performances in the Premier League era under Hürzeler.

Coming into a game during a moment of high magnitude and pulling off an effortless defensive display like he did yesterday proved everything about why Dunk is still our best defender.

From his blocks to composure on the ball, Dunk added maturity in a moment of adversity, and that deserves immeasurable credit.

My unpopular opinion is that without Yalcouyé, maybe Albion wouldn't have won this game. Despite the impressive low blocking from the Albion defence, the Malian added an espresso shot of excitement to the Albion midfield.

Perhaps Sunderland were not expecting to be chased down from every angle, but Yalcouyé broke up the play to carve out more opportunities for the Seagulls than expected, which earned him a high rating.

title: Manchester City Starting XI vs Liverpool: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
description: Manchester City Predicted XI vs Liverpool as Erling Haaland Returns for Anfield TestManchester City head to Anfield with the biggest team news centred on Erling Haaland, and the answer is simple. He i...
fullText:
Manchester City head to Anfield with the biggest team news centred on Erling Haaland, and the answer is simple. He is fit, available and expected to start against Liverpool.

Enzo Maresca had a concern after Haaland limped off during Norway duty, but it has not developed into anything serious. The update from the City boss was clear: "He's good. He went to Marbella, had two or three days off, played golf. Had some recovery. He's ready for Anfield." He added, "He's good, the players are thinking: international teams, some days off and go again. He was good."

That matters. Haaland remains the reference point in this Manchester City attack and his record in big games means there was never going to be much appetite for caution if he was anywhere near full fitness. He also has history in this fixture after scoring a stoppage-time penalty winner away at Liverpool last season.

Antoine Semenyo is also expected to be involved from the start. There has been no formal declaration on his condition, but training on Thursday strongly indicated that the issue which forced him to withdraw from Ghana duty has eased. Barring a late setback, he should keep his place.

That leaves the final attacking spot as a real selection call. Jeremy Doku is fit again and pushing hard to start, which puts Iliman N'Diaye under pressure. Doku brings more direct running, more chaos and more speed, which may sway the decision for a game of this profile.

The more interesting question is in midfield. Rayan Cherki offers creativity in the No 10 role, while Ayyoub Bouaddi would give City more balance if Maresca wants Enzo Fernandez pushed further forward alongside Elliot Anderson.

Phil Foden is unavailable as he serves the last game of his suspension. Nico O'Reilly remains a doubt after missing training following his withdrawal from the England squad.

Donnarumma; Nunes, Dias, Guehi, Gvardiol; Fernandez, Anderson; Semenyo, Cherki, Doku; Haaland

For Manchester City, the core of the side looks settled. The real debate is about the margins, and against Liverpool at Anfield, those margins usually decide everything.

title: Prep talk: Volunteers fill multiple roles to help high school teams succeed
description: Bennett Rogers of Palos Verdes High volunteers at football games to run the camera.
fullText:
High school sports programs are filled with dozens of volunteers — manning the snack bar, taking tickets, helping provide security, cleaning floors, carrying equipment and taking statistics.

One of the most entrusted volunteers in football is the cameraman. That person must film the entire game, whether from the press box or the sideline.

Bennett Rogers is in his first year as Palos Verdes High's cameraman. He sits in the end zone and has a camera that goes up so high on a tripod that it could be waving a flag. His son coaches for Palos Verdes, so he volunteered to shoot the games.

His most important equipment is a portable, comfortable chair that lasts through four quarters.

"That's the key for my age," he said.

To all the moms and dads volunteering, you're the unsung heroes. Just make sure you have a sturdy chair when taking video.

This is a daily look at the positive happenings in high school sports. To submit any news, please email eric.sondheimer@latimes.com.

title: Is Eagles' Saquon Barkley playing vs Jaguars? Is Jalen Hurts injured?
description: Is Saquon Barkley playing for Eagles against the Jaguars, and why is Jalen Hurts on injury report?
fullText:
LONDON − The Eagles won't have running back Saquon Barkley when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Oct. 11.

Barkley is among five Eagles ruled out for the game.

The others are WR DeVonta Smith, C Drew Kendall, S Marcus Epps and WR Hollywood Brown. OLB Jonathan Greenard is listed as "questionable" even though he hasn't practiced all week because of an ankle injury.

Buy Philadelphia Eagles tickets

Interestingly, Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was listed on the team's final injury and status report on Oct. 9. He was listed as having a calf injury. But Hurts was a full participant in practice that day and is cleared to play.

The Eagles shuffled their backup quarterback QB rotation during the week. They released veteran Andy Dalton, thus moving Tanner McKee up to the backup with rookie Cole Payton as the No. 3. Dalton, 38, had gotten into the Eagles' game against the Chicago Bears on Sept. 28.

He threw one pass, an interception into the end zone from the Bears' 2 yard line, during the Eagles' 27-7 loss. Hurts at the time was in the medical tent getting evaluated for a concussion. He was cleared to return for the Eagles' next offensive series.

As for Barkley, he left the Eagles' 24-20 loss to the Rams on Oct. 4 with a hamstring injury on a first-quarter run to the sideline and did not return. The Eagles lost his backup, Tank Bigsby, to injury later in the game. That left Will Shipley as the only other running back on the 53-man roster.

Since then, the Eagles placed Bigsby on the injured list and promoted both Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele from the practice squad to the 53-man roster. It's expected that Shipley and Pierce will be the Eagles' main ball carriers against the Jaguars.

Smith, meanwhile, is missing his second straight game with the hamstring injury. He was plagued by a strained hamstring during training camp and missed nearly three weeks.

title: NFL power rankings, updated entering Sunday Week 5
description: Power rankings for all 32 NFL teams entering Sunday Week 5.
fullText:
We've reached the fifth week of the season, and the NFL now has just 3 undefeated teams remaining. With the 
Kansas City Chiefs taking the week off as one of the first two teams to have a bye week, we are assured that at least one will remain in Week 6.

How will we rank them along with the other two unbeaten teams in this week's power rankings? Let's jump in and find out.

MORE: 7 NFL teams with best chance to win Super Bowl LXI entering Week 5

Sep 27, 2026; Miami Gardens, Florida, USA; Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis (2) passes the ball against the Kansas City Chiefs during the third quarter at Hard Rock Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images

#32 Miami Dolphins: It's been bad from day 1 this season in South Beach. The Dolphins are the only team that hasn't scored 50 points through 4 games. If you root for the Dolphins, we suggest you pay close attention to the College games to see which player Miami will take #1 overall next year.

#31 Tennessee Titans: The Titans are giving the Dolphins a run for their money in the offensive futility department. Their 55 total points through 4 games is easily the second lowest in the league. They take on a winless Texans team this Sunday in a battle for the basement in the AFC South.

#30 Los Angeles Chargers: Stop us if you've heard this one before…"The Chargers have lost both Rashan Slater and Joe Alt and will be without their top two tackles for the foreseeable future. Justin Herbert is in for another rough season.

#29 New York Jets: That Week 1 victory is a distant memory. This team is gasping for air and a home loss this weekend against the Browns may just knock them down for good. It's still early, but they aren't bouncing back if they lose that game.

#28 Washington Commanders: The injuries keep piling up at QB as well as on their offensive line. Jayden Daniels will attempt to come back this week, but what version of him will the Commanders get?

#27 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: They pulled off a miracle win on Thursday night to move up a few spots. That win told us more about the Cowboys than it did about the Bucs, but they did manage to salvage hope for this season if they can hold on until Baker gets back.

#26 Arizona Cardinals: They feel like an improved team, but the wins haven't happened yet. This week they host the Lions in what should be a high-scoring affair. This might be a game the Birds can win.

Oct 4, 2026; Houston, Texas, USA; Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) passes the ball against the Dallas Cowboys during the first half at Reliant Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images

#25 Houston Texans: Teams don't generally bounce back from 0-4. The Texans travel to Nashville to take on the team that used to wear the Baby Blues in Houston back when the Titans were the Oilers. If the Texans lose this one, somebody is getting benched or fired.

#24 Dallas Cowboys: Oh boy. Losing in Jerry World to a winless Bucs team was downright frightening to watch. Joey Porter should make this defense better, but he isn't going to help them stop the run.

#23 New Orleans Saints: The Falcons ran all over them on Monday, handing the Saints a second straight home loss. This week they host the undefeated Vikings as they try to avoid the dreaded Hat Trick. It won't be easy down in the Big Easy, but the Saints need to win this one to stay in the AFC South race.

#22 Green Bay Packers: They won a game they needed to in Tampa, but they still have tons of kinks to work out. The offense needs to figure out how to move the ball without relying on their offensive line. Good luck.

#21 Philadelphia Eagles: We had to drop the Eagles down considerably after last week's loss and a rash of injuries, trades, and retirements that will hinder their offense in the short term. Jalen Hurts is going to need to be Superman this week in Jacksonville if the Birds are going to avoid a third straight loss.

#20 Indianapolis Colts: They beat the Commanders in London, but the offense is still sputtering while the defense still looks beatable. This should be a good test this Sunday in Pittsburgh against an apparently equally mediocre Steelers team.

#19 New England Patriots: They had an impressive victory last Sunday in Buffalo. Drake Maye needs to build on that momentum if the Patriots are going to make a playoff push.

#18 Pittsburgh Steelers: Two wins at home and two losses on the road. This week they get the Colts in Pittsburgh, so there's reason to be hopeful.

Sep 24, 2026; Green Bay, Wisconsin, USA; Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (9) during the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Hanisch-Imagn Images

#17 Atlanta Falcons: Two games in a row since the return of Michael Penix have featured impressive results from the Atlanta running game. The defense has also impressed, and the Falcons will look to build on that this Sunday night against the Lamar-less Ravens.

#16 Carolina Panthers: Like the Falcons, the Panthers look like an improved team with an exciting offense. Both teams sit at 2-2 atop the NFC South division. This week, Bryce Young and friends get a week off with their bye.

#15 Cincinnati Bengals: The defense is still a bit of a weakness, but it was the offense that let them down at home last Sunday against a tough Jaguars squad. Now they may have to figure things out without their top two offensive weapons in Chase and Higgins. Luckily, they won't need much to get past the Dolphins this week.

#14 Detroit Lions: The defense is going to be a problem for them all season long. This week they take on the Cardinals in the desert; if they can't outscore Jacoby Brissett and Co., then this might be a long season in the Motor City.

#13 Cleveland Browns: Let's hear it for the "first place" Cleveland Browns, ladies and gentlemen!!! This team believes in what Todd Monken is preaching, and Deshaun Watson looks like a serviceable NFL QB. They very well could go into MetLife and beat up on a reeling Jets team.

#12 New York Giants: Another surprising first-place team. The NFC East looks like it's devolving into a dumpster fire, and the G-men may just be the least trashy team in the division, even without Jaxson Dart. If they win this Sunday in Washington, the fans might actually dare to dream.

#11 Los Angeles Rams: Two wins and two losses through 4 games isn't ideal, but this team will be fine. This week they will have their hands full as they host the Bills on Monday Night in what could very well be a Super Bowl preview.

MORE: Predicting upsets in Week 5 of NFL season

Oct 4, 2026; Santa Clara, California, USA; Denver Broncos quarterback Bo Nix (10) looks to pass against the San Francisco 49ers during the first half at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images

#10 Denver Broncos: They looked a bit outmatched against a tough 49er team last Sunday, and they lost both starting corners, Patrick Surtain and Riley Moss, in the process. They should be back fairly soon, and the team should be able to mask their loss while facing a bumbling Chargers offense this Sunday.

#9 Las Vegas Raiders: They gave the Chiefs all they could handle last week in what looked like a playoff-caliber matchup. This team is for real, but they have a tough matchup this Sunday as they will travel to Foxboro for the second straight season to take on the Pats, who will look for revenge for last year's opening weekend loss.

#8 Baltimore Ravens: Lamar Jackson is going to miss at least one game, if not more. Tyler Huntley is an experienced backup, and he knows how to hand the ball to Derrick Henry. This week they travel to Atlanta for a Prime Time, Sunday Night matchup against Bijan Robinson and the Falcons.

#7 Chicago Bears: Two games without their starting QB, and the Bears have 2 wins to show for it. This weekend they will look to stay hot as they travel to Lambeau Field to take on their hated division rival Packers. Even without Caleb Williams, it feels like the Bears will be too much for Green Bay.

#6 Jacksonville Jaguars: This team looks like one of the better teams in the league right now. Liam Coen isn't asking much of Trevor Lawrence while the team's defense has been playing nearly lights-out football. This week they host a limping Eagles team as they look to stay on top in the AFC South.

Sep 9, 2026; Seattle, Washington, USA; Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold (14) takes the field for warm ups before a game against the New England Patriots at Lumen Field. Mandatory Credit: Joe Nicholson-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

#5 Seattle Seahawks: They took care of business at home against a hapless Chargers team. Things get tougher this week as they host the undefeated 49ers in what should be a key game come season's end when it comes to playoff seeding. The backfield is still in disarray, as evidenced by the fact that they almost signed the ghost of Joe Mixon this week.

#4 Minnesota Vikings: They're undefeated, and that's a good thing. They played the Dolphins and didn't score a touchdown; that's a bad thing. OK, sure, Hockenson could have had a touchdown, but that was in the 57th minute of the game. The defense is the lead story with this squad, and they will need to stay hot if they are going to keep winning, especially if they will be without Justin Jefferson for another week.

#3 Buffalo Bills: They dropped from the top spot after losing a head-scratcher at home to the Patriots. Chalk it up as a bad day at the office, but it was certainly a missed opportunity to knock down their biggest division threat in the early going. Things won't get easier this week as they take on the Rams in LA on Monday Night.

#2 Kansas City Chiefs: The Chiefs cruise into their early season bye week at a perfect 4-0. Early bye weeks are usually troublesome when a team is hot and will more likely need the rest later in the season, but after losing Rashee Rice to a hamstring injury, the bye may have come at a perfect time. Mahomes and friends will be back to work in week 6 when they host the Chargers.

#1 San Francisco 49ers: Four games in and the 49ers are sitting at a perfect 4-0. Their 122 points scored rank 2nd in the league while they boast an NFL-best +58 point differential. This week, San Francisco will have their hands full as they travel to Seattle to take on the Hawks in a key NFC West showdown.

title: Sneaky Patriots must-start for fantasy football managers in Week 5
description: Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson could have a breakout game in Week 5 against a favorable Raiders run defense.
fullText:
New England Patriots running back TreVeyon Henderson is a worthwhile player to start as a flex option in fantasy football for Week 5 against the Las Vegas Raiders, particularly with Rhamondre Stevenson's knee issue creating uncertainty in New England's offensive backfield.

Henderson has recorded 38 carries for 141 yards and a touchdown through four games played this season, averaging 3.7 yards per attempt. He also has one reception for six yards, giving him 147 yards from scrimmage. Henderson most recently handled 14 carries in last week's victory over the Buffalo Bills and recorded 42 yards. His season-high is 76 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown on 16 carries, which came in Week 2 against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Stevenson has been limited in practice this week due to injury. Although he may still play, any reduction in his workload will open the door for more opportunities for Henderson, especially in scoring situations, giving him appeal as a high-upside player for fantasy football team managers.

The Raiders have allowed the sixth-most rushing yards to opponents in the NFL this season with 538 yards, and they have also given up four rushing touchdowns. Las Vegas also yielded 177 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns to Kansas City Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III in Week 4, making Henderson a favorable Week 5 matchup play.

title: Yankees Must Move On From Stanton To Fix Roster Holes
description: The Yankees got swept by Tampa Bay. It is time to stop holding onto Giancarlo Stanton and build a team that can actually win.
fullText:
Following their AL Division Series sweep by the Tampa Bay Rays, the New York Yankees have been eliminated from the playoffs. This loss exposes a roster that simply cannot compete at the highest level. The most glaring issue is the heavy contract tied up in Giancarlo Stanton, a player who misses too many games and hits too little when he is healthy. With his deal nearing its end, the front office faces a hard choice about his future. Keeping him around blocks the path to a better team.

Stanton has been a liability for years, not just because of injuries but also due to poor production. Even when he plays, his numbers have dropped compared to his prime years. The team needs to cut ties and free up money for players who can help right now. Yahoo Sports reports that the organization faces a genuine choice regarding whether to evaluate his remaining capabilities. The answer should be no. They need to stop waiting for a player to get healthy and start building with guys who are ready to play every day.

Instead of wasting spots on Stanton, the Yankees should focus on filling specific gaps with smarter moves. Paul Goldschmidt wants to keep playing, but only as a bench bat against left-handed pitching. "I'd like to continue playing, so we'll see if that opportunity happens," Goldschmidt told Newsday's Roger Rubin after New York's elimination. He hit .299 with 11 home runs against lefties this year, which is useful. However, he should never be an everyday starter again. The team needs to give Ben Rice the full-time job at first base after his 41-homer season. Goldschmidt can be a tool, not a crutch.

The same logic applies to the catcher position. Austin Wells needs a backup who can hit, not a ghost from the past. In a recent Sports Illustrated piece, Joe Najarian advised the Yankees to re-sign Gary Sanchez. "Hear me out: a reunion with Gary Sanchez to back up Wells would be a solid offensive upgrade," Najarian wrote. Sanchez hit 12 home runs for the Brewers this year and has the power to change a game. A cheap one-year deal for him makes more sense than paying Stanton to sit on the bench. The Yankees have holes to fill, and they need to use their resources wisely to fix them.

title: Is Ashton Jeanty playing today? Injury update, fantasy advice for Week 5
description: Here's what we know about Ashton Jeanty's chances of playing in Week 5.
fullText:
When the Las Vegas Raiders take the field for their Week 5 contest against the New England Patriots, the team is hoping to have running back Ashton Jeanty in the lineup.

Jeanty is dealing with both foot and ankle injuries, although the foot injury is the new one and the bigger concern.

After logging a full practice on Wednesday, Jeanty was downgraded to a limited session on Thursday, when he had the foot injury added, and then he was a no go on Friday ahead of drawing the questionable tag.

With just hours to go before kickoff, here's what we know about his chances of suiting up in Week 5 against New England.

MORE: AFC power rankings for Week 5 see Raiders climb despite loss

Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty (2) runs with the ball in the third quarter against the Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium. Credit: David Brytus-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

According to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, Jeanty is "hopeful to play," but the Raiders are still going to work him out pregame before making a final determination.

Rapoport adds that Jeanty's foot injury is a "flare up of plantar fasciitis."

"Raiders RB Ashton Jeanty, who missed practice late in the week due to a flare up of plantar fasciitis along with an ankle injury, is hopeful to play today, sources say. But it's not definite and he'll work out pregame to see how he's feeling. Las Vegas elevated a RB in case," Rapoport reported.

MORE: NFL power rankings entering Week 5 of NFL season

As Rapoport notes, the elevation of Roman Hemby suggests the Raiders are at least preparing themselves for the absence of Jeanty.

Without the former No. 6 pick, Las Vegas would only have two healthy backs on the roster, hence Hemby's elevation just in case.

We'll have a definitive answer an hour and a half before the 1 p.m. ET kickoff, when the Raiders and Patriots drop their inactives.

Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty (2) exits the field after the game against the Miami Dolphins at Allegiant Stadium. Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The best thing for fantasy owners might be to just have Jeanty ruled inactive because this seems like a shaky situation in which Jeanty could re-aggravate his injury and leave the contest early.

If Jeanty sits, backup running back Mike Washington is a viable starting option because, if nothing else, he should see a ton of volume, as Jeanty is averaging 24 touches per game.

However, if Jeanty plays, he has to be in lineups, if for no other reason than the volume we just mentioned. The only way we wouldn't start Jeanty is if there's a report he'll be limited.

title: Roberto De Zerbi sees promising signs in Tottenham draw at Man Utd
description: Tottenham Hotspur's wait for a first Premier League win of the season continues but Roberto De Zerbi takes his side to Spain for a training camp having seen promising signs in the late draw at Manchester United. A big-spending summer after scraping survival last term has increased expectations in north London, but Spurs remain without a victory after six matches.
fullText:
Tottenham Hotspur's wait for a first Premier League win of the season continues but Roberto De Zerbi takes his side to Spain for a training camp having seen promising signs in the late draw at Manchester United.

A big-spending summer after scraping survival last term has increased expectations in north London, but Spurs remain without a victory after six matches.

Tottenham have only previously managed that in 1955-56 and 2008-09, but there was a sense of positivity around fans, staff and players after the latest fixture in that run.

Spurs fought back from Bryan Mbeumo firing United ahead and a Rodrigo Bentancur red card to snatch a 1-1 draw on Saturday night, when skipper Dominic Solanke headed home in stoppage time.

"We showed the right reaction. We played a great game," boss De Zerbi said.

"I think we are playing well, not (just) today, also the other games before Manchester, but today has been the game where for the first time in this season we showed to be a team.

"We played for the team-mates, we played together, we believed until the end of the game, we stayed inside of the game in every situation, and we attacked as a team, we defended as a team, the right football behaviour."

Tottenham will have the chance to build on that during a training camp in Spain ahead of their return to action at home to promoted Coventry next Monday.

"To work together, to stay together, to go for dinner together, to know better each other, because to be a team you have to know the team-mates, to stay together," De Zerbi said of the benefits of the trip.

"We have to build the team. Now the target is to build the team, not the group of the players.

"We are a great group of players, but we are not a team yet. Today, this game, we show to be a team.

"To be a team is to play for the team-mates, suffer together, attack together, defend together, the players who come inside five minutes, three minutes, like Mateus Ferdandes, they have to play like they are in the first 11, without problems, without other faults.

"We have to find the balance between the confidence in ourselves and to be hungry in the training and in the games."

title: How the Green Bay Packers plan to honour late NFL legend Mike Ditka revealed
description: The Green Bay Packers will honour the greatest personality in their rival Chicago Bears’ history before their Week 5 game. The Bears-Packers rivalry in the NFL is arguably the oldest in the league’s history, tracing its origins back to 1921.
fullText:
The Green Bay Packers will honour the greatest personality in their rival Chicago Bears' history before their Week 5 game.

The Bears-Packers rivalry in the NFL is arguably the oldest in the league's history, tracing its origins back to 1921. Ditka kept that historic rivalry alive with him for decades, and his passing on Friday, October 9, has led to an honourable gesture by the Packers.

Despite going 5-15 against the Bears when Ditka was coaching them, the Packers will honour one of their greatest rivals in their next game, rising above the rivalry to honour the legendary NFL figure.

Sunday, October 11 will add the latest instalment in the iconic Bears-Packers rivalry, but the game will start with an unprecedented friendly moment between the organisations.

The Packers have confirmed that they will host a moment of silence for Ditka before hosting the Bears at Lambeau Field.

"One of the fiercest competitors in NFL history, Mike helped define the intensity and tradition of the Packers-Bears rivalry, the oldest in professional football. He embodied the toughness and passion that have made the rivalry one of the most storied in all of sports."

"While he was a formidable opponent, his contributions to the game and to a rivalry that has meant so much to both franchises will always be respected and remembered by the Green Bay Packers."

Ditka played as a WR for the Bears from 1961-66, registering a paltry 3-9 record against Vince Lombardi's formidable Packers of that generation.

He used the Packers hate from his playing days to fuel the rivalry as a coach, dominating the rivalry between 1982 and 1992, also bringing the Bears their only Super Bowl win in franchise history.

Both organisations are rising above past hatred and uniting to honour one of the greatest figures in NFL history, not just an iconic staple of the Bears-Packers rivalry.
