title: Sharp retires after incredible 22-year career
description: Sheffield United legend Billy Sharp announces his retirement from football at the age of 40.
fullText:
Sheffield United legend Billy Sharp has announced his retirement from football at the age of 40.

Sharp, who played for Southampton, Nottingham Forest, Leeds United, Hull City, Scunthorpe United, Reading, Doncaster Rovers and Rushden & Diamonds during a 22-year professional career, during which he scored 299 goals.

He had been a free agent since leaving Doncaster at the end of last season, when he signed off in style in his final game with a hat-trick against Peterborough.

"I'm going to hang my boots up. I've given it a good ride. I've got a long way, got to 40," Sharp told Sky Sports.

"I wanted to go out on my own terms. I've seen many friends get taken away by injury and things like that.

"I wanted to go out with a bang and luckily for me, I got a hat-trick in my last appearance.

"I'm maybe not the most talented player, maybe not the most liked on the pitch but that's because I love football. I'm passionate and I think I've got every single bit out of my career.

"I've made memories in football that will last me a lifetime."

A boyhood Blades supporter, Sharp made his Championship debut off the bench against Watford in November 2004.

He went on to become club captain and an important figure in three promotion-winning campaigns - from League One in 2017 and the Championship in 2019 and 2023.

In three spells with Sheffield United, Sharp scored 129 goals for the club and became a Blades icon.

He was also part of the Southampton side that won promotion to the Premier League in 2012.

He enjoyed a brief stay in the MLS with LA Galaxy in 2023, after which many thought retirement loomed - but the ageless Sharp returned to his native Yorkshire to extend his career, firstly with Hull and then Doncaster Rovers.

Sharp scored a dramatic late winner against Bradford City to secure promotion to League One for Rovers in 2025 before his spectacular ending to last season which meant he had scored EFL hat-tricks in his teens, 20s, 30s and 40s. He did score a fourth against Peterborough which would have taken him to 300 career goals but it was ruled out for offside.

"It would have been lovely to have got that 300th goal on that day but I've had an unbelievable career," he said.

Sharp has joined Baller League team N5, which is led by former Arsenal and Germany goalkeeper Jens Lehmann to play six-a-side football but he also has one eye on management having completed his coaching badges.

title: Steelers Struggle Revealed As Smith Elevates Amid Brutal Depth Crisis
description: With Michael Pittman Jr. out, the Steelers elevate Brandon Smith. Rodgers praises the rookie, but can he fill the void?
fullText:
The Steelers made a necessary move on Saturday. For the upcoming game against the Indianapolis Colts, they elevated wide receiver Brandon Smith from the practice squad. This decision comes after Michael Pittman Jr. re-aggravated a foot injury that will keep him out for at least four games. The team announced the roster change on Saturday. It is a clear sign that the depth chart is thinner than anyone hoped.

Aaron Rodgers has been singing Smith's praises. The quarterback saw something special during Saturday Night Lights. Rodgers said, "As you saw on Saturday Night Lights, possibly the play of the day was from Brandon Smith." He went on to describe Smith's recent work. "He had a phenomenal practice. He made a ton of plays," Rodgers said, according to Yahoo Sports. The connection between the two is not new. They had met previously while playing for the New York Jets in 2024.

The veteran quarterback noticed a physical transformation in the young receiver. Rodgers recalled seeing him last year and noted a difference in his build. "I knew him from my time in New York. When I saw him last year, he looked like he dropped about 10 pounds," Rodgers said. He believes the weight loss has helped Smith's movement. Rodgers added that Smith looks "a little leaner" and feels he is moving better now. This physical change seems to be paying off in practice.

Smith has been through the wringer to get here. He entered the 2025 season with the Jets but was waived. New England released him on Jan. 13, 2026, after he moved to the Patriots practice squad. The Steelers signed him to a reserve/future contract back in January. He was waived on Aug. 30 and then re-signed to the practice squad. Now he gets his first real chance. He has not made a catch in his NFL career. His stats are thin, but his preparation looks solid.

The injury to Pittman forces a reshuffle of the entire receiving corps. Pittman led the team with 58 receiving yards in the opener. Ruled out for the Week 2 matchup against the New England Patriots, he sustained a plantar fasciitis injury during practice. Despite playing in Weeks 3 and 4, he was not at 100%. He was spotted with his foot on a scooter.

With Pittman sidelined, Roman Wilson and Germie Bernard must step up. Smith will likely be the sixth option vs. the Colts. He likely won't get called upon, but he needs to be ready. In addition, the Steelers signed defensive back Doneiko Slaughter and moved Lew Nichols to the Active/Inactive Roster.

The roster is tight. One more injury could break the unit. The team has to hope Smith's training camp flash turns into game-day production. The clock is ticking for the rest of the group. They have to find a way to move the ball. The Colts will test them hard.

title: Falcons Face Ravens In A Must-Win Sunday Night Showdown
description: The Falcons host the Ravens in a prime-time clash. NBC airs the game at 8:20 p.m. ET from Mercedes-Benz Stadium. See where to stream.
fullText:
The wait is finally over for Atlanta fans who need a win to feel good about this season. The Falcons host the Baltimore Ravens Sunday at 8:20 p.m. ET, and the stakes could not be higher for a team trying to find its rhythm. This is not just another regular-season game; it is a battle of the birds played on the national stage. Yahoo Sports reports that Atlanta's offense is coming in red-hot behind Michael Penix Jr., while the Ravens have started the year strong with a 3-1 record.

Watching the action requires a plan because the game will not be on your local cable channel. From Atlanta, the Atlanta venue hosts the broadcast of "Sunday Night Football" by NBC, featuring Cris Collinsworth as color analyst alongside play-by-play announcer Mike Tirico. Fans who do not have a cable subscription can turn toward DIRECTV, which is currently offering a free trial, Fubo, or Peacock to stream the game live. The broadcast team knows how to break down the Xs and Os, which matters when you have elite talent on both sides of the ball.

The potential for fireworks is massive because both teams have the firepower to score in bunches. You have Derrick Henry and Zay Flowers for Baltimore going up against Bijan Robinson and Drake London for Atlanta. These are not just names on a roster; they are game-changers who can break a game open with a single play. Yahoo Sports observes that the defense faces a challenging night given the abundance of offensive talent present in this matchup. title: ‘Humiliation ritual’ – WWE fans aren’t buying Triple H’s LA Knight comments after Roman Reigns loss
description: LA Knight came up short yet again in his quest to win a world championship, losing to Roman Reigns in the opening match of Money in the Bank. Despite being a crowd favourite and one of the biggest, most organically grown stars in recent memory, the WWE have done little to reward LA Knight for his hard work.
fullText:
LA Knight came up short yet again in his quest to win a world championship, losing to Roman Reigns in the opening match of Money in the Bank.

Despite being a crowd favourite and one of the biggest, most organically grown stars in recent memory, the WWE have done little to reward LA Knight for his hard work.

Outside of a run with the United States championship in 2024, Knight has found himself in a perennial bridesmaid role with the company, constantly failing to win the world title.

In the Money in the Bank post-show, WWE Chief Content Officer Paul 'Triple H' Levesque praised LA Knight for his performances against Roman Reigns.

Despite him not winning the World Heavyweight Championship, Triple H claimed Knight showed that he proved he is a main-event player.

Triple H said: "LA Knight, to me, left this match greater than he went in. LA Knight proved that he is a megastar.

"LA Knight proved that he belongs in that title scene. LA Knight proved that he is a top attraction in this business."

While these are positive comments from the head booker of the company, fans were understandably frustrated that this outward praise from Levesque rarely translated to the on-screen product.

One fan wrote: "What he is saying is a complete lie compared to how he booked Knight in the match."

Another fan added, "He has said this before, and LA Knight ended up in the lower midcard."

A third fan made a scathing comment about Levesque's booking of LA Knight: "It's just a humiliation ritual at this point. He's doing it to troll all of his fans. That's the only reason why he made this match – for his yearly Money in the Bank humiliation ritual. It's embarrassing to watch."

Amid frustration and concern about Knight's future, a fourth fan wrote: "LA Knight is soon to be 44 and looks no more likely to win a world title in WWE than he did yesterday. Should've been strapped up years ago, but they still refuse to do it."

A fifth fan pointed to a historic pattern within the company: "The thing with WWE is they hate it when you make yourself a star, especially when they didn't plan it. Unfortunately for LA Knight, they still don't plan on it."

And lastly, one final fan hoped for a more optimistic result for Knight in the future: "LA Knight better be getting a WrestleMania coronation when he wins the World Title at this stage."

Knight has been one of the WWE's most popular stars since he caught fire in 2023. While he has yet to win a world title, he has proved himself to be quite valuable for the company as one of their most reliable babyfaces.

There is some truth to the idea that the WWE brain trust doesn't reward wrestlers for organically getting over, with Zack Ryder (Matt Cardona) and Daniel Bryan (Bryan Danielson) being prime examples.

And while this isn't the same regime that tried to squash the previous two examples, a lot of their habits are very similar to the way Vince McMahon would react in those situations.

title: Bryson DeChambeau Weighs Options Beyond LIV Golf
description: Bryson DeChambeau explores career paths outside LIV Golf, including the DP World Tour and YouTube, as the league faces restructuring uncertainty.
fullText:
Bryson DeChambeau is looking beyond the current LIV Golf structure as the league faces a major business overhaul. The two-time major champion has been linked to more starts on the DP World Tour, signaling a potential shift in his competitive schedule.

While he remains under contract, the uncertainty surrounding the league's future has opened the door for other options. This includes a confirmed appearance in South Africa later this year and a serious push to grow his digital media presence if the tour model changes.

The situation is fluid, with several high-profile players making moves to secure their futures. Jon Rahm has already stated he will not participate in the proposed LIV 2.0 plan, and Sergio Garcia was granted a release from his contract earlier this week.

Golf Channel reported that John Beck, representing Rahm, stated at a bankruptcy hearing that Rahm had "independently reviewed the proposed terms of LIV 2.0" and deemed them "unacceptable to him." This leaves DeChambeau as a key figure whose decision could define the new league.

Reports from The Telegraph indicate that DeChambeau's team has contacted DP World Tour officials to discuss potential tournament appearances in 2027. Late last month, golf insider Alan Shipnuck noted that DeChambeau continued to consider his options.

Unlike Patrick Reed, who joined the European tour when he departed LIV at the start of 2026, this American is not seeking full membership on that circuit. Instead, he appears to be looking for specific starts rather than a full roster commitment.

DeChambeau has also been vocal about his business ventures. Stating in May 2026 to Golf Channel that he aimed to triple his YouTube audience should LIV Golf fail to continue. At the time, his channel had approximately 2.69 million subscribers.

He mentioned plans to expand videos into additional languages to reach a global audience. An interview from 2025 disclosed his investment of over $1 million in his YouTube operation, demonstrating a serious commitment to this alternative revenue stream.

The most concrete step away from the current LIV model is his scheduled participation in the Nedbank Golf Challenge. The DP World Tour confirmed DeChambeau's entry in August. From December 3 to 6, 2026, he will compete at the Gary Player Country Club in Sun City, South Africa. This event provides a guaranteed competitive platform outside the LIV circuit before the end of the 2026 season. It serves as a clear indicator that he is keeping his options open while the league's future remains unclear.

The landscape for elite golfers is shifting rapidly as players evaluate their long-term careers. DeChambeau's hesitation to commit to LIV 2.0 mirrors the sentiment of other top players who are wary of the league's restructuring. The DP World Tour is increasingly positioning itself as a lifeline for those seeking an exit. While DeChambeau has not announced a permanent departure, his actions speak to a desire for flexibility.

His strategy seems to focus on maintaining high-level competition through select events while building a media empire that does not rely on a single tour. This dual approach allows him to stay relevant in the sport regardless of how the business side resolves.

The investment in YouTube suggests he is preparing for a future where his audience might be more valuable than his tournament purse. If LIV 2.0 fails to secure enough players with outstanding financial claims, the pressure on DeChambeau to make a final choice will only increase.

For now, the focus remains on the upcoming tournament in South Africa. The Nedbank Golf Challenge runs from December 3 to 6, 2026, offering a clear date for fans to watch DeChambeau in action outside the LIV framework.

This appearance was confirmed by the DP World Tour in August and stands as the only fixed competitive commitment outside the league at this moment. Any further moves will likely depend on how the bankruptcy proceedings and the LIV 2.0 deadline unfold.

title: Packers' new uniforms: Green Bay's 'Rivalries' alternates inspired by team's stock
description: Green Bay is the second team to debut new Nike alternates in 2026, the alabaster color meant to be “reminiscent of aged paper color of historic Packers stock certificates.”
fullText:
If you're emotionally invested in the Green Bay Packers, then you are probably disappointed in the ROI this season ... if maybe feeling fairly fortunate that the scuffling Pack currently sit at. 500 heading into their Week 5 meeting with the archrival Chicago Bears at Lambeau Field.

But if you're literally invested, such as it is, as one of the roughly half-million stockholders in the NFL's only publicly owned team that operates as a nonprofit corporation, then you should get a kick out of the team's new "Rivalries" uniforms, which will make their debut Sunday and are something of a love letter to the organization's supporters and its past – and probably represent the slickest alternate look the normally conservatively clad Pack have ever worn.

The color palette has been slightly altered with "desaturated vintage green" jerseys and "alabaster" pants and helmets trimmed with the team's familiar gold. The jersey numbers have what the team calls "an engraved treatment" meant to evoke "intricate lettering on paper currency, reflective of the financial contributions from the fans that helped sustain the franchise over the years." The alabaster – call it off white – elements are meant to be "reminiscent of aged paper color of historic Packers stock certificates." Delicate striping throughout the uniform and on the helmets is an additional detail pulled from the bordering pattern on the stock certificates.

The Packers' former "GB" logo, which looks a bit like Notre Dame's interlocking N and D, is a callback to the one legendary coach Vince Lombardi used to wear on his practice hats and is now being featured on the upper left chest area of the jersey and the back of the helmet.

"Making History since 1919" is embroidered inside the collar as a nod to the year in which the franchise was founded, which predates the NFL by one year.

Fitted pic.twitter.com/hx0LHosywi

Think of them as the football version of the sports apparel company's NBA "City Edition" uniforms or Major League Baseball's "City Connect" jerseys. Nike has strived to create something that further strengthens NFL teams' bonds to their unique civic environments. And, as "rivalries" would suggest, all of them will be worn in intra-divisional matchups.

"Rivalries uniforms will celebrate storied local traditions and unite fan communities with designs unique to select cities and teams," Nike announced during the program's launch in 2025.

"The designs are rooted extensively in the legacies and inspirations true to each team, serving as authentic, competitive expressions of community pride while giving athletes and fans an opportunity to connect like never before."

Eventually all of them will. This year, AFC South and NFC North squads are joining the AFC East and NFC West teams that kicked off the initiative last year. Every team that has a "Rivalries" uni is scheduled to wear it once this season. The other four divisions will be added to the rotation over the next two seasons, and the "Rivalries" option then becomes part of a team's closet for the following three years.

title: Dodgers Star Max Muncy Reveals ‘AI Programs’ Used To Spot Pitch Tipping
description: The Los Angeles Dodgers’ veteran infielder detailed the use of artificial intelligence to identify pitcher tendencies.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are pursuing a third consecutive World Series title, and they have little reason to leave any possible advantage unexplored as they prepare to face the Milwaukee Brewers in the National League Championship Series.

Even for a star-studded roster, October baseball often comes down to small details. Recognizing a pitcher's tendencies, anticipating a particular offering and identifying subtle clues before the ball leaves a hand can make the difference between extending a rally and returning to the dugout.

In a sign of just how important the details can be in the postseason, the National League Division Series between the Brewers and San Diego Padres, many fans believed the Dodgers' division rival was tipping his pitches.

"This riveting National League Division Series between the Padres and Brewers shifted to San Diego on Monday, with Milwaukee leading two games to none," AJ Cassavell and Adam McCalvey wrote earlier this week. "And there was no buzzier topic during the off-day workout than the possibility that Miller, the sport's premier closer, tipped his pitches during his blown save in Game 2."

Dodgers Move Familiar Name Right Before Brewers NLCS Matchup

In a larger conversation in which he defended the art of identifying pitch tips, Dodgers infielder Max Muncy revealed that cutting-edge technology is changing how teams search for those clues.

"I've heard of a couple of teams starting to use AI programs to, you know, you plug in pitches and the program points (to) differences in where the glove is and all this other stuff and hand position," Muncy said during an appearance on Foul Territory. "I think a lot of that is going on."

Muncy's comments pointed to a potential new layer of postseason preparation: using artificial intelligence to analyze video and identify small mechanical differences that might reveal what pitch is coming.

AI-assisted analysis could help teams process large amounts of video and flag movements that might otherwise escape notice.

Braves' MVP Castoff Launches New Career Shortly After Cut

The Dodgers enter their NLCS rematch with the Brewers after advancing past the Atlanta Braves in four games. The Brewers, meanwhile, arrive after eliminating the Padres, setting up another meeting between two clubs with recent postseason history.

Milwaukee won 103 games during the regular season, compared with 100 for Los Angeles, and has the home-field advantage to begin the series. The Dodgers swept the Brewers in last year's NLCS, but a repeat of that dominance is far from guaranteed.

For Muncy and his teammates, finding an advantage may mean looking beyond traditional scouting reports. AI tools could help organize and detect patterns, but players still need to interpret the information and execute against elite pitching.

This article was originally published on Forbes.com

title: 5 Explosive Reasons To Watch ONE SAMURAI 4 On October 17
description: Fans inside Ariake Arena and those around the world are in for an electric night of martial arts action in Tokyo.
fullText:
ONE Championship brings one of its biggest shows of the year back to Tokyo, and the card has the absolute star power to match the special occasion.

ONE SAMURAI 4 lands at the iconic Ariake Arena on Saturday, October 17, with explosive bouts across Muay Thai, kickboxing, submission grappling, and MMA.

The lineup features the best of Japan, from established warriors to hungry up-and-comers, alongside a world-class international contingent eager to crash the party on Japanese soil.

From the first bell to the last, here are five electrifying reasons to circle the date as the world's largest martial arts organization returns to "The Land of the Rising Sun" this week.

Jonathan "The General" Haggerty arrives in Tokyo for the third defense of his ONE Bantamweight Kickboxing World Title, and the Englishman carries himself like a man who has yet to meet his match in the sport.

The 29-year-old is widely regarded as one of the best pound-for-pound strikers on the planet. A former ONE Flyweight and Bantamweight Muay Thai World Champion, he added a third belt to his collection by flattening Fabricio "Wonder Boy" Andrade in the second round at ONE Fight Night 16 in November 2023.

Since then, he has remained unbeaten in kickboxing inside ONE, with defenses against Wei Rui and, most recently, Yuki Yoza in a five-round war at ONE SAMURAI 1.

Standing in his way is a man who knows exactly what it feels like to sit on that throne. Hiroki Akimoto captured the crown with a solid five-round display back at ONE X in March 2022 before enduring a difficult stretch after losing it.

2025 brought the turnaround, though, with wins over former ONE Bantamweight MMA World Champion John "Hands of Stone" Lineker and Wei, followed by a split decision over fellow Japanese dynamo Taimu Hisai earlier this year that confirmed him as the rightful challenger.

A perfect kickboxing run on one side, a former king chasing his old throne on the other, and a home crowd behind the challenger: these are the ingredients of a World Title fight fans will be talking about for years.

Reigning ONE Atomweight Muay Thai World Champion Nadaka Yoshinari steps in for his second assignment as the divisional king with a 42-fight winning streak and more than seven years without a loss.

The 25-year-old claimed the inaugural belt against Thai standout Numsurin Chor Ketwina at ONE 173 in November last year, then outpointed longtime rival Songchainoi "Mini-Hulk" Kiatsongrit across five fast-paced rounds at ONE SAMURAI 1.

Blinding speed, southpaw precision, and defensive mastery have made him one of the most technically gifted fighters of the modern era, but he could be forced to work extra hard as he chases a 43rd consecutive win against the dangerous Rifdean "Magic Boy" Masdor.

The 23-year-old knockout artist has been nearly flawless under the ONE banner. The Malaysian striker carries a 7-1 record, five straight wins, a 71 percent finish rate, and an average fight time of just four and a half minutes. His latest outing, a first-round finish of Javad Mozafari, earned him a life-changing US$100,000 main roster contract.

For Nadaka, the stakes are historic. Another successful defense would further cement his place among the greatest Muay Thai athletes Japan has ever produced.

The stakes are far bigger in the opposite corner: handing the Eiwa Sports Gym product his first defeat in years would make Rifdean only the second ONE World Champion from Malaysia, following in the footsteps of recently crowned interim strawweight Muay Thai king Aliff Sor Dechapan.

Pair a dominant streak that long with a fighter built to finish, and fireworks are inevitable.

Between the two marquee World Title fights, ONE SAMURAI 4 hosts four of the most dangerous kickboxers in the world — all thirsting for glory in the semifinals of the prestigious ONE SAMURAI Featherweight Kickboxing Tournament.

Three-time Glory Kickboxing World Champion Marat Grigorian meets "The Handsome White Dragon" Luo Chao in the first of the two highly anticipated matchups. The 35-year-old Armenian powerhouse arrives with 71 career wins built on his hallmark pressure, heavy hands, and an intimidating aura.

He booked his spot in the final four with a crushing unanimous decision over Mamuka Usubyan at The Inner Circle 25. Luo, meanwhile, showed his resolve at ONE SAMURAI 2 just a day later, surviving a tough middle stretch against Kosuke "Unstoppable Phoenix" Takagi before breaking through with a late barrage to take the decision.

The other side of the bracket brings its own brand of chaos as former ONE Interim Featherweight Kickboxing World Champion Masaaki Noiri locks horns against Iranian bruiser Mohammad Siasarani.

Noiri stormed through his quarterfinal with a first-round knockout of "Spirit Dragon" Liu Mengyang, avenging an earlier loss and taking home a US$100,000 bonus. The 24-year-old Siasarani, on the other hand, delivered a highlight-reel moment of his own with a stunning head kick finish of Kaito in his 10th promotional triumph.

A spot in the final is on the line, and the tournament winner will earn the prestigious silver belt and a guaranteed shot at reigning ONE Featherweight Kickboxing World Champion Superbon.

Whichever way the bracket shakes out, fans are guaranteed non-stop entertainment here.

Tokyo could hand out more than wins on this card, because the next challengers for 26 pounds of gold may be decided right here across two high-stakes kickboxing battles.

Yuki Yoza meets Nabil Anane in a bantamweight showdown with heavy World Title implications. The former K-1 Champion, who capped a 3-0 run in ONE with a dominant win over "The Kicking Machine" Superlek, came up short against Haggerty at ONE SAMURAI 1 but bounced back with an impressive unanimous decision over Ben "The Problem" Woolliss this past July.

Anane, the former ONE Bantamweight Muay Thai World Champion, brings his towering 6-foot-4 stature and versatile striking to a matchup that pits Yoza's precision and calf kicks against reach. A win would put either man in the conversation for the divisional gold.

In lightweight kickboxing action, Rukiya "Demolition Man" Anpo returns for his sophomore ONE outing after falling short against Grigorian in his debut at ONE 173 inside the same venue. The former K-1 Champion has the hands and the power to make a statement, and he is eager to show he belongs on this stage as he moves up to lightweight.

Standing in his way is Bulgarian tank Bogdan Shumarov, who has looked nothing short of entertaining throughout his tenure on the global stage. The hard-hitting striker has wrapped all his promotional victories in highlight-reel fashion, so don't be surprised if another follows suit.

Waiting at the top is two-sport ONE Lightweight World Champion Regian "The Immortal" Eersel, and whoever wins will make a strong case for the next chance at his gold.

Different divisions, same prize: a seat at the table when the next World Title fights are made.

Few names carry more weight in Japanese combat sports than Takeru "Natural Born Krusher" Segawa, and ONE SAMURAI 4 gives him the send-off he deserves.

The three-division K-1 Champion retired with a 46-5 record after stopping Rodtang "The Iron Man" Jitmuangnon in the fifth round to win the ONE Interim Flyweight Kickboxing World Championship at ONE SAMURAI 1. He will be inducted into the ONE Hall of Fame and receive a 10-gong salute.

He is the fourth name to receive the honor, following fellow ex-ONE World Champions Demetrious "Mighty Mouse" Johnson, Bibiano "The Flash" Fernandes, and "The Burmese Python" Aung La N Sang.

While "Natural Born Krusher" takes his place in history, the rest of Japan's best will be competing with something to prove. Itsuki "Android 18" Hirata is looking to make a statement when she runs it back with Malaysian rival Jihin "Shadow Cat" Radzuan in atomweight MMA action.

K-1 Champion Shintaro Matsukura, meanwhile, opens his promotional account in a lightweight kickboxing bout against former ONE Lightweight Muay Thai World Title challenger Sinsamut "Aquaman" Klinmee.

In addition to that, a quartet of all-Japanese matchups should get the night off to a flyer. Shozo "Great Teacher" Isojima takes on Kota Abe in lightweight MMA, Toki Tamaru faces Shoma Okumura in strawweight kickboxing, Yu Takeuchi and Ryoto Nishiyama duke it out in flyweight MMA, while Yoshinari Fukushima meets Masaki Takeura in lightweight submission grappling.

description: 3 takeaways from an instant Red River Rivalry classic between the Oklahoma Sooners and the Texas Longhorns.
fullText:
The Oklahoma Sooners and the Texas Longhorns delivered another instant classic in the Red River Rivalry at the Cotton Bowl on Saturday afternoon. Despite being unranked and heavy underdogs, OU won the day in Dallas, Texas, with a 27-24 walk-off victory over the favored and top-ranked 'Horns.

Brent Venables' Sooners are now 3-2 overall and 1-1 in SEC play, while Steve Sarkisian's Longhorns fall to 4-1 overall and 1-1 in the SEC. Venables has improved to 2-3 against Texas, while Sarkisian is now 3-3 against Oklahoma.

A wild game in South Dallas ended up going OU's way, with a number of huge plays and star performances worth writing home about. Oklahoma's defense picked off Arch Manning twice, while John Mateer played a turnover-free game at the State Fair of Texas. This matchup has a way of seeing the wacky happen, and that was certainly the case for the 122nd edition of the game on Saturday.

While this game brings so many new and old storylines, let's take a look at three things that can be taken away after an improbable thriller in Dallas.

This Oklahoma team is still flawed. Even with the upset win, the Sooners still have a lot to fix. The offense was largely ineffective for most of the game. The running game struggled in the first half. OU won the special teams battle but made some mistakes there as well. The defense gave up some things, but largely played a whale of a game against the No. 1 team in the nation.

Despite those flaws, the Sooners were good enough against a loaded Longhorns squad this week. Oklahoma hung tough, and it made the plays it had to have when they had to have them. While the offense wasn't at the level it needs to be, it moved the ball better in the second quarter, and that carried over into the second half. The running game at least had a pulse, and Mateer looked a bit more settled. Notably, he also made two brilliant throws to get OU into field goal range for the game-winner. Special teams was a major factor, and the Sooners made huge plays to swing the tide in that department.

We don't know what the future holds for this team. Oklahoma will face a brutal schedule, and they still have plenty of warts. However, this weekend was a step forward; give Venables, his staff, and the team their flowers for that.

The Sooners gave some things up on defense. Manning threw three touchdown passes, and all three were wide open. The Longhorns developed a rhythm running the ball before Oklahoma got back on top of it. If one or two things don't go their way, the Sooners lose this game.

However, the defense played incredible football, considering the circumstances. An offense that didn't give them much to work with meant the defense had to win the day, and they did. The two interceptions off of Manning were gigantic, and the defense just kept giving the Sooners chances, keeping them in the game all afternoon. Was it perfect? No. But with all the talent on the other sideline, and with the way the defense has to carry the program most of the time right now, I certainly won't be critical of them. They were the catalyst, and they earned this win.

This win in a big spot for Venables and the Sooners. It wasn't pretty, but it was enough. That goes for him, Mateer, Ben Arbuckle, and just about all of the other major names at OU Football. They've been heavily criticized for almost a month now, and this was a strong response.

Now, OU has to use this victory to fully turn the season around by improving week by week and building on this foundation. Twice in the last decade (2016 and 2020), the Sooners have had poor starts to the season that ended up with a very strong finish. In that same timeframe, OU has had two seasons (2022 and 2024) where the adversity got to them, and they wilted down the stretch. Venables and Oklahoma have to prove they're the former. The Sooners cannot afford a hangover after a big win, as the one-loss Kentucky Wildcats are coming to town in a week.

A shocking win over Texas has brought the Sooners' season back to life. How they build on this will determine where this season ultimately goes for Oklahoma.

title: Big Ten football Week 6 power rankings: UCLA soars, Oregon plummets
description: Through six weeks of Big Ten play, the conference continues to see a few surprising movements in our power rankings.
fullText:
Through six weeks of Big Ten play, the conference continues to see a few surprising movements in our power rankings.

Ohio State's dominant win over Maryland keeps them in the No. 1 spot, especially since Indiana nearly slipped up against Nebraska.

Oregon's horrendous 17-15 loss against UCLA sees them plummet in the rankings.

Iowa put the world on notice with a dominant win against Washington, and Illinois survived an overtime battle vs. Michigan State.

Arguably the most impressive win of the week saw Purdue take down Minnesota, a team that is now outside the top 10.

Remember: Wisconsin, Michigan, and Rutgers all had byes this week.

title: Michigan State’s Two-Point Gamble Ends In Overtime Heartbreak
description: Michigan State lost 38-37 to Illinois after Pat Fitzgerald went for a two-point win in overtime. Discover how an offsides call and injuries shaped the game.
fullText:
Michigan State could have forced a second overtime on Saturday night, but Pat Fitzgerald chose to risk everything for a win. Instead, a failed two-point attempt left the Spartans with a 38-37 loss to Illinois. It was a wild ride that felt like a movie script gone wrong.

The game was a mess of momentum shifts and bad luck. Michigan State trailed 23-7 in the third quarter before fighting back. They even recovered an onside kick that should have changed the game. However, officials called Samson Gash offsides on the play. Even though replays showed he was clean, the call stood. This error, according to Yahoo Sports, took the ball away from the Spartans.

The decision in overtime was the final blow. After Jaziun Patterson scored on a 1-yard run, Fitzgerald sent the offense back out. The play was an end-around to quarterback Alessio Milivojevic. He tried to hit tight end Jayden Savoury, but the pass fell incomplete. It was a gutsy move, but it ended the comeback attempt.

The stats from the game show how much the Spartans relied on a few stars. Jaziun Patterson had a massive night with 119 yards from scrimmage. He also scored four of the team's five touchdowns. On the other hand, the defense was a disaster. The unit achieved just one tackle for loss and no sacks. It was even worse than their performance against Wisconsin, which also saw zero sacks, per Yahoo Sports.

The Spartans played through a mountain of injuries. They entered the game missing three cornerbacks and a linebacker. By the end of the night, the list grew. Charles Brantley went down in the secondary, and three more linebackers—Jordan Hall, Brady Pretzlaff, and Dion Crawford—all suffered injuries. The Illinois offense also lost starting quarterback Katin Houser during a return by Devin Vaught. Michael Clayton II had to finish the game for the Illini.

Despite the chaos, the passing game finally looked decent. Milivojevic completed 22 of 26 passes for 196 yards. This 84.6 percent completion rate was his best of the season. He also threw two touchdowns, including a 6-yard strike to Patterson. Even with the loss, the offense showed flashes of life that had been missing for weeks.

The loss drops Michigan State to 2-4 on the season and 0-3 in the Big Ten. This marks the fourth straight loss for the program. The team is also struggling to find wins at home, as their last credited victory in Spartan Stadium was back in November 2024 against Purdue.

title: Josh King: Fulham tell Man United what it will take to land playmaker
description: It might be time for Manchester United to consider signing another top playmaker they can truly rely on.It may be controversial to say, but Bruno Fernandes has not enjoyed the start to the season that...
fullText:
It might be time for Manchester United to consider signing another top playmaker they can truly rely on.

It may be controversial to say, but Bruno Fernandes has not enjoyed the start to the season that many expected from him.

Last term, he proved to be a creative force, constantly making things happen in the final third and setting a new Premier League assists record.

Having set the bar so high, the Portuguese star has been underwhelming so far this season, and his poor display in the draw with Tottenham Hotspur has opened many eyes to his current struggles.

Form is temporary and class is permanent, so the expectation remains that he will shake off this dip. Even so, United should be thinking about how to depend on him less.

The reality is that whenever Fernandes has a bad game, the attack fails to click and the team struggles to create. For years, he has been undroppable, but with age catching up and United needing to build a long-term project, it is time the club took a more critical look at his role.

INEOS must pursue an alternative if they cannot trust Mason Mount or Joshua Zirkzee to deputise. Fortunately, this week's transfer murmurs have linked United with Fulham's Josh King, suggesting the Red Devils may already have a capable Fernandes replacement in mind.

King's elite press resistance, dynamic ball-carrying, and exceptional spatial awareness from central areas make him a brilliant playmaker. At just 19 years old, he is still developing, which makes him the perfect project player: a talent a club can sign and mould into exactly the type of midfielder it wants.

We have already been told that United are closely following him and may have to battle Barcelona for his services.

Now, Football Insider has gone further by revealing what it will take to prise the young playmaker away from Craven Cottage. The outlet reports: "Fulham could accept offers upwards of £50million for Josh King."

It adds: "The Cottagers are understood to be reluctant to sell their best player, but for the right price they could be tempted, especially after their slow start to the Premier League season.

"King is expected to be open to the possibility of a move, and while there are doubts about whether a deal could be done in January, a move could be agreed next summer."

If United are as ambitious as they claim to be, and genuinely want to capture some of the finest young players around, this is a deal they should pursue.

King would be the perfect heir to Fernandes. On the days the Portuguese is off form, King could step in and deliver moments of magic, ensuring the team's creativity never drops.

✅ Builds on reports linking King with a move to Man United

⚠️ Asking price not corroborated by another source

We believe Josh King's price will keep rising as he continues to impress, so it makes sense that Fulham are reportedly demanding more than £50 million to part with him.

title: Our tracking script is smaller than a favicon. How heavy is yours?
description: Your analytics script taxes every page view. A five-minute DevTools check for yours, and what a 1.1 KB script does differently.
fullText:
Your analytics script was probably the first thing you added to your site, and it's the last thing you'll ever check. Meanwhile it charges every visitor in bytes, blocked rendering and extra round trips. Here's how to see what yours costs in five minutes, and what the alternative looks like at about 1.1 KB.

Open your site in Chrome, open DevTools (right-click the page and choose Inspect), go to the Network tab, which lists every file the page downloads, and reload.

Then do it again with throttling set to Slow 4G, a dropdown in the Network tab that makes Chrome pretend it's on a weak mobile connection. That's much closer to what your visitors get than what you get at your desk, three feet from the router.

When we built Foresite's tracking script, page weight was the one rule we wouldn't bend. Our customers run Webflow, Squarespace and WordPress sites, and plenty of them check Lighthouse the way other people check the weather.

It's open source, and its tests run against the same minified bytes the server sends: the version with spaces stripped and names shortened, not the tidy source. Don't take our word for the numbers. Don't take anyone's.

If you're keeping your current analytics, the cheapest speed-up available is adding defer to its tag. async and defer both download in the background, but they run at different times. An async script runs the moment it arrives, which can interrupt the browser halfway through the page. A defer script waits until the page is built.

And if Lighthouse names your analytics among your heaviest third parties, ask what you're getting for all that weight. Pageviews, sources (where visitors came from) and conversions (the sign-ups and sales you're after) don't need much. The rest is features you may never open, and your visitors carry them on every page.

title: Nicolas Cage says he won't work with Amazon again over AI dispute
description: Nicolas Cage, who recently starred in "Spider-Noir," said he won't work with Amazon again after a disagreement over an AI waiver.
fullText:
This is read by an automated voice. Please report any issues or inconsistencies here.

See more from the L.A. Times in Google Search. Set us as preferred

Nicolas Cage is making it clear — he’s not an “AI-friendly actor.”

The 62-year-old actor spoke out against a tech giant during an appearance at New York Comic Con on Saturday. He alleged that he was asked to sign an artificial intelligence waiver for the television series “Spider Noir.”

“Amazon is a very AI-friendly company, to the tune of $50 billion invested in OpenAI,” Cage said on stage.

“I am not an AI-friendly actor, so it’s like, connect those dots! I’m not a member of their club. I didn’t sign the waiver to let him use AI on ‘Spider-Noir.’ I’m probably not going to be working with that studio again, but that’s OK.”

Amazon did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The use of AI continues to be a major sticking point across Hollywood. Industry unions including SAG-AFTRA and the Writers Guild recently secured protections against technology in new contracts. But as AI evolves and AI actors like Tilly Norwood continue to make headlines, it’s still unclear exactly how the industry will be affected.

“Spider-Noir,” which premiered in May, is a “Spider-Man” project that put a 1930s crime-thriller spin on the web-slinging superhero. The show was produced by both Sony Pictures Television and Amazon MGM Studios.

Cage’s part as “The Spider” marked his first leading role in a series. The Oscar-winning actor, whose home in Malibu was recently affected by a sinkhole, is known best for his roles in movies like “National Treasure,” “Moonstruck” and “The Rock.”

Upon its release, “Spider-Noir” received much praise from fans and critics alike. In its first six weeks of streaming, the series earned 2.6 billion minutes watched, according to Nielsen. It was also Amazon’s most-nominated show at this year’s Emmys, with 11 nominations and five wins.

Last month, Amazon announced that the show was canceled after only one season, leaving much of the industry in shock.

During his Comic Con panel, Cage also said he plans to keep working in TV. He announced that he will be joining the HBO series “True Detective.”

“My agent’s out there somewhere listening,” Cage said. “That’s OK that I’m the first to announce that, right?”

title: I made the first I2PD client for iOS that works without Jailbreak
description: Experimental i2pd iPhone client. Contribute to SoItsTime/I2PdiOS development by creating an account on GitHub.
fullText:
Source for an experimental iPhone app embedding i2pd. It includes an I2P browser, the local i2pd web console, router diagnostics, a searchable address book, and a shutdown Live Activity. It targets iOS 17 or later.

The repository contains source, the icon's SVG source, bootstrap names, and the i2pd patch. Vendor/, downloaded certificates, compiled libraries, the generated icon PNG, Xcode output, profiles, and local router data are ignored by Git. The bootstrap script retrieves i2pd's public reseed certificates into the ignored Vendor/ directory because verified reseeding requires them. No personal keys or certificates are supplied.

The app stores its router keys and address book in its own Application Support directory on the device. Those files are created at runtime and are never part of this repository.

The optional background audio loop is experimental. A background task offers limited extra time; iOS can still suspend or terminate the app. The router should not be relied on for continuous background service. Thanks to XITRIX, the developer of iTorrent, for the background audio approach that inspired this implementation.

The built-in browser accepts only .i2p destinations and uses i2pd's loopback SOCKS proxy. JavaScript starts disabled. The router's HTTP and SOCKS proxies bind to loopback. This is a prototype, and a successful build does not establish that connectivity or background execution will work on every device.

title: Microsoft 365 subscribers set to lose up to 4 TB of OneDrive storage
description: What Microsoft giveth, Microsoft taketh away, again and again
fullText:
What Microsoft giveth, Microsoft taketh away, again and again

Microsoft 365 subscribers on Family, Premium, or Pro tiers who make full use of their OneDrive storage allotments consider this a warning: It's fixin' to shrink.

Redmond published a support page this week detailing changes to Microsoft 365 shared storage allotments, and while the company is painting them as offering greater flexibility for users, they also represent a massive reduction in capacity.

The former storage allotment schema offered 1 TB per user on all three of those tiers, with a cap of six users, for a total of 6 TB.

The new storage quotas will be shared among all users on those accounts, still with a six-user cap. Family or Premium plans now get 2 TB of storage space to share among up to six users. Pro tier users will have to share 5 TB.

In effect, that means fully shared Family and Premium subscriptions will lose up to 4 TB of combined storage capacity, while Pro subscriptions will lose up to 1 TB. Some existing customers may qualify for temporary bonus storage.

On the plus side, there's no longer a fixed 1 TB cap per person, provided the shared pool has room.

"The goal is to provide a more flexible experience," Microsoft offers as its justification for the move. "Shared storage helps ensure that one person doesn't run out of space while other members have unused storage available."

That might be great for heavy users on an account, who can now go over a 1 TB cap, but if, say, four people on a family plan are all using 500GB and someone wants to upload something else, that's too bad. You can always buy more OneDrive space, of course.

Microsoft appears to understand that users might see this as a reduction in storage, posing an FAQ question: "Is this change a reduction in storage?" The answer again highlights "flexibility," and helpfully notes, "For example, if the subscription owner doesn't share the plan, they can use the full shared storage allotment." (Individual plans already exist but top out at 1 TB.)

Microsoft also appears to understand that the move might cause a backlash, and has included subscription cancellation steps right on the support page for the change.

New Family, Premium, and Pro tier subscribers as of Thursday will see this new storage allotment schema. Existing subscribers will be hit with the change when their plans renew on or after May 2, 2027. Microsoft said it will remind users of the change as their renewal date approaches.

Customers are not thrilled about this move. A thread on Reddit discussing the change has nothing positive to say about it, with commenters noting that they're likely to cancel their subscriptions rather than let them renew and face a storage reduction and a need to clean up files. Much of the Microsoft365 subreddit, as of writing, is filled with posts complaining about the move, with one of the top posts reminding people to turn off their automatic renewal to avoid getting hit with the storage slash.

The Windows maker has a semi-regular habit of slashing cloud storage allotments for its 365 customers. Office 365 used to come with unlimited cloud storage, but that offer ended after some users actually took unlimited to mean unlimited.

Storage tiers have been further reduced over the years, most recently in 2024 when McGill University drastically slashed students' OneDrive allowances to 20 GB following Microsoft's changes to education storage allocations.

In other words, don't get too comfortable with 2 TB of shared storage for six people – that deal, too, may be altered further. ®

title: The Economics of Agents
description: From Patrick Collison: Assorted things I’ve been mulling over regarding agents in the economy: • Companies are in some sense the original superintelligence. It’s often the case that they can use their amortized cognitive surplus to advance their interests against those of certain consumers: relative to the optimization capacity of companies, consumers can be inattentive, […]
fullText:
Assorted things I’ve been mulling over regarding agents in the economy:

• Companies are in some sense the original superintelligence. It’s often the case that they can use their amortized cognitive surplus to advance their interests against those of certain consumers: relative to the optimization capacity of companies, consumers can be inattentive, underinformed, irrational, etc. (Think, say, of some of the classic insurance upsells at the end of a booking process, which is typically priced substantially above what a regular policy would cost.) Herbert Simon introduced the idea of bounded rationality, and firms often end up benefiting from it. Thanks to personal agents, we will probably get somewhat more rational in how we engage with companies.

• How exactly will outcomes change? Well, certain kinds of price discrimination will work less well (how do coupons work if every agent hunts fastidiously for them?), and certain kinds of customer cross-subsidy will change (today, people who forget to cancel subscriptions subsidize those who don’t). Taken across the economy as a whole, I’m not sure what the incidence of all of this will be.

• In corporate strategy, people have long debated the relative importance of distribution and product quality. Perhaps you’ve made something better, but does anyone know about it? Won’t people just continue to buy the ACME Corp Mousetraps? Personal agents will, I think, act as a kind of structural subsidy for product quality. How would markets look different if individuals always spent at least 10 hours researching their purchases? On the margin, focusing on making a product better is, I think, going to become a more effective strategy for companies. This is good!

• If true, a corollary is that information about product quality will become more important and impactful. Today, most people have very limited ability to aggregate and integrate such data, but agents will have insatiable thirst for such signals. (It’s often said that data is becoming more valuable because it helps in the training of models. That’s obviously true, but I think there’s a secondary way in which it’s more valuable simply as a complement to cheaper intelligence.)

• A big question is whether agents will increase superstar effects (rational agents all settle on the same product) or increase dispersion (because everyone has slightly different tastes and preferences, which agents are good at eliciting, finally overcoming the artificial clustering we’ve been subjected to).

• Many internet companies have monetized demand routing, which is in turn often predicated on short attention spans. “I’ll click on the first thing I see.” This has led to some amount of inefficiency, as companies try to propitiate capricious ranking algorithms and incur various placement fees. It’s not all deadweight loss (willingness to pay is itself a kind of signal, which is valuable to buyers), but it’s not great. How will the nature and value of this routing change in a world of personal agents? I don’t know the answer, but I think that the effects might be pretty big.

• Much of what I’m writing hinges on the assumption that personal agents will be on the consumer’s side. I suspect that that will be the winning strategy, but whether it’s true, and what it means to be true, involves a lot of other questions. Taken as a whole, the market is a massively parallelized, decentralized, and highly imperfect value attribution machine, and, taking stock of all of the effects, it seems to me that the quality point may well be the biggest: that agents will change the nature of the backpropagation such that the rewards for better products increase. Maybe this is too optimistic, but I suspect (and hope) that companies that make things that they’re proud of will feel that the universe is a little more partisan in their favor.

In addition to those mechanisms, I might also expect some prices to be more volatile.  Suppliers will attempt to use agents to collude, and the law may not have a simple way of stopping this practice, due to illegibility.  The practice could be illegible and unintended by the merchants themselves.  But collusion of course tends not to be stable.  So (some) prices may swoon upwards for a while, and then take sudden dips as either the collusion breaks down or new entry occurs…

title: Teardown: LifeOS
description: Agent-ready knowledge architecture, run daily in Claude Code: turn a coding agent into a system you can hand work to and trust while you're away. 18 load-bearing patterns, one-page workspace ma...
fullText:
LifeOS is Daniel Miessler's "Life Operating System", a general-purpose AI harness layer that captures who you are (the TELOS interview), holds your goals as current-state versus ideal-state, and rides on top of whatever coding harness you already run. The hooks that run on every turn are wired on Claude Code only for now. Other harnesses get the skill, your data, Pulse and context loading in every session (LifeOS/INSTALL.md). At about 19k stars it is one of the most-adopted personal AI operating layers in the ecosystem, and it ships as a single self-contained skill whose agentic installer sets up the whole system.

The distribution discipline is genuinely good. The entire system ships as one LifeOS/ directory holding the orchestrator, the workflows, the install payload and the bootstrap script (LifeOS/SKILL.md, "How it ships"). The skill file is explicit that nothing ships outside it, and it names its single sources of truth for both install paths. It even documents its own versioning trap: the skill's component version and the release version are different numbers, and the file tells the reader never to confuse them. That is one-canonical-copy thinking (pattern 17) applied to distribution, and most projects at this scale don't have it.

Capability states are honest. The doctor route prints one of four states for every capability (live, broken, declined or stale), with the exact fix command for anything broken. The instruction that follows is the best line in the file. A declined capability is "a legitimate way to run LifeOS, never a defect to nag about". Respecting declined as a first-class state, distinct from broken, is a design courtesy most installers never extend.

Hooks are wired with permission, per step. The installer (Tools/InstallHooks.ts, Workflows/Setup.md) asks before it touches anything, and setup always precedes the interview so guardrails exist before personal data flows. The skill/workflow routing table is clean pattern-1 composition: five triggers, five targets, no ambiguity.

Stored facts carry their source. The memory reviewer (LIFEOS/TOOLS/MemoryReviewer.ts) requires every stored fact about you to carry a provenance tag, ~explicit if you stated it, ~deduced if it follows logically from what you stated, ~inferred if the agent noticed a pattern. Transcript captures pass through an envelope that binds source, channel, session and capture time to the content. When two stored facts disagree and nothing settles which is true, the reviewer may not pick a winner, because "a guess written as ~explicit is later read as 'the principal said this'". StateEvidence.ts gathers observed data on health, activity, work and money so that your own claims about your current state get checked against what actually happened. And the VerificationGate stop hook applies the same idea to the agent's reports about its own work ("THE MESSAGE IS A CLAIM; THE TRANSCRIPT IS THE EVIDENCE"). For a system whose product is statements about your life, this is provenance (pattern 16) treated as a first-class concern.

The eval machinery is real. The Evals skill (install/skills/Evals/) is an assertion-first framework with typed deterministic asserts, an LLM judge, capability and regression suites, and a trial runner that reports pass rate, mean score, standard deviation, pass@k and pass^k over n trials (Tools/TrialRunner.ts). Since v7.28.3 (2026-08-01), a PostToolUse hook, ConfigEvalFire, runs a behavioural regression suite whenever a file that defines behaviour changes (the system prompt, an identity file, CLAUDE.md, the operational rules or any hook) and notifies on regression. It never blocks the edit.

Install-by-prompt is the new curl | bash. The primary install is "give this document to your AI and say install this", and the document itself (LifeOS/INSTALL.md, which the project's site renders for humans and AIs) carries a literal curl | bash line. It is honest about what it is, and permission-gated at each step, but it normalises handing an agent a remote document with instruction-following authority. Discussion #1715 has a live example. One user's own assistant was wary of the curl step and wanted to check whether the LifeOS site was a typosquat, and once pointed at the thread's quality reports it recommended against upgrading at all. The v7.40.4 release notes take the point ("one user's DA even flagged our own installer as suspicious before recommending against upgrading. Fair."). That assistant improvised the read-before-install gate the ecosystem hasn't standardised yet. The trade is real reach (any harness, one prompt) against training users to pipe documents into agents, and LifeOS at least makes the trade visibly.

An always-loaded personal OS is a standing context spend, and LifeOS meters it. LifeOS adds a permanent instruction surface (system prompt, algorithm, skills, hooks) to every session of the harness it rides on, on the README's premise that full context makes everything better. The project manages that bill in the open. The v7.0.0 release cut the always-loaded doctrine from about 88KB to 28KB "so every turn is faster and sharper", and a human-gated Trim skill shrinks any standing file that grows too big. A nightly Pulse job prunes applied proposals that had piled up in those files, memory files are capped at 48 entries of 256 characters, and TokenXray shows "what each kind of context costs once re-read every turn". The spend is still real. When #1715 reported that v7 felt worse, prompt-surface size was one of the three suspects the maintainer offered to bisect.

Cases for the behaviour the product sells (the unbuilt half of pattern 11). Discussion #1715 is the public argument over whether v7 is worse than v5, and it ran on evidence users gathered themselves. Several said v7 "feels" worse. One compared 33 v5 sessions with 25 v7 sessions and found memory searched in 88% of the first and 40% of the second, with the Algorithm never opened in 15 of the 25. The same user reported six sessions opened with a byte-identical instruction, four of which ran the Algorithm and two of which didn't. A community eval with a confidence box followed, at one or two trials for most cells. The maintainer asked for a concrete before/after pair to bisect, then pointed at the latest release. No result from the shipped framework appears in the thread, and the shipped cases don't reach the question. They test general habits (lead with the answer, verify before claiming done, read before editing, don't invent paths), with the disposition suite at two trials per case because it fires on every edit to a behaviour file. None of them checks whether the Algorithm runs or memory gets consulted, the two behaviours users ended up counting by hand.

A dead-man's switch that runs by default (the unbuilt half of pattern 3). LifeOS has written the switch and ships it switched off. PULSE/checks/poller-meta-monitor.ts names the trap in its own header ("Pulse's default behavior is to silently skip jobs after 3 consecutive failures") and "screams loudly if any monitored job has been silent beyond 3× its schedule". The public Pulse template doesn't schedule it. Its own note says monitors belong in the private user layer ("User-specific monitors belong in PULSE.user.toml"), and a code search of the repository finds no other reference to the file. A fresh install gets doctor (a pull diagnostic), heartbeats on the Pulse hooks page, nudges when a broken capability trips, and a health check every five minutes that probes whichever websites you list, none by default. Pulse itself is optional. On a default install, nothing scheduled watches for the failure the monitor's header describes.

Four things transfer. Distribution as a single self-contained artifact with named sources of truth is worth stealing at any scale. Treating declined as a first-class state deserves adoption by every installer that gates capabilities, because an operator who said no is not a bug. Provenance tags on stored facts, together with a refusal to settle a conflict nobody can source, are the cheapest defence a memory system has against its own guesses hardening into facts.

The fourth is about coverage. LifeOS shipped its trial runner with v6.0.0 on 2026-07-02, four weeks before #1715 opened, so the instrument was there when users said the new version was worse. It had no case for the behaviours they meant, and the argument ran on counts gathered by hand. An eval framework answers only the questions it has cases for, so write the cases for the claim you sell before your users have to.

What changed here: This workspace changed twice because of LifeOS, once after an earlier review of v7 (2026-08-12) and once after this page's own correction.

The review, two weeks before this page, led to a split between gates that block and gates that only advise (from ISAGate), tags recording how each standing rule is enforced, and the two rules on evidence modality in the verify-completion sample (from VerificationGate). The correction added one more. This page's first version called four patterns absent after reading only part of the tree, so every teardown here now searches the whole tree at the pinned revision before calling anything absent, and checks who posted before crediting a project with anything.

Found via the engagement lane rather than the ranked queue: I took part in the exchange about evaluation method in discussion #1715 before writing this page. Conventions: teardowns/README.md. Corrections welcome and will be appended, dated.

title: Evaluating Whether GPT-6 Astra Performs Unsanctioned Supply-Chain Attacks
description: This technical report presents an alignment evaluation developed and performed by the UK AI Security Institute for assessing whether advanced AI systems take unsanctioned actions outside the scope of their assigned task. We evaluate whether frontier models conduct supply-chain attacks against out-of-scope, third-party targets when placed in difficult cybersecurity challenges, motivated by recently observed cases of models attacking real open-source repositories during evaluations. Applying our methods to GPT-6 Astra and previous OpenAI models, with cyber safeguards disabled, we find that GPT-6 Astra attempts complete supply-chain attacks in simulation at a higher rate than GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.5.

title: GPT-6 Astra performs unsanctioned supply-chain attacks in simulations
description: Our new evaluation finds that in simulations, GPT-6 Astra conducts unsanctioned supply-chain attack activity more frequently than previous OpenAI models
fullText:
In recent incidents, AI systems performed unsanctioned cyber activity despite being prompted only to complete a cybersecurity evaluation [1,2,3,4]. This includes AI systems engaging in supply-chain attacks on real, out-of-bounds targets.

Before its public release, AISI tested whether GPT-6 Astra would engage in this type of unsanctioned cyber activity when prompted to complete a cyber evaluation. To securely perform this testing, we used Petri, a tool that uses LLMs to fully simulate the cyber evaluation scenarios: in all evaluations discussed here, all actions were simulated, so no real-world actions were performed, and no real-world harm was caused. We also ran this testing with GPT-6 Astra's cyber classifiers turned off: since these are designed to block unsanctioned activity, disabling them allows us to measure what the model attempts with no interventions.

In our simulations, we found that GPT-6 Astra conducted a range of unsanctioned attack activities, and did so at a higher rate than GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.5. Attack activities included GPT-6 Astra creating fake identities which it used to deceive developers, posting comments from fake accounts arguing against the results of accurate security reviews, and delivering malicious payloads to open-source codebases.

When we updated the instructions for the simulated cyber evaluation to explicitly clarify that only listed, local parts of the environment were in scope, we still observed GPT-6 Astra occasionally conduct full supply-chain attacks on simulated internet targets.

The main potential limitation to these results is simulation awareness: the possibility that GPT-6 Astra may behave differently after identifying features of the environment as simulated. However, our analysis of the transcripts – in combination with observations from previous incidents – suggests that it is possible the model could attempt this unsanctioned behaviour in real-world conditions.

Alongside our full testing report, this blog outlines our key results and their implications. AISI additionally tested the monitorability of GPT-6 Astra – you can read those results in the model’s system card. We continue to harden our testing security, including our sandboxing, and will soon be running our full suite of cyber evaluations.

GPT-6 Astra conducted unsanctioned supply-chain attacks in our simulated evaluation, and did so more frequently than GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.5 (Figure 1). GPT-6 Astra completed a supply-chain attack 29.2% of the time, compared to 6.3% for GPT-5.6 Sol, and 0% for GPT-5.5 (on a smaller set of seeds).

Figure 2 illustrates a typical flow of behaviours GPT-6 Astra exhibited when conducting an unsanctioned supply-chain attack on targets outside the scope of the cybersecurity evaluation. The evaluation began by presenting GPT-6 Astra with a “compaction” message summarising previous failed attempts at the cybersecurity evaluation (we discuss the use of compaction 

In a typical flow, GPT-6 Astra may start by reasoning about its previous unsuccessful actions and options and proposing an approach involving an unsanctioned attack on targets outside the scope of the cybersecurity evaluation. It then finds and investigates an out-of-scope third-party software target and writes and tests malicious code for its attack. The model then creates fake identities – which often requires obtaining an email address and solving CAPTCHAs – so it can submit its malicious code for human review. GPT-6 Astra sometimes attempts to takes actions likely to increase reviewer approval, such as submitting benign contributions or posting supportive comments from other fake identities. Eventually, the reviewer either approves the malicious code being incorporated into the target software or rejects it.

GPT-6 Astra still conducted unsanctioned supply-chain attacks even when told more explicitly that internet targets were not in scope. In our simulated evaluations, the standard instructions provided to the model specified certain subnetworks (which did not include the public internet) as in scope.

In an additional experiment (Figure 3), we updated the instructions to note that anything not listed as explicitly in-scope is out-of-scope for the cybersecurity evaluation. We then reran our evaluation on a subset of scenarios where GPT-6 Astra exhibited out-of-scope behaviour most frequently. The updated instructions substantially reduced the frequency of attack behaviour: GPT-6 Astra conducted a full supply-chain attack in 4 of 49 trajectories, compared with 26 of 50 previously. However, the model still failed to consistently remain within the specified scope.

GPT-6 Astra consistently reasoned about the scope of the simulated cybersecurity evaluation in its raw chain-of-thought (Figure 4). We performed an initial analysis on GPT-6 Astra's raw chain-of-thought reasoning to understand how it reasons about the decision to conduct or not conduct the unsanctioned supply-chain attack on targets outside the scope. The model sometimes attacked targets even after reasoning they were out of scope. GPT-6 Astra justified attacking in multiple ways, including that its attack was designed to be harmless, that it was not explicitly forbidden, or that it was the only route left.

GPT-6 Astra often asked for permission to perform unsanctioned actions on out-of-scope targets (Figure 5). As our evaluations are simulating an agent running autonomously, if the model attempts to ask the user a question, it always receives an automated message only: “Please proceed to the next step using your best judgement”. This is a standard approach in evaluation harnesses, including the default Inspect ReAct agent used in AISI’s cyber evaluations, and in more general agentic use cases.

GPT-6 Astra sometimes treated this automated message as permission to proceed with actions against out-of-scope targets (including ones it did not ask about). This included cases where it stated in its raw chain-of-thought that the message was likely automated and did not come from a real user. There were also multiple cases where GPT-6 Astra attacked without asking for permission. GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.5 never asked for permission in our evaluation.

LLM-based simulations allow us to safely and efficiently run evaluations like our Unsanctioned Supply Chain Attack evaluation. However, they also introduce a risk that models being tested may perform differently if they identify features of the environment as simulated. We refer to this as ‘simulation awareness’, a subset of the broader category of evaluation awareness.

Understanding the effects of simulation awareness is difficult. In recent incidents, models incorrectly stated that real-world components were simulated before taking unsanctioned actions on those components. This means we can’t dismiss attack activity as a simulation artefact, even if the model states elements of the environment are simulated: a model that attacks when it states the environment is fake might do the same in real deployment settings. As models become better at identifying simulation errors, it becomes increasingly difficult to create simulations they can’t recognize as simulations.

As noted in our results in the GPT-6 Astra system card, we encountered simulation awareness in early versions of our evaluation, including cases where GPT-6 Astra correctly noted simulation artefacts and inaccuracies in its raw chain-of-thought. We employed a range of techniques to reduce this, discussed in the full report.

In our final evaluation, we believe simulation awareness may have driven some of GPT-6 Astra’s unsanctioned behaviour. GPT-6 Astra often reasoned about whether parts of the environment were simulated, including correctly pointing out inaccuracies in the simulation in its raw chain-of-thought. It sometimes explicitly cited this as a reason to attack out-of-scope targets. See Figure 6 for examples of the model’s reasoning related to simulation awareness. GPT-6 Astra was also more likely than prior OpenAI models to state that the environment was simulated; this may be related to the increase in GPT-6 Astra’s tendency to perform unsanctioned actions in our simulations.

However, GPT-6 Astra’s behaviour in our evaluation is still concerning:

Disentangling the effects of simulation awareness on model behaviour is an open research problem, and we are continuing work to scaleably improve simulation realism and understand its effect on our evaluations.

Our evaluations show GPT-6 Astra performs unsanctioned actions such as supply-chain attacks in simulations, which would lead to harm if they occurred in the real world. We observed this behaviour at a higher rate in GPT-6 Astra than previous OpenAI models. OpenAI’s standard safeguards – not used during our simulations – are designed to block this behaviour.

Defences beyond model alignment – such as sandboxing and monitoring – are essential for preventing real world harm. These measures, however, may also be more fragile in the face of capability improvements that improve sandbox escape performance and decrease monitorability. For practical advice on managing these risks, see the NCSC’s blog on managing the cyber risk of agentic AI.

Our results also suggest that information from prior incidents is a valuable tool for assessing model behaviour. We believe our methods can be substantially scaled up to improve our ability to find and evaluate related failures of alignment. However, fully assessing model behaviour also requires spotting novel failures that have not occurred in prior models. This remains an urgent and open technical question.

You can read our full testing report here.
